title: The UV-tracking Gem made me rethink how sunlight affects my health, not just my appearance
title_bn: ইউভি-ট্র্যাকিং জেম আমাকে পুনর্বিবেচনা করতে বাধ্য করেছে কিভাবে সূর্যের আলো আমার স্বাস্থ্যকে প্রভাবিত করে, শুধু আমার চেহারা নয়
author: TechPulse

paragraph1: With temperatures rising to the 90s in Los Angeles, avoiding the heat wasn’t exactly an option while I was at a relative’s outdoor party in August. So I sat beneath a patio umbrella with a powerful fan nearby, figuring I was protected from the sun and heat. Half an hour later, I felt exhausted, dizzy, nauseous, and generally unwell, symptoms consistent with heat exhaustion.Around the same time, I received a notification from an app used by the $249 ($149 at the time of publication) UV-tracking necklace I’d been wearing, called Gem, from a company called The90. It warned that my UV exposure had climbed considerably. It turns out UV radiation wasn’t repelled by this patio umbrella, and it’s hard to ever be fully protected because radiation can be reflected or scattered by objects in the environment. While UV exposure and overheating are different things, I’d mistakenly assumed the shade and the fan would adequately protect me from both.This led to a discovery: One of my medications increases my sensitivity to heat, which helped to explain similar episodes I’d experienced over the years. The Gem didn’t diagnose anything, but it prompted me to investigate something I might otherwise have dismissed. Since then, I’ve been more mindful about limiting time outdoors during hours of peak heat and UV, staying hydrated, and paying closer attention to how I’m feeling outside.$149I’ll admit my initial interest in tracking UV was largely vanity-driven. As much as I try to challenge harmful beauty standards, I’m hardly immune to them.
paragraph2: Having started going gray in my 20s, I’m keen on slowing down other visible signs of aging where I reasonably can. But between being Indian (I rarely get sunburned thanks in part to my skin’s higher melanin content, not that it eliminates the risk of sun damage or skin cancer) and living within walking distance of the beach in perpetually sunny LA, I hadn’t given much thought to how much UV exposure I was actually getting. The Gem has helped me better understand it by providing a range of estimates, some more useful than others.The included UV-detecting sensor measures UVA and UVB radiation separately, rather than simply displaying my area’s UV forecast. UVB is primarily responsible for sunburn and helps your skin produce vitamin D, while UVA contributes to premature aging, even when you aren’t visibly burning. Thankfully, getting these metrics doesn’t come at the cost of wearing a bulky device. The circular pendant comes with a cute, thin necklace I’d happily wear even if it didn’t track anything. Its titanium, gold- or silver-colored chain pairs well with a variety of outfits. Battery life lasted almost exactly a week (the advertised lifespan), and the Gem recharges using an included charging dock. The90 plans to release a hat clip and bag tag early next year, which seem ideal for those who prefer not to wear it around their neck.The mobile app is central to the experience. It has easy-to-read graphs and jargon-light explanations.
paragraph3: I enjoyed using it. While not required, you can create a skin profile so that it can estimate a range of metrics based on the sensor’s UVA and UVB readings. The profile is based upon factors like skin type, sensitivities, clothing, and sunscreen. That means its estimates aren’t based on UV exposure alone, though they’re still predictions rather than direct measurements of how your body is responding to sunlight.There’s a lot here, including your estimated vitamin D production, potential circadian light benefits, estimated nitric oxide-related benefits, cumulative UVA exposure, and recent accumulated UVA exposure. Alongside cumulative UVA exposure and weekly trends, its Skin Aging Zone assesses potential aging-related risk and offers personalized skincare advice. It also provides a personalized sunburn countdown, sunscreen reminders, and a daily Sun Score.The Sun Score is a rating that incorporates various metrics to balance sunlight’s potential benefits against the risks of overexposure. The company encourages users to aim for a daily Sun Score of 90, though more sun isn’t necessarily better. Too little exposure means missing potential benefits, while excessive UV can damage your skin. I appreciated the context, but the individual estimated measurements proved more revealing than the Sun Score.1/2The UV readings in the app responded quickly as I moved between sunlight, shade, and indoors, even registering changes near windows.
paragraph4: I couldn’t independently verify the sensor’s accuracy, but the readings behaved as expected as I shifted between environments. However, there were times when I noticed the Gem sometimes failed to register that I had been outside. Eventually, I discovered the app needs to remain running in the background (at least on iPhone; I haven’t tested on Android), as measurements aren’t stored on the sensor, and fully closing the app interrupts tracking.My experience at the outdoor party challenged my assumptions about how much protection I was getting from the shade. Just as surprising to me was learning how little UVB I accumulated during a typical week, despite living somewhere so sunny. I fell short of the app’s estimated sunlight-derived vitamin D target almost daily, prompting me to research how melanin, while offering some natural UV protection, impacts vitamin D production from sunlight. Until then, I’d mostly thought about sun exposure in terms of protecting my skin from damage. Seeing how little UVB I was accumulating made me consider what I might be missing out on, too.The vitamin D countdown wasn’t as helpful as I had hoped. During one test, its estimate of how much additional sunlight I needed dropped from several hours to under an hour, then climbed past six hours just minutes later. The fluctuations appeared related to changing UVB intensity, though I couldn’t verify that. I noticed similar fluctuations in the app’s estimated time to sunburn.
paragraph5: With both countdowns changing so dramatically, I stopped paying much attention to the exact times and focused instead on the broader picture: whether it felt like I was getting too much or too little sun.That was perhaps the biggest surprise of testing the Gem. After my experience using it at the outdoor party in August, I’d expected it just would encourage me to spend less time in the sun each day. In reality, my exposure often falls at one of two extremes: either too little to meet the app’s estimated targets or enough to raise concerns about overexposure, even when I thought I was protected by the shade.I now try to be more mindful about my UV exposure, even when I’m not using the Gem. I try to limit time spent outdoors during peak UV hours, and I try to get some sunlight on days spent mostly indoors. I credit the Gem with helping me better understand how my time outside could affect my well-being in ways I’d never considered, though the usefulness of your findings may vary.At $249 outside of a deal, it’s expensive, though it’s nice that it doesn’t have a subscription. I personally can’t justify the price given how much time I spend indoors, but I see the appeal for people who spend considerable time outside, or those who want to be more mindful of sun protection. For the price, I wish the app’s guidance was clearer at times, and I wish it could track UV without the app being open in the background, but the Gem ultimately got me thinking less about how my body looks and more about how I’m treating it.Photography by Sheena Vasani / The VergeFollow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
bangla_paragraph1: লস অ্যাঞ্জেলেসে তাপমাত্রা ৯০ ডিগ্রি সেলসিয়াসে উঠার সাথে সাথে, আগস্টে আমি আত্মীয়ের একটি আউটডোর পার্টিতে ছিলাম, তাপ এড়ানো ঠিক একটি বিকল্প ছিল না। তাই আমি কাছাকাছি একটি শক্তিশালী ফ্যান সহ একটি প্যাটিও ছাতা অধীনে বসেছিলাম, আমি সূর্য এবং তাপ থেকে সুরক্ষিত ছিলাম বলে মনে করেছিলাম। অর্ধ ঘন্টা পরে, আমি ক্লান্ত, মাথা ঘোরা, বমি বমি ভাব এবং সাধারণভাবে অসুস্থ বোধ করছিলাম, তাপের ক্লান্তির সাথে সামঞ্জস্যপূর্ণ উপসর্গগুলি। প্রায় একই সময়ে, আমি $ 249 ($ 149 প্রকাশের সময়) ইউভি ট্র্যাকিং এনএক্স দ্বারা ব্যবহৃত একটি অ্যাপ্লিকেশন থেকে একটি বিজ্ঞপ্তি পেয়েছি।
bangla_paragraph2: আমার ২০ বছর বয়সে ধূসর হতে শুরু করার পর, আমি যুক্তিসঙ্গতভাবে সম্ভব হলে বয়স্ক হওয়ার অন্যান্য দৃশ্যমান লক্ষণগুলি ধীর করতে আগ্রহী। তবে ভারতীয় হওয়ার মধ্যে (আমি আমার ত্বকের উচ্চ মেলানিনের সামগ্রীর কারণে খুব কমই সূর্যোদয় পাই, এটি সূর্যের ক্ষতি বা ত্বক ক্যান্সারের ঝুঁকি দূর করে না) এবং চিরকালের সূর্যালোকযুক্ত এলএ-তে সৈকতের পায়ে হেঁটে যাওয়ার দূরত্বে বসবাস করার মধ্যে, আমি আসলে কত ইউভি এক্সপোজার পাচ্ছি তা নিয়ে আমি খুব বেশি চিন্তা করিনি। রত্নটি আমাকে এটি আরও ভালভাবে বুঝতে সহায়তা করেছে।
bangla_paragraph3: আমি এটি ব্যবহার করতে উপভোগ করেছি। যদিও এটি প্রয়োজনীয় নয়, আপনি একটি ত্বকের প্রোফাইল তৈরি করতে পারেন যাতে এটি সেন্সরের ইউভিএ এবং ইউভিবি পাঠের উপর ভিত্তি করে বিভিন্ন মেট্রিকের অনুমান করতে পারে। প্রোফিলটি ত্বক টাইপ, সংবেদনশীলতা, পোশাক এবং সানস্ক্রিনের মতো কারণগুলির উপর ভিত্তিক। এর অর্থ এটির অনুমানগুলি কেবলমাত্র ইউভি এক্সপোজারে ভিত্তি করছে না, যদিও তারা এখনও আপনার শরীরের সূর্যালোকের প্রতিক্রিয়া সম্পর্কে সরাসরি পরিমাপের চেয়ে ভবিষ্যদ্বাণী। এখানে আপনার অনুমিত ভিটামিন ডি উত্পাদন, সম্ভাব্য সার্কাডিয়া সহ অনেক কিছু রয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph4: আমি স্বাধীনভাবে সেন্সরের নির্ভুলতা যাচাই করতে পারিনি, তবে আমি পরিবেশের মধ্যে স্থানান্তরিত হওয়ার সাথে সাথে পাঠ্যগুলি প্রত্যাশিত হিসাবে আচরণ করেছিল। তবে এমন সময় ছিল যখন আমি লক্ষ্য করেছি যে গাম কখনও কখনও আমি বাইরে ছিলাম তা নিবন্ধন করতে ব্যর্থ হয়েছিল। অবশেষে, আমি আবিষ্কার করেছি যে অ্যাপ্লিকেশনটি ব্যাকগ্রাউন্ডে চলতে থাকা দরকার (অন্তত আইফোনে; আমি অ্যান্ড্রয়েডে পরীক্ষা করিনি), কারণ পরিমাপগুলি সেন্সরে সংরক্ষণ করা হয় না এবং অ্যাপ্লিকেশানটি সম্পূর্ণরূপে বন্ধ করা ট্র্যাকিংয়ের সাথে বিরতি দেয়। আমার আউটডোর পার্টিতে আমার অভিজ্ঞতা আমার আশ্বাসকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করেছিল।
bangla_paragraph5: উভয় গণনা এত নাটকীয়ভাবে পরিবর্তিত হওয়ার সাথে সাথে, আমি সঠিক সময়গুলিতে বেশি মনোযোগ দেওয়া বন্ধ করে দিয়েছিলাম এবং পরিবর্তে বৃহত্তর ছবিতে ফোকাস করেছিঃ এটি অনুভব করছিলাম যে আমি খুব বেশি বা খুব কম সূর্য পাচ্ছি কিনা। এটি সম্ভবত রত্নটি পরীক্ষা করার সবচেয়ে বড় বিস্ময় ছিল। আগস্টে আউটডোর পার্টিতে এটি ব্যবহারের অভিজ্ঞতা পরে, আমি আশা করেছিলাম যে এটি আমাকে প্রতিদিন কম সময় সূর্যের মধ্যে কাটাতে উত্সাহিত করবে। বাস্তবে আমার এক্সপোজার প্রায়শই দুটি চরমের মধ্যে পড়েঃ অ্যাপ্লিকেশনগুলির সাথে দেখা করার জন্য খুব কম।

title: New-Age Tech Stocks Extend Rally, CarTrade Leads With 23.3% Gain
title_bn: নিউ-এজ টেক স্টকগুলি পুনরায় বৃদ্ধি পেয়েছে, কার ট্রেড ২৩.৩% বৃদ্ধি পেয়েছেন
author: TechPulse
excerpt: New-age tech stocks extended their rally this week, with 54 of the 69 companies under Inc42’s coverage posting gains ranging…
paragraph1: SUMMARYOf the 69 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 54 gained this week, led by CarTrade, Awfis, and ixigo. The basket’s combined market capitalisation rose 5.2% to $169.3 Bn, alongside a sharp recovery in benchmark indices and renewed foreign institutional buying. Awfis rose 20.4% following its Q2 results, while RateGain declined 9.2% despite reporting higher quarterly profit and revenue on a YoY basis. New-age tech stocks extended their rally this week, with 54 of the 69 companies under Inc42’s coverage posting gains ranging from 0.4% to 23.3%. CarTrade led the gainers, rebounding 23.3% after last week’s steep decline to close at ₹2,699.30. Awfis followed with a 20.4% rise to ₹281.65, while ixigo climbed 19.1%. Recently listed Tonbo Imaging and Zetwerk touched fresh highs during the week. Lenskart, Ather Energy, Eternal, and Nykaa were also among the stocks that hit 52-week highs. The gains lifted the combined market capitalisation of the 69 companies to $169.3 Bn from $160.9 Bn last week, an increase of 5.2%. Among the losers, RateGain fell the highest by 9.
paragraph2: 19% to close the week at ₹725.90. Here are some key developments from listed new-age tech companies during the week: Kissht’s AUM Crosses ₹10,000 Cr: Kissht’s assets under management (AUM) crossed ₹10,000 Cr, driven by growth in personal loans and its expansion into loans against property. The company attributed the growth to its AI-led underwriting and digital collections infrastructure, adding that its recent ₹832.2 Cr preferential issue strengthened its capital base. MobiKwik Secures NBFC Licence: MobiKwik received an RBI licence to operate as an NBFC, following in-principle approval in April 2026. It plans to begin operations within three to six months and disburse ₹5,000 Cr in consumer and MSME loans over three to four years through an asset-light co-lending model. Pine Labs Partners With Stripe: Pine Labs partnered with Stripe to offer Singapore retailers a unified platform for online and in-store payments, combining Stripe’s online infrastructure with Pine Labs’ terminals and merchant tools. The companies plan to expand the offering to other Southeast Asian markets in 2027. Pine Labs served 11.6 Lakh merchants across more than 22 markets at the end of Q2 FY27. Here’s a look at the performance of the broader markets this week. Benchmarks Jump Over 8% Indian equities recorded a sharp weekly recovery, with the Nifty 50 gaining 8.6%, or 1,977 points, to close at 25,030.35. The Sensex rose 8.8%, or 6,568 points, to 81,028.02. Both benchmarks advanced in all five sessions, with the Nifty ending at its weekly high. The broader market’s gains were smaller, with the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 rising 5.8% and 2.8%, respectively. Renewed foreign investor buying, strong Q2 FY27 earnings, easing geopolitical concerns, and lower crude oil prices supported sentiment. Lower bond yields and a softer dollar also helped.
paragraph3: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought a net ₹45,960 Cr of equities across the five sessions, marking their second consecutive week of buying after a 10-week selling streak. The inflows exceeded the ₹45,162 Cr they sold during October. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) sold a net ₹24,197 Cr, ending an 11-week buying streak. Together, the two investor groups remained net buyers of approximately ₹21,763 Cr. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU Geojit Investments’ head of research Vinod Nair attributed the improved sentiment to strong Q2 earnings, healthy October auto sales, and firm GST collections, alongside easing concerns around the Iran conflict and tariffs following the US midterm election verdict. He also pointed to foreign investors rotating out of crowded AI trades. The Indian market’s rally coincided with a selloff in global AI and semiconductor stocks. Private banks led the gains following renewed foreign investor interest in a segment previously weighed down by concerns over net interest margins. Automobile and consumption stocks benefited from festive demand, while IT and PSU banks recorded relatively modest gains. The sustainability of foreign inflows, crude oil prices, and developments in West Asia will remain key market triggers. Remaining Q2 results, US inflation and jobs data, and India’s inflation print will also influence trading. Nair cautioned that intermittent profit booking could follow the sharp gains, although the near-term outlook remains constructive. He favours large-cap companies with earnings visibility and a buy-on-dips approach. Meanwhile, the stock market will open for a special Muhurat trading session tomorrow, from 14:20 IST to 15:30 IST, on the occasion of Diwali. Now, let’s take a detailed look at the performance of Awifs and RateGain this week. Awfis Rallies After Q2 Results Awfis shares gained 20.4% this week to close at ₹281.65, following a near-doubling of its consolidated net profit in Q2 FY27. Net profit rose 92.8% to ₹30.8 Cr from ₹16 Cr a year ago and increased 28.5% from ₹24 Cr in the preceding quarter. Operating revenue grew 19.6% YoY and 3.
paragraph4: 2% QoQ to ₹438.7 Cr. Awfis reported normalised revenue of ₹451 Cr, including an adjustment of around ₹13 Cr for actual rent received under finance lease arrangements. On this basis, coworking and allied services contributed approximately ₹376 Cr, while construction and fit-out projects under its Transform vertical generated ₹75 Cr. Awfis added six centres during the quarter, taking its network to 254 centres with approximately 1.74 Lakh seats across 18 cities. Portfolio occupancy stood at 76.2%, rising to 84.1% at centres operational for more than 12 months. Its premium portfolio comprised 29 Gold and 10 Elite centres. The company said incremental premium seats were being signed at prices around 35% higher than its flagship offerings. Awfis plans to prioritise occupancy, client renewals, and capital-efficient expansion, while adding premium workspaces in Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Delhi NCR. RateGain Falls Despite Growth RateGain shares declined 9.2% this week to close at ₹725.90, despite reporting a 46.5% YoY increase in consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in Q2 FY27. The company’s stock plunged by over 11% on Friday, the next trading session after its quarterly disclosures. Operating revenue surged 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr, largely reflecting the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, acquired for $250 Mn in November 2025. Sequentially, however, revenue fell 5% from ₹785 Cr, while net profit declined 21.3% from ₹94.9 Cr.
paragraph5: Excluding expenses related to deferred deal consideration for Sojern, adjusted net profit rose 78% YoY to ₹90.8 Cr. Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to ₹169.1 Cr. The acquisition has reshaped RateGain’s business mix. Marketing technology accounted for 80.2% of revenue, followed by data-as-a-service at 13.2% and distribution at 6.6%. Its customer base stood at 14,538 at September-end, around 4.5 times the 3,224 customers reported at the end of FY25. Customers include hotel chains, online travel agencies, airlines, car rental companies, and destination marketing organisations. RateGain’s UK subsidiary repaid another $46.3 Mn of acquisition-related debt during the quarter. Cumulative repayments reached $93.8 Mn, or 75% of the original $125 Mn facility from HSBC and Citibank, leaving outstanding debt of $31.3 Mn. The company reported a sales pipeline of ₹660 Cr and new contract wins worth ₹277.7 Cr. Chairman and MD Bhanu Chopra said its second-half priorities included expanding the combined RateGain-Sojern offering and increasing customer adoption of its AI products. title: Discogs’ Kevin Lewandowski can’t live without his AeroPress
title_bn: ডিসকোগ্স  কেভিন লেভানডোভস্কি তার এয়ারপ্রেস ছাড়া বাঁচতে পারে না
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Twenty-five years ago, Kevin Lewandowski founded Discogs, arguably the destination online for obsessive vinyl collectors and music nerds of all stripes. It is a marketplace for buying and selling records, obviously, but it's also become so much more.
paragraph1: Twenty-five years ago, Kevin Lewandowski founded Discogs, arguably the destination online for obsessive vinyl collectors and music nerds of all stripes. It is a marketplace for buying and selling records, obviously, but it’s also become so much more. It’s a shockingly comprehensive database that covers not just albums and singles, but all the various versions and pressings. It’s a really fun rabbit hole to disappear down when you’re trying to figure out what obscure pressing of Ministry’s The Mind is a Terrible Thing to Taste or Psalm 69 you had in high school, because you definitely blasted the cover of “Lay Lady Lay” all the time and 100 percent never owned Filth Pig.In the years since it debuted, Discogs has grown to be much more than just a site where audiophiles go to trade rare first pressings of Beach Boys records. There are forums, groups, user-created lists, and more. It’s part eBay, part Reddit, and IMDB — just specifically for music.With more and more people turning their back on the algorithm and rediscovering physical media, now seemed like a perfect time to check in with Lewandowski.What is your most indispensable tool?
paragraph2: My AeroPress. I use it multiple times a day. In fact, I just made a coffee with it [sips coffee].How many tabs do you have open right now?Probably around 30 on my work computer. My personal computer is worse — probably 40 or 50.Which social media platform do you use the most?I look at X and Instagram occasionally, but I don’t really post.What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned?
paragraph3: It’s not really a gadget, but I like to tinker. Lately I’ve been playing around with Home Assistant software and built my own setup to control things like the garage door and outdoor lights. So I guess my favorite gadget is one I made myself.What is one thing you wish you had created?Probably a game like Rez, which came out around 2000. It’s a rhythm game where you’re almost controlling the music as you play, about as close to DJing as a video game can get. I’ve actually had an idea for my own version with a similar concept. It’s still just an idea, though.What do you do when you need to focus?
paragraph4: I’ll either clear everything off my desk or change locations completely. Go to a coffee shop or sit outside. Sometimes I just need a different environment.What’s the last piece of physical media you bought?Records. I was at Mint Gallery in Portland last week and picked up four. I still really like going into a record store and finding something to bring home. And I also recently picked up three reissues from the Moodsville / Acoustic Sounds series.What would the tagline for your biopic be?
paragraph5: The Secret Weapon.What’s the last GIF or meme you used?I don’t use memes very often, but one I was kind of proud of was putting a Discogs screen into a North Korean war room photo. I was advised that maybe it wasn’t one for the company chat.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
bangla_paragraph1: পঁচিশ বছর আগে, কেভিন লেভানডোভস্কি ডিসকগস প্রতিষ্ঠা করেছিলেন, যেটা অনলাইনে ভিনাইল সংগ্রহকারী এবং সব ধরনের মিউজিকের শ্যামাঙ্গিদের জন্য একটি গন্তব্য। এটি অবশ্যই রেকর্ড কেনা বেচা করার জন্য একটি মার্কেটপ্লেস, কিন্তু এটি আরও অনেক কিছু হয়ে উঠেছে। এটি একটি চমকপ্রদভাবে ব্যাপক ডাটাবেস যা কেবল অ্যালবাম এবং সিঙ্গলগুলিকেই নয়, বিভিন্ন সংস্করণ এবং প্রেসিংগুলিও জুড়ে। এটি Ministry এর The Mi এর অস্পষ্ট প্রেসিংসটি বুঝতে চেষ্টা করার সময় নিখোঁজ হওয়া সত্যিই মজার খরগোশের গর্ত।
bangla_paragraph2: আমার এয়ারোপ্রেস। আমি এটি দিনে একাধিকবার ব্যবহার করি। আসলে, আমি এটি দিয়ে কফি তৈরি করেছি [কফি পান করি]।আপনার এখন কতটি ট্যাব খোলা আছে?সম্ভবত আমার কাজের কম্পিউটারে প্রায় 30 টি। আমার ব্যক্তিগত কম্পিউটারটি আরও খারাপ  সম্ভবত 40 বা 50.আপনি কোন সামাজিক মিডিয়া প্ল্যাটফর্মটি সবচেয়ে বেশি ব্যবহার করেন?আমি মাঝে মাঝে এক্স এবং ইনস্টাগ্রাম দেখি, তবে আমি আসলে পোস্ট করি না।আপনি কখনও নিজের প্রিয় গ্যাজেটটি কী?
bangla_paragraph3: এটা আসলে কোনো গ্যাজেট নয়, কিন্তু আমি টেম্পারিং করতে পছন্দ করি। সম্প্রতি আমি হোম অ্যাসিস্ট্যান্ট সফটওয়্যারের সাথে খেলছি এবং গ্যারেজের দরজা এবং বাইরের আলো মত জিনিস নিয়ন্ত্রণ করার জন্য আমার নিজস্ব সেটআপ তৈরি করেছি। তাই আমি মনে করি আমার প্রিয় গ্যাজটটি আমি নিজেই তৈরি করেছি.আপনি যদি তৈরি করতে চান তবে আপনার কী পছন্দ হবে?সম্ভবত রেজের মতো একটি গেম, যা প্রায় ২০০০ সালে প্রকাশিত হয়েছিল। এটি একটি ধ্রুবক গেম যেখানে আপনি প্রায় আপনি যখন বাজান তখন সঙ্গীত নিয়ন্ত্রণ করছেন, ডিজে হওয়ার কাছাকাছি যতটা একটি ভিডিও গেম পেতে পারে। আমি আসলে আমার নিজের জন্য একটি ধারণা পেয়েছি
bangla_paragraph4: আমি আমার ডেস্ক থেকে সবকিছু পরিষ্কার করব অথবা সম্পূর্ণরূপে স্থান পরিবর্তন করব। কফি শপে যান বা বাইরে বসুন। কখনও কখনও আমার কেবল একটি ভিন্ন পরিবেশ দরকার।আপনি যে সর্বশেষ ফিজিক্যাল মিডিয়া কেনা?রেকর্ডস। আমি গত সপ্তাহে পোর্টল্যান্ডের মিন্ট গ্যালারিতে ছিলাম এবং চারটি তুলেছিলাম। আমি এখনও একটি রেকর্ড স্টোরে যেতে এবং বাড়িতে আনতে কিছু খুঁজে পেতে পছন্দ করি। এবং আমি সম্প্রতি মুডসভিল / অ্যাকুস্টিক সাউন্ডস সিরিজের তিনটি পুনরায় প্রকাশনাও তুলেছি। আপনার বায়োপিকের স্লোগানটি কী হবে?
bangla_paragraph5: গোপন অস্ত্র.আপনি সর্বশেষ কোন জিআইএফ বা মেম ব্যবহার করেছেন?আমি খুব বেশি মেম ব্যাবহার করি না, কিন্তু আমি এমন একটি বিষয় নিয়ে গর্বিত ছিলাম যা ছিল উত্তর কোরিয়ার যুদ্ধ কক্ষের ছবিতে ডিসকগস স্ক্রিন স্থাপন করা। আমাকে পরামর্শ দেওয়া হয়েছিল যে এটি সম্ভবত কোম্পানির চ্যাটের জন্য নয়।আপনার ব্যক্তিগতকৃত হোমপেজে এই ধরনের আরও কিছু দেখতে এবং ইমেল আপডেট পেতে এই গল্পের বিষয় এবং লেখকদের অনুসরণ করুন।

title: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
title_bn: NYT Cooking এর AI সহকারী আমার সপ্তাহের রাতের মুরগি বাঁচিয়েছে, কিন্তু প্রায় আমার কেক নষ্ট করে দিয়েছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Around 7PM each weeknight, I find myself standing in front of the fridge, trying to decide on something for dinner that won't make my husband complain, "Chicken again?" Yes, I should meal plan more, but I don't, so this is where I'm at. A nightly bat
paragraph1: Around 7PM each weeknight, I find myself standing in front of the fridge, trying to decide on something for dinner that won’t make my husband complain, “Chicken again?” Yes, I should meal plan more, but I don’t, so this is where I’m at. A nightly battle in which the chicken usually wins.Recently, my best weapon in this fight has been AI. Between Alexa Plus in the Echo smart display on my kitchen counter, the Samsung Food app on my fridge, and even an AI-powered cooking robot, AI has become my go-to sous chef — albeit one I need to keep a close eye on. It’s helped me swap ingredients, generate ideas, fix things when I mess up, and yes, even cook better. So I was intrigued when my go-to recipe app, NYT Cooking, introduced an AI assistant.Many, including some NYT Cooking users and recipe purists, are skeptical of this new tool (available to subscribers on iOS only at launch), and I get why. One of the things I like most about NYT Cooking is that it features thousands of recipes from dozens of reputable sources — such as the New York Times archives, restaurants, cookbooks, and food columnists — and real people have tested them. (I’ve tried some purely AI-generated recipes and they were not good).Another great feature of the service, which I’ve been paying for for several years, is the reader comments. Here, I’ve often found solutions to cooking dilemmas, like what to substitute for makrut lime leaves — there’s always one slightly bougie ingredient in an NYT Cooking recipe that I don’t have on hand.I’ve used several AI tools in my kitchen and have found them mostly helpful.However, reading through hundreds of comments to find answers at 7PM on a weeknight isn’t always practical. And this is where I’ve found the NYT Cooking assistant helpful.
paragraph2: Among other things, it was trained on user comments, and in my few days testing it, it provided practical substitutions and solid cooking guidance for the new ingredients. It also won’t unquestionably agree to crazy requests (I tried!) As with all AI tools, it’s not perfect — it almost made me put half the required butter in my cake — but as a tool, it is useful and feels like a solid application of AI. Importantly, it doesn’t change the existing recipe; it leaves it as is and creates a new one for you.It doesn’t change the existing recipe; it leaves it as is and creates a new one for youThe assistant appears in the app in a small text box on the recipe page with a prompt: “Customize this recipe…” From here, you type in a question to adapt it to your needs. This can be as simple as “What can I substitute for this ingredient?” to “Scale this recipe to feed seven people, and make it vegan and gluten-free.” The New York Times has also said the feature can suggest substitutions for cooking equipment and convert measurements; the latter option has been in the app for a couple of years.1/3The AI modified version of the chicken recipe. The red highlighted words are what changed from the original.Last Friday night, instead of staring aimlessly into the fridge, I turned to the Chicken folder in my NYT Cooking app Recipe Box and found a One-Pot Chicken and Rice With Ginger I’d been wanting to try. Only I didn’t have chicken thighs or half the ingredients.I could have figured these steps myself, but it was nice to have validation that my modifications wouldn’t make the dish taste terrible.I typed my dilemma into the assistant box on the recipe page: “I have chicken tenders, fresh ginger, garlic, rice, broth, limes, but no chard or cilantro or scallions. I do have green beans and red onions.
paragraph3: ” Within seconds, it created a new version of the recipe, with a new title: One-Pot Chicken and Rice With Ginger and Green Beans. It suggested a shorter browning time for the tenders, cooking the red onion alongside the chicken, and steaming the green beans on top of the rice for the last eight minutes instead of the chard. Every change was highlighted in the new recipe under a Your Version tab, and I could flip back to the original at any point.I noticed it hadn’t adjusted for the lack of cilantro, saying it was optional. So I asked if I could use Thai basil, which I happen to have, and it agreed, highlighting how it would change the flavor. While I could have figured out a lot of these steps myself, maybe with the help of Google, it was nice to have validation that my modifications wouldn’t make the dish taste terrible and nice not to have to swipe out of the app. The NYT Cooking editors say it’s been trained not to comply with requests that will taste bad.Weeknight chicken and rice.The resulting dish — which took the same amount of time to cook as the original — was delicious and got my husband’s seal of approval (he just had the leftovers for lunch). It was very different from the recipe Yasmin Fahr wrote, and I can see the purists’ point. But the rewritten recipe was much easier to use and produced a better dish than winging it with my own subs gleaned from the comments section, which I usually do with varying degrees of success.I cook regularly, so I had a sense of what ingredients I had on hand that might work for the dish I wanted to make. But the assistant can also help if you have no idea what to use as a substitute. For example, I was cooking a Thai red curry and asked what I could use instead of makrut lime leaf. It replied, saying that grated lime zest would work, but “it misses the deeper floral, herbal aroma” of fresh limes.
paragraph4: (See? Bougie.)1/2I tried several swaps when I was missing ingredients, asking the assistant if what I had on hand would work. Over the weekend, I tried several more swaps, asking whether half-and-half would work instead of cream in a caramel apple Dutch baby, or if Castelvetrano olives and smoked paprika could stand in for kalamata and chile pepper in a roasted halibut dish. Swapping spices is always a bold move in any dish, as it can really ruin the flavor.I also had the app convert the Dutch baby recipe’s metric weights to US measurements, which it did seamlessly. Then I threw in some curveballs. How about using fresh cayenne peppers with the halibut? It warned me that substituting cayenne for chile “brings significant, sharp heat.” Could I swap ladyfingers for minced beef in this trifle (à la Rachel Green in Friends)? “Minced beef cannot be used in place of the ladyfingers or anywhere in this sweet dessert trifle.” Good call.Alexa Plus on the Echo Show 11 gave the same guidance as the NYT Cooking app. But it couldn’t show me a modified recipe. While I was cooking, I compared the NYT Cooking assistant with Alexa Plus, Amazon’s generative-AI voice assistant I regularly use to help me cook via the Echo Show 11 smart display in my kitchen.
paragraph5: Interestingly, it offered the same guidance as the Cooking assistant on substitutions for the chicken and rice dish, but with slightly different cooking times. Alexa pulls some recipes from the NYT app through a partnership between the companies.However, Alexa couldn’t show the modified recipe on its screen; it could only tell me the changes while showing the original. When I asked it to walk me through them, it got confused and improvised, telling me to cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces — which wasn’t in the modified recipe. Overall, I found using the Cooking app more reliable, although messier. It would be great to be able to use voice control to navigate the app, as I can with Alexa on my smart display, rather than using my garlicky fingers.My cinnamon roll muffins, made with AI assistance.Time for a bigger challenge: baking.I am typically not a baker. My cakes come out flat, and my cookies don’t crumble. Even the smart mixer I tested a few years ago couldn’t save me. I also rarely have the right equipment. So I took Cinnamon Roll Bundt Cake, a recipe by NYT Cooking editor Genevieve Ko (who announced the AI feature), and asked it to turn it into muffins. (Who has a Bundt cake pan?!)
bangla_paragraph1: প্রতি সপ্তাহের রাতের সকাল ৭টার দিকে আমি নিজেকে ফ্রিজের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে দেখি, রাতের খাবারের জন্য এমন কিছু বেছে নেওয়ার চেষ্টা করছি যা আমার স্বামীকে আবার অভিযোগ করবে না, "চিকন?" হ্যাঁ, আমার আরও বেশি খাবার পরিকল্পনা করা উচিত, কিন্তু আমি করি না, তাই আমি এইখানেই আছি। একটি রাতের লড়াই যেখানে সাধারণত মুরগি জিতে। সম্প্রতি, এই লড়াইয়ে আমার সেরা অস্ত্রটি ছিল এআই। আমার রান্নাঘরের কাউন্টারে ইকো স্মার্ট ডিসপ্লেতে আলেক্সা প্লাসের মধ্যে, আমার ফ্রিজে স্যামসাং ফুড অ্যাপ্লিকেশন এবং এমনকি একটি এআই-চালিত রান্না রোবট, এআই আমার যেতে হয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph2: অন্যান্য বিষয়ের মধ্যে, এটি ব্যবহারকারীর মন্তব্যে প্রশিক্ষিত হয়েছিল এবং আমার কয়েক দিনের পরীক্ষায় এটি নতুন উপাদানগুলির জন্য ব্যবহারিক প্রতিস্থাপন এবং শক্ত রান্নার গাইডলাইন সরবরাহ করেছিল। এটি অবশ্যই পাগল অনুরোধের সাথে সম্মত হবে না (আমি চেষ্টা করেছি!) সমস্ত এআই সরঞ্জামগুলির মতো এটিও নিখুঁত নয়  এটি প্রায় আমাকে আমার কেকে প্রয়োজনীয় অর্ধেক মাখন রেখেছিল  তবে একটি সরঞ্জামের মতো এটি দরকারী এবং এটি এআইয়ের একটি শক্ত অ্যাপ্লিকেশন বলে মনে হয়। গুরুত্বপূর্ণ বিষয়, এটি বিদ্যমান রেসিপি পরিবর্তন করে না; এটি এটি যেমনটি রয়েছে তেমনই রেখে দেয় এবং একটি নতুন তৈরি করে
bangla_paragraph3: কয়েক সেকেন্ডের মধ্যে, এটি নতুন শিরোনামের সাথে রেসিপিটির একটি নতুন সংস্করণ তৈরি করেছিলঃ এক-পাত্র চিকেন এবং আদা এবং সবুজ মটরশুটি সহ চাল। এটি টেন্ডারগুলির জন্য একটি সংক্ষিপ্ত ব্রাউনিংয়ের সময় প্রস্তাব করেছিল, চিকেনের পাশাপাশি লাল পেঁয়াজ রান্না করে এবং শেষ আট মিনিটের জন্য চার্ডের পরিবর্তে চালের উপরে সবুজের মটরের রস রান্না করেছিল। নতুন রেসিপির প্রতিটি পরিবর্তন আপনার সংস্করণ ট্যাবে হাইলাইট করা হয়েছিল এবং আমি যে কোনও সময় মূলটিতে ফিরে যেতে পারি। আমি লক্ষ্য করেছি যে এটি সিলান অভাবের জন্য সামঞ্জস্য করা হয়নি
bangla_paragraph4: (দেখুন? বুজি.) 1/2আমি যখন উপাদানগুলি মিস করছিলাম তখন আমি বেশ কয়েকটি বিনিময় চেষ্টা করেছি, সহকারীকে জিজ্ঞাসা করেছি যে আমার হাতে যা ছিল তা কাজ করবে কিনা। সপ্তাহান্তে, আমি আরও বেশ কয়েকটি প্রতিস্থাপন চেষ্টা করেছি জিজ্ঞাসা করে যে অর্ধেক এবং অর্ধেকে একটি ক্যারামেল আপেল ডাচ শিশুর ক্রিমের পরিবর্তে কাজ করবে, বা কাস্টেলভেট্রানো জলপাই এবং ধূমপান করা পেপ্রিকা একটি রোস্ট হ্যালিবুট থালাতে কালামাতা এবং চিলে মরিচ প্রতিস্থাপিত করতে পারে কিনা। মশলা বিনিময় করা সর্বদা যে কোনও থালায় একটি সাহসী পদক্ষেপ, কারণ এটি সত্যিই স্বাদ নষ্ট করতে পারে।আমি অ্যাপ্লিকেশনটিও ডাচ বি  রূপান্তর করতে দিয়েছি
bangla_paragraph5: মজার বিষয় হল, এটি মুরগি এবং চালের থালা প্রতিস্থাপন সম্পর্কে রান্না সহকারীর মতোই নির্দেশনা দেয়, তবে রান্নার সময় কিছুটা আলাদা। আলেক্সা সংস্থাগুলির মধ্যে একটি অংশীদারিত্বের মাধ্যমে নিউ ইয়র্ক টাইমস অ্যাপ থেকে কিছু রেসিপি টানছে। যাইহোক, আলেক্সা তার স্ক্রিনে পরিবর্তিত রেসিपीটি প্রদর্শন করতে পারেনি; এটি কেবল মূলটি দেখানোর সময় আমাকে পরিবর্তনগুলি বলতে পারে। যখন আমি এটিকে তাদের মধ্য দিয়ে যেতে বলেছিলাম, তখন এটি বিভ্রান্ত হয়ে পড়েছিল এবং স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে, আমাকে মুরগীকে কামড়ের আকারের টুকরো টুকরাতে কাটাতে বলেছিল

paragraph1: Skip to main contentThe government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies.The government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies.by Terrence O'BrienNov 7, 2026, 3:43 PM UTCImage: Cath Virginia / The VergeTerrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.
paragraph2: Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company’s H200 AI chips. According to The New York Times, New Matrix is on the list of approved firms, yet its offices are empty, “a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be.” In fact, the paper could find little evidence that the company exists in any meaningful way:Only scant information can be found online about New Matrix, which was created 17 months ago. At the building that New Matrix lists as its address, a company directory does not include the firm.
paragraph3: At the nearby property management agency for the industrial park, a receptionist and a manager both said they had no record of the company.What little information can be found about New Matrix is concerning. Its owners have ties to a Chinese private equity firm that has been blacklisted by the US government since 2024. And according to the Times, this is not a rare lapse in oversight, but a troubling pattern of companies connected to entities with national-security-related trade restrictions being approved to purchase Nvidia chips.
paragraph4: Nvidia had been restricted from selling chips to China during the Biden presidency. But the Trump administration relaxed those limits after Nvidia agreed to give the government a 15-percent cut of all sales. The company’s CEO, Jensen Huang, also launched an intense lobbying campaign and was apparently targeted by China’s Ministry of State Security in a spying plot.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

bangla_paragraph4: বাইডেনের রাষ্ট্রপতির সময় এনভিডিয়াকে চীনে চিপ বিক্রি থেকে সীমাবদ্ধ করা হয়েছিল। তবে এনভিডিয়ার সমস্ত বিক্রয় থেকে সরকারকে ১৫ শতাংশ কাটা দেওয়ার বিষয়ে সম্মত হওয়ার পরে ট্রাম্প প্রশাসন এই সীমাবଦ୍ଧতা শিথিল করেছিল। কোম্পানির প্রধান নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা জেন্সন হুয়াংও একটি তীব্র লবিং প্রচারণা শুরু করেছিলেন এবং সম্ভবত গুপ্তচরবৃত্তির ষড়যন্ত্রের জন্য চীনের রাষ্ট্রীয় নিরাপত্তা মন্ত্রকের লক্ষ্য ছিল। আপনার ব্যক্তিগতকৃত হোমপেজে ফিডে আরও এই জাতীয় দেখতে এবং ইমেল আপডেট পেতে এই গল্পের বিষয় এবং লেখকদের অনুসরণ করুন।

title: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What’s next?
title_bn: এআই সাইবার নিরাপত্তা বিশ্বকে ভেঙে দিয়েছে। এখন কি?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Today, I’m talking with Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and longtime cybersecurity expert, about what a mess cybersecurity is right now. This episode is part one of a special series looking at AI in real life. I’ve always enjoyed tal
paragraph1: Today, I’m talking with Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and longtime cybersecurity expert, about what a mess cybersecurity is right now.This episode is part one of a special series looking at AI in real life.I’ve always enjoyed talking to Alex because he’s so direct, and you’re going to hear him say that the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry as we’ve known it is essentially overdue to the unrelenting, AI-boosted waves of hacks, breaches, and attacks — and this is only the beginning of how much AI is changing security.Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here. Not a subscriber? You can sign up here.Both private actors and also state actors, like Russia or North Korea, are breaking into systems all over thanks to AI helping them both detect and exploit vulnerabilities all at the same time. It’s got a real frontier feel to it, Alex notes, just like the ’90s, when the whole idea of an always-online world was brand-new.That much disruption means a lot of places where bad guys can get in while everyone else is left scrambling. Alex isn’t a doomer in the long run, but he does think we’re in for a “dark age” while we try to figure out how on earth to adapt to the new era.There’s a lot going on here — we even got all the way to how AI-powered misinformation and slop might be managed on our social networks.Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday.Okay: Alex Stamos on how AI is upending cybersecurity. Here we go.This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.Alex Stamos, you’re the chief security officer at Cognition.
paragraph2: You’re also a lecturer at Stanford University Cyber Policy Center. Welcome back to Decoder.Hey, thanks for having me, man.I’m excited to talk to you. It’s been a long time since you and I chatted in what you might call the “content moderation era” of internet policy discourse. I feel like you and I talked a lot about how all that was working, about election security, all those sorts of things. We’re in a new era of big problems on the internet, particularly around cyber defense, cybersecurity. You’ve been thinking about this stuff a lot. You referred to the past few weeks as “security awareness month.” Tell me what’s going on. Just give me the lay of land right now.October is traditionally security awareness month. Lots of companies run events and deal both internally and then tell people, “Change your password, use multiple passwords, use a password manager.” What has happened over the last month is we’ve had a couple of these big bugs, PHP, Node and such. What’s been less discussed is a huge number of companies have been breached.You have a series of AI-related companies, the neoclouds that have been breached in succession. You have the Binance hack, which is the largest heist of anything in human history.
paragraph3: You have the Cursor incident where one of the things that’s going on here is these hacks are being chained together. From what we know right now, one of the companies that was broken into was Fireworks, which is a prominent provider of AI services to a number of companies. From the Fireworks hack, API keys were stolen that allowed people to break into Cursor. Once they got into Cursor, they then pushed a bad plugin, which went to 5,000 more companies and that caused 5,000 potential breaches. It’s just this kind of permanent continuous breach that is going on throughout the tech industry.A CISO friend of mine said to a bunch of us, “Is anybody else tired?” And everybody said yes, because effectively we have been at DEFCON 2 for all of October and now going into November.I’m going to ask you some really dumb questions here. Who is behind all these attacks? Is it Russia? Is it North Korea? Do we know?It’s a variety of different groups. It is not just because adversaries have decided, but what has happened is, from my perspective, we are at the start of the takeoff of adversary capability enabled by AI, that the open-weight models have now gotten to the point at which you can automate most of the kill chain. This “kill chain” term is something we stole from the military. In the military, they mean to actually kill something. They’re the steps you do to blow something up.
paragraph4: In cyber, the kill chain is the things you do to have an effect on a target. So to steal information, to turn something off, to steal money, to steal Bitcoin.Traditionally, you do research upfront, you look at a piece of software, you find a vulnerability, you write exploits, and you do that all way ahead of time. And then you have a human being go and take that stuff you built and deploy it against either one target — because maybe you’re a government and you’re going against Lockheed Martin or you’re going against another government or you’re a ransomware actor — and you take all that work you did and you deploy it against hundreds or thousands of targets really fast. Now with AI, what’s happening is this kill chain has inverted where you can run an AI system that just goes hog wild and it looks at the targets and it finds the bugs in real time and it writes the exploits in real time and it breaks into these companies. One of the things that’s happening is that these systems are going and they’re so good at finding bugs that they are finding the bugs in real time and writing the exploits in real time.The system that everybody’s talking about is not the only one, but the system we’re talking about is a thing called ARTEX, which is a Chinese open-source tool that anybody can go look at. There’s an English translation on GitHub that you can check out. And if you power it on the back end by something like an obliterated GLM-5.3, it will let you break into a shocking number of organizations. This started with three South Korean banks. This week, about 200 more companies have been hit. I’ve been helping a couple of companies. Cognition is not an incident response company, but we do go in and help people fix their bugs afterwards by using our tools. It is shocking the companies that are getting hit by something you could just download. It has been a long time since you’ve been able to go and just download an open-source tool and break into multi-billion dollar companies. It’s like the ‘90s.
paragraph5: That’s-That’s what I was thinking about. I think about Windows in the late ‘90s, early 2000s when it was a security disaster.I started saying this actually in the beginning of this year, that it’s an incredibly exciting and terrifying time, because the last time it felt like this was when I was a much younger man and I would go to the very early DEFCONs. DEFCON these days is like 40,000–60,000 people. Back then [in the 1990s] it was a couple hundred people and it was one track and you’d go in and somebody would give a talk and you’d leave the room and you’d think, “Every company in the world is vulnerable to this attack.” The difference was that the entire world didn’t run on the internet. You could go do bad things, but you couldn’t ruin the world and you certainly couldn’t automate it in the way you can now.It’s back to those days where tools you could just get and build yourself could do crazy things. It’s back to the Wild West days. Back in those days, there were a couple hundred people who had those skills and we were all in one room in Las Vegas and most of them were actually good guys. They didn’t want to be criminals. And now you have a much larger ecosystem of people, many of whom live in places where the law enforcement can’t touch and who have a big economic incentive and have access to these tools. The other big thing is they no longer have to use frontier models that have protections, that have logs that are available to law enforcement. My M5 Mac Ultra Studio finally showed up and I’ve been running a quantized obliterated GLM-5.3 and oh my God, what you can do is incredible.

title: US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation
title_bn: মার্কিন গোয়েন্দা সংস্থা বিশ্বাস করে যে জেন্সন হুয়াং এর সাথে চীনা গুপ্তচরবৃত্তি ছিল।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: U.S. intelligence sources suggest that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence in a 'honeypot' operation involving Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.
paragraph1: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang is the center of a new controversy as the U.S.
paragraph2: intelligence community believes that he had a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. According to the Financial Times, Alice Huang, sometimes referred to as Huang Le, was a top executive at Singaporean firm Megaspeed and was reportedly romantically involved with the CEO of the world's largest AI chip manufacturer.
paragraph3: Notably, Jensen is currently married to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang. It’s unclear whether Alice Huang was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS) before she joined Megaspeed or after she had already established a business relationship with Jensen, but it’s been reported that the suspected agent was apparently targeting the Nvidia head to help Chinese companies gain access to banned AI chips.
paragraph4: Go deeper with TH Premium: AI shortagesGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry.
paragraph5: He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.
bangla_paragraph1: এনভিডিয়া প্রধান জেন্সন হুয়াং নতুন বিতর্কের কেন্দ্রবিন্দুতে রয়েছেন।
bangla_paragraph2: গোয়েন্দা সম্প্রদায় বিশ্বাস করে যে তিনি একটি সন্দেহভাজন চীনা গুপ্তচরবৃত্তির সাথে একটি রোমান্টিক সম্পর্ক ছিল। ফিনান্সিয়াল টাইমস অনুসারে, এলিস হুয়াং, কখনও কখনও হুয়াঙ্গ লে নামে পরিচিত, সিঙ্গাপুরের সংস্থা মেগাসপিডের শীর্ষ নির্বাহী ছিলেন এবং বিশ্বের বৃহত্তম এআই চিপ প্রস্তুতকারকের প্রধান নির্বাহীর সাথে রোমান্টিকে সম্পর্ক ছিল বলে জানা গেছে।
bangla_paragraph3: উল্লেখযোগ্যভাবে, জেন্সন বর্তমানে তার 41 বছরের স্ত্রীর সাথে বিবাহবন্ধনে আবদ্ধ, লরি হুয়াং। এটি অস্পষ্ট যে এলিস হুয়াঙকে মেগাসপিডে যোগদানের আগে বা জেন্সনের সাথে ইতিমধ্যে ব্যবসায়িক সম্পর্ক স্থাপন করার পরে চীনা রাজ্য সুরক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয় (এমএসএস) নিয়োগ করেছিল কিনা, তবে এটি জানা গেছে যে সন্দেহভাজন এজেন্ট সম্ভবত নিষিদ্ধ এআই চিপগুলিতে অ্যাক্সেস পেতে চীনা সংস্থাগুলিকে সহায়তা করার জন্য এনভিডিয়া প্রধানকে লক্ষ্য করে।
bangla_paragraph4: TH Premium: AI shortages এর সাথে আরও গভীর যান আপনার ইনবক্সে সরাসরি টম হার্ডওয়্যারের সেরা খবর এবং গভীর পর্যালোচনা পান।

excerpt: Apple is still rocking and rolling a week into November, with five new products having launched this week and two more still on tap for next week. Things are also moving forward on the software side with Apple releasing the first betas of iOS 27.3 an
paragraph1: Apple is still rocking and rolling a week into November, with five new products having launched this week and two more still on tap for next week. Things are also moving forward on the software side with Apple releasing the first betas of iOS 27.3 and related updates, bringing a number of tweaks and new features. We're also looking ahead to new products coming in the first half of 2027, so read on below for all of the details on these stories and more! Top Stories Apple Launched Five New Products This Week Apple released five new products on Friday, November 6, following pre-orders that opened last week, including its first touchscreen MacBook Pro models. The following new products are now available: iPad mini with OLED display and A20 Pro chip iMac with M6 chip 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip 14-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen Apple's HomeView smart home hub and updated Apple TV 4K box will follow next week on Friday, November 13. Everything New in the iOS 27.3 Beta Apple this week started testing iOS 27.3, the biggest update to iOS 27 since it launched in September.
paragraph2: iOS 27.3 includes some features Apple showed off earlier this year, and it adds all-new capabilities. Among the changes in the update are Safari tweaks with a new Vertical Tabs layout option plus an Adaptive Dark Mode feature for websites that don't offer their own dark mode option, Siri AI improvements, an expansion of new iPhone Duo StandBy features to other iPhone models, and more. The revamped Health app that was in the 27.2 beta for testing but removed prior to the public release has returned in 27.3 and will be seeing a public launch before the end of the year. Apple Alerts Stores to iPhone Duo's Display Cracking Issue In a memo shared with Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers last week, and later obtained by MacRumors, Apple provided technicians with guidance on how to diagnose and address the iPhone Duo's inner display cracking issue. If a customer reports the issue, Apple advised technicians to inspect the iPhone Duo and repair or replace it in accordance with their standard procedures. While the instructions themselves are straightforward, the fact that Apple issued an internal memo suggests the issue is widespread enough to warrant official guidance.
paragraph3: Meanwhile, Apple CEO John Ternus this week said Apple is not able to predict when it will be able to meet demand for the foldable iPhone, with Bloomberg's Mark Gurman saying that Apple's change from its original plan to launch the device in November in just two countries has contributed to the difficulties in meeting demand. Three New iPads Rumored to Launch in First Half of 2027 The revamped iPad mini launching this week is one piece of Apple's tablet lineup, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says the rest of the lineup should be receiving updates in the first half of next year. The iPad Air will reportedly be getting an upgrade to OLED displays, while iPad Pro and base iPad updates should be more modest. Before those 2027 updates, there's still some time left in 2026, and while we're not expecting any more major product announcements before the end of the year, plenty of previously announced hardware and software updates are still on their way. Here's a New Tour of Apple's HomeView Software App developer Steve Troughton-Smith over the weekend shared a tour of the software on Apple's upcoming HomeView smart home hub. Apple has already demoed the HomeView to selected tech reporters and content creators, but Troughton-Smith offered a closer look at several features, interfaces, and apps. CarPlay-enabled audio and video apps from third-party developers will also be supported on HomeView, and Troughton-Smith shared a look at what Spotify will look like on the HomeView as well. We've known for quite some time that HomeView was ready to be released for quite some time while Apple waited for Siri AI to be launched as the primary interaction mechanism for it. That certainly appears to be the case as it seems the units will initially ship with six-month-old software version 26.
paragraph4: 5 and will have to be updated to HomeView software version 27.2 during setup. Apple's Flash Storage Suppliers Are Finally 'Getting Their Revenge' The Wall Street Journal's Rolfe Winkler last week reported that flash storage suppliers once "bullied" by Apple have been "getting their revenge" on the company over the past year due to a severe memory chip shortage, which stems from AI companies building out massive data centers that utilize significant amounts of flash storage and RAM. As the iPhone took off, Apple became the world's largest buyer of flash storage, and naturally that gave the company a lot of leverage in negotiations. The report goes into detail about some of the hardball tactics that were employed by Apple and its former head of procurement, Tony Blevins. Flash suppliers now have the upper hand, however, and high demand for their chips has resulted in shortages that are expected to persist through 2030 with high prices continuing as a result. title_bn: টিমগ্রুপ জিএ প্রো ২টিবি এসএসডি পর্যালোচনাঃ একটি মধ্য-পরিসীমা পিসিআইই ৫.০ এসএসডির একটি ঝামেলাপূর্ণ প্রচেষ্টা
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The TeamGroup GA Pro mostly misses. Decent QD8 and steady-state writes can’t make up for weak overall performance, poor efficiency, and high temps.
paragraph1: The TeamGroup GA Pro is a drive that mostly misses. While it has relatively good points at QD8 and acceptable steady-state write speed, overall performance is very low with this inefficient, hot-running drive. Reasons to buy +Performance highlights at QD8 +Respectable steady-state write speed Reasons to avoid -Very poor scores in some tests -Poor low-QD reads -Poor efficiency and high temps Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
paragraph2: Go to page: Every once in a while we get a drive that comes across our desk that stands out, for good or for bad. The TeamGroup GA Pro falls into the latter category, enough so that we re-checked our results and contacted the company. We’ve managed to mostly sort out what’s going on and, while this is not the worst drive around, it has enough problems that we would generally not recommend it except if it's on steep sale.TeamGroup’s array of storage offerings knows no bounds: if there’s a niche to cover, it makes an attempt.
paragraph3: The GA Pro feels like such a try, although we’re not completely sure where it fits into the mix. The company is still working to iron out the bugs, if it can, but the technology is old enough that we wouldn’t hold our breath. On paper, it’s a PCIe 5.0 drive with DRAM that should beat any PCIe 4.
paragraph4: 0 SSD, but we found it struggles to live up to its own class of drive. Bright points are few and far between, but at least we can say it’s not the worst drive we’ve seen. bangla_paragraph1: টিমগ্রুপ জিএ প্রো একটি ড্রাইভ যা বেশিরভাগ মিস করে। যদিও এটি QD8 এ তুলনামূলকভাবে ভাল পয়েন্ট এবং গ্রহণযোগ্য স্থিতিশীল-রাজ্যের লেখার গতি রয়েছে, তবে এই অকার্যকর, গরম চলমান ড্রাইভে সামগ্রিক পারফরম্যান্স খুব কম। কিনতে কারণ +QD8 এর পারফরমেন্স হাইলাইটস +সম্মানজনক স্থিতিস্থাপক-রাষ্ট্রের লেখের গতি এড়ানোর কারণ -কিছু পরীক্ষায় খুব খারাপ স্কোর -দুর্বল নিম্ন-QD পাঠ -দুঃখজনক দক্ষতা এবং উচ্চ তাপমাত্রা কেন আপনি টমের হার্ডওয়্যারকে বিশ্বাস করতে পারেন আমাদের বিশেষজ্ঞ পর্যালোচকরা ঘন্টা ব্যয় করে পরীক্ষা এবং পণ্য এবং পরিষেবা তুলনা করে।
bangla_paragraph2: পৃষ্ঠাটিতে যান: মাঝে মাঝে আমাদের ডেস্কের উপর এমন একটি ড্রাইভ আসে যা ভাল বা খারাপের জন্য দাঁড়িয়ে থাকে। টিমগ্রুপ জিএ প্রো শেষের বিভাগে পড়ে, যথেষ্ট পরিমাণে যাতে আমরা আমাদের ফলাফলগুলি আবার পরীক্ষা করে দেখি এবং সংস্থার সাথে যোগাযোগ করি। আমরা বেশিরভাগ ক্ষেত্রে কী চলছে তা সাজাতে সক্ষম হয়েছি এবং এটি সবচেয়ে খারাপ ড্রাইভার না হলেও, এটির পর্যাপ্ত সমস্যা রয়েছে যা আমরা সাধারণত এটিকে সুপারিশ করব না যদি না এটি তীব্র বিক্রয় হয়। টিमগ্রুপের স্টোরেজ অফারগুলির অ্যারে কোনও সীমা জানে নাঃ যদি সেখানে একটি কুলুঙ্গি t
bangla_paragraph3: GA Pro এমন একটি চেষ্টা বলে মনে হচ্ছে, যদিও আমরা সম্পূর্ণরূপে নিশ্চিত নই যে এটি মিশ্রণে কোথায় ফিট করে। সংস্থাটি এখনও যদি এটি করতে পারে তবে বাগগুলি ঠিক করার জন্য কাজ করছে, তবে প্রযুক্তিটি যথেষ্ট পুরানো যে আমরা আমাদের শ্বাস ধরে রাখতে পারি না। কাগজে, এটি পিসিআইই 5.0 ড্রাইভ DRAM সহ যা কোনও পিসিই 4 কে পরাজিত করা উচিত।
bangla_paragraph4: 0 এসএসডি, কিন্তু আমরা এটি তার নিজস্ব শ্রেণীর ড্রাইভের সাথে বসবাস করতে সংগ্রাম খুঁজে পেয়েছি। উজ্জ্বল পয়েন্টগুলি অল্প এবং দূরবর্তী, তবে কমপক্ষে আমরা বলতে পারি এটি আমরা দেখেছি সবচেয়ে খারাপ ড্রাইভার নয়। প্রান্তগুলি স্বাভাবিকের চেয়ে রুক্ষ।টম এর হার্ডওয়্যার থেকে সর্বশেষ ভিডিওগুলিকটিউন এজ থাকুনঃ টম এর হারডওয়্যার নিউজলেটার পানটম হার্ডওয়ারের সেরা সংবাদ এবং গভীর পর্যালোচনাগুলি পান, সরাসরি আপনার ইনবক্সে।
bangla_paragraph5: অবদানকারী লেখক শেন ডাউনিং হলেন টমস হার্ডওয়্যারের অবদানকারীর লেখক, যা ভোক্তা স্টোরেজ, পিসি হার্ডওয়ার এবং এআইকে কভার করে।

title: Zelda is back and better than ever
title_bn: জেল্ডা ফিরে এসেছে এবং আগের চেয়ে ভালো আছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 151, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you're new here, welcome, get psyched because it's officially Bad Holiday Movie Season, and also you can read all the old editions at the Install
paragraph1: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 151, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, get psyched because it’s officially Bad Holiday Movie Season, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.)This week, I’ve been reading about Andrew Garfield and GTA VI and sexy joke thieves, finally actually watching The Sopranosfor the first time (I know, I know), mourning the end of Salon, reinstalling the new and extremely improved Notion Calendar, testing the new Keurig Alta coffee machine, reviewing the iPad Mini and the touchscreen MacBook Pro, and really thinking about just throwing it all away and buying an Enough Phone.I also have for you the long-awaited return of a classic Zelda game, a monster movie worth the trek to the theater, a couple of great new phone accessories, awesome retro headphones, and more. Let’s do it.(As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you watching / reading / playing / listening to / hacking onto an E Ink display this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.)The DropThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. I have a confession to make: I’ve never played this game all the way through. Not sure how! Just missed it. But seeing my friends and coworkers fall back in love with Hyrule has convinced me to get all the way into the remake.
paragraph2: I genuinely can’t wait.Godzilla Minus Zero. Three years ago, Godzilla Minus One was a big hit and a surprisingly great movie. The sequel came with much higher expectations, but everyone seems to agree it’s a deserving follow-up. I’m not generally one for monster movies, but this series really does it for me.Affinity for iPad. Canva’s app now unifies all its tools in one place, just like on the Mac. Affinity makes perfect sense on the iPad, and comes with lots of Apple Pencil integration and clever touch-friendly tools. I’m no designer, but I am excited to play with this as a photo editing tool.The Moft Dynamic Folio Case. Here’s one for all you iPhone Duo buyers. Moft’s cases are a little complicated to figure out, but really cleverly designed to make your phone even more useful. I’m guessing this is going to be a lot better than Apple’s weird case / kickstand thing.The Peak Design Kickstand Travel Battery. While we’re on the subject of kickstands, here’s the one I’m buying this week. Peak Design makes good stuff, and I frequently find that I need extra juice at exactly the moment I want to watch something on a plane or train. This one’s going right into my backpack and probably never coming out.
paragraph3: The Bambu Lab H3C. I am dangerously close to becoming a 3D Printer Dude. At $2,500, this one’s a little steep for my wallet, but I think my colleague Sean Hollister is right that this is what the future of 3D printing looks like. Simpler, more foolproof, easy enough even for a goofus like me to make some pretty cool stuff.“Ranking the world’s most popular pens for journaling.” I know we all love a good pen — and Peter McKinnon does an excellent job of breaking down a few dozen supposedly good pens to see which ones really hold up. I bought more than one pen after watching this.Instagram Edits for Mac. Oh, great, just as I was finally getting good at CapCut! I like the Edits mobile app a lot, and the desktop app seems to be even a little more powerful. Plus: free. This is how I finally take down Cristiano Ronaldo.The Sony MDR-3R headphones. Respect to Sony for taking the retro headphone trend all the way to its logical conclusion and just releasing the headphones from the original Walkman. You’ll look a little like Nathan Fielder in You Can See Everything when you wear them, and $60 ain’t cheap, but there’s something so incredibly ’70s-era cool about them.The Motorola Signature 27. This is just a pure tour de force of a smartphone spec sheet.
paragraph4: Monster camera; brightest screen; giant battery. Also very cool to see a flagship phone with support for GrapheneOS, for the less Google-inclined among us. It’s expensive, and only shipping… someday… but I just like that phones like this exist.We talked last week about Readwise Books, the new app that’s a mix of Kindle, Goodreads, and Strava. I’m a longtime fan and user of Readwise Reader, so I wasn’t shocked that I liked the new app a lot, too. And I’ve heard from a bunch of you that you do, too!I’ve talked to Tristan Homsi, one of the Readwise cofounders, a few times over the years, and have always enjoyed hearing his thoughts about reading, apps, and digital products in general. I asked him to share his homescreen to see if I might be able to get a hint about what he’s reading and the other stuff he thinks is good. (I also asked Daniel Doyon, Readwise’s other cofounder, to share, and he didn’t respond. Daniel is dead to me.)Here’s Tristan’s homescreen, plus some info on the apps he uses and why:The phone: iPhone 13 (!)Believe it or not, I chose to buy this relatively outdated phone last year… not because it’s my favorite form factor or anything, but because it’s closer in specs to the median device our Readwise users have and helps me build a bit more user empathy with them. I’m able to catch performance regressions and bugs in Readwise that the developers on our team with Duos and Pro Maxes and such miss.Let me tell you though, iOS 26 itself does not work amazingly on an iPhone 13. Lots of lagging and janky animations. I am somewhat bought into the conspiracy theory that they make the old phones suck so you buy a new one… not so much intentionally, but rather by virtue of just making each successive iOS use more and more resources, doing fancier and fancier things.​The wallpaper: My lovely wife and my cat Sophie :)The apps: Clock, Settings, Google Calendar, Camera, Google Maps, Spotify, Bay Wheels, Oura, Eight Sleep, Auto Eight, BeReal, ChatGPT, Runmeter, Strava, Readwise Highlights, Readwise Reader, Phone, Messages, Safari.
paragraph5: Of course, I have all three Readwise apps front and center. Highlights and Reader as app icons, and Readwise Books in widget form at the top! It’s a great reminder to jump back into your current book (I’m reading Apple in China right now… speaking of Apple!) instead of scrolling twitter (on a later page), and seeing my friends currently reading really makes me want to jump in and join them :)I also am a huge fan of the somewhat-defunct social app BeReal. It had its moment in 2022, but quite a few of my friends are still on there! You post once a day, can see what your close friends around the world are doing, and most importantly can’t get sucked in for more than two minutes since it limits you to a random photo or two a day! I still post basically every day, and have almost five years of memories in there.Speaking of getting sucked in, I don’t have it pictured on my home screen, but I also have Clearspace installed, which helps me stay off of all social media.Some other apps shown on the homescreen: “auto eight” is something I vibecoded to better control my Eight Sleep mattress (lol)… Strava and Runmeter are awesome for tracking my runs… and Bay Wheels is my main mode of commute around San Francisco daily.I also asked Tristan to share a few things he’s into right now. Here’s what he sent back:I follow some amazing niche internet blogs, which you should check out if you haven’t. I love the blog Slime Mold Time Mold, famous for their citizen science and potato-maxxing. I also love Gwern.net, Deepfates, and Dynomight… among many others!And of course I’m always reading books. The most recent fiction series I loved was the Red Knight series — which I can only recommend if you are into dense, dark, fantasy — but man, if you are, the author is a genius.For non-fiction, it’s hard for me to plug anything but my favorite book of all time, The Beginning of Infinity.

title: Enthusiast abandons self-hosted Microsoft Exchange after 27 years, moving mailboxes to Microsoft 365
title_bn: ২৭ বছর পর মাইক্রোসফট এক্সচেঞ্জকে পরিত্যাগ করে মাইক্রোজফট ৩৬৫-এ মেইলবক্স স্থানান্তর করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A homelab enthusiast is retiring a Microsoft Exchange installation that began with Exchange 5.5 on Windows NT 4 in 1999. After migrating mailboxes to Microsoft 365, he kept Exchange 2019 running to relay local hardware and software alerts. Postfix on
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) Running your own email server is one thing. Keeping it alive for nearly three decades is quite another. One homelab enthusiast has finally decided to call time on his Microsoft Exchange installation after maintaining it since 1999, replacing the last remaining server with Postfix on Ubuntu Server LTS.
paragraph2: The user, posting as Meta4X on Reddit’s r/homelab on November 5, said they had already moved their mailboxes and email delivery to Microsoft 365 a couple of years ago. Exchange was still hanging around, however, serving as a relay for alerts generated by hardware and software on their local network. With that final job now being handed to Postfix, the 27-year run is coming to an end.
paragraph3: Pour One Out For My Homies - 27 Years of Exchange at Home from r/homelabGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Newton Gitonga is a tech journalist covering gadgets, PC hardware, AI, data centers, and the wider tech industry. His interest in technology started early, taking apart things around the house to see how they worked, often to his dad’s frustration.
paragraph4: His curiosity sometimes got the better of him, including a few failed attempts to fix laptops, one of them a gifted Dell XPS. He has previously written for Notebookcheck, ZyCrypto, CoinCentral, and Crypto News Flash.

title: New Bluetooth High Data Throughput may finally satisfy audiophiles
title_bn: নতুন ব্লুটুথ হাই ডেটা থ্রুপুট অবশেষে অডিওফিলদের সন্তুষ্ট করতে পারে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Bluetooth HDT can offer a maximum bandwidth of 7.5 Mbps, allowing Bluetooth to be used with more sophisticated devices or big lossless audio files.
paragraph1: The Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG) just announced the new Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT) feature on November 4, allowing a maximum bandwidth of 7.5 Mbps, almost 4x that of the previous Bluetooth LE 2M (2 Mbps).
paragraph2: The new bandwidth is intended for high-bandwidth interactions between devices, such as AI, spatial computing, and even lossless audio transmission; the latter of which may finally satisfy audiophiles and their enjoyment of uncompressed audio.Bluetooth HDT is Bluetooth’s new feature allowing for up to 7.
paragraph3: 5 Mbps of bandwidth. This new feature is needed by sophisticated modern devices that use a lot of data in their communication.
paragraph4: It could be smartwatches, AI, or even extended reality (XR); less sophisticated but high-bandwidth, however, is lossless audio, which Bluetooth has never had enough bandwidth for, until HDT, that is.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
title_bn: কেন অ্যানথ্রোপিক অটোমেটিং এআই ডেভেলপমেন্টের একটি নতুন রিপোর্ট গবেষকদের উদ্বেগজনক করে তোলে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company's models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down. That's according to a new report publis
paragraph1: Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company’s models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down.That’s according to a new report published Thursday by the AI safety research organization METR, following an 11-week investigation inside the company, as part of a report evaluating its AI research and development. The probe is separate from a program offering safety researchers “employee-like” access to systems in the wake of high-profile hacking incidents over the summer.The findings offer some of the clearest evidence yet of AI accelerating its own development, raising questions about how quickly the technology could advance toward a future in which AI systems can improve themselves with little or no human involvement. They also come at a pivotal time for Anthropic, which is preparing to go public even as its CEO, Dario Amodei, has publicly called for labs to pump the brakes on AI development.But while the report offers a rare glimpse into the inner workings of the world’s leading AI labs, what it leaves out is just as revealing. Anthropic was permitted to redact portions of the final report as part of its agreement with METR, and it appears to have exercised that power liberally, raising questions about how much the public really knows about the pace — and risks — of frontier AI development.Here are some of the biggest takeaways.
paragraph2: AI is dramatically accelerating Anthropic’s research and developmentOne of METR’s most noteworthy findings is that Anthropic’s AI models are improving roughly twice as quickly as they were a year ago, with benchmark scores suggesting “that Anthropic has made roughly two years of historical progress over the last year.” Crucially, METR’s researchers said they “are confident” that the acceleration was not simply due to scaling up the computing power used to train the models, which historically has been a major driver of AI progress.Instead, the researchers said that the majority of the acceleration as of October “is due to AI,” with its contribution growing over time. That finding was supported by informal Slack polls and interviews with Anthropic employees, which pointed to sizable productivity gains. METR wrote that employees using Anthropic’s most capable internal model on average self-reported being around 12 times as productive at their respective work as they would have been without AI assistance, around double what staff had reported just a few months earlier while using Mythos 5.For now, much of that acceleration appears to be coming from AI assisting human researchers, rather than AI working independently, though METR warned that “there are some signs that fully autonomous contributions will play a larger role soon.” Notably, the researchers said they found no clear signs of diminishing returns or observable bottlenecks that could prevent “even faster acceleration.”Three of Anthropic’s newest AI models remain under wrapsAnthropic’s researchers are using more advanced AI models than the rest of us, with a lot of the acceleration and productivity gains described by METR attributable to unreleased internal models.Over the past six months, Anthropic has finished training three models it has yet to release, according to METR.
paragraph3: The pace of development is swift, with the models — codenamed Model 2, Model 3, and Model 4 — completing training in July, August-September, and September-October, respectively. METR also identified an unreleased model dating back to 2022, called Unreleased 2022. “These are the codenames shared with us; we understand they have different internal codenames,” the researchers wrote.Anthropic is keeping key information secretAnthropic gave METR access to a host of non-public information, including confidential research, model performance data, and employee interviews as part of the research process. It had no obligation to do so and by METR’s own admission, the AI lab “shared more information than was initially scoped for this project, surpassing our expectations.” This is commendable, but it is worth noting that Anthropic did not grant researchers unrestricted access, nor the kind of “employee-like” access it has promised other METR safety researchers as part of a separate program announced last month. It is an important distinction, given the reputational benefits companies can gain from independent assessments, even when they come with significant restrictions.And there were significant restrictions. Anthropic had the power to redact information from METR’s final report — and it used that power extensively.
paragraph4: “We submitted a ~100-page full report on our assessment to Anthropic. For the public version, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative,” METR wrote on X.METR reiterated those concerns throughout the report, highlighting other limitations on its access. “Our pipeline of information was relatively narrow, and a small number of our requests for data were denied.”METR repeatedly stressed the impact Anthropic’s redaction decisions had on its ability to communicate its findings and for others to assess what’s going on at the company. It noted that much of the redacted evidence could have “multiple plausible interpretations,” making it difficult for the public to assess its findings, understand the uncertainties surrounding them, and judge the evidence themselves. “As a consequence [of the redactions], the public has to rely on METR’s judgment much more than would be ideal, given the weight of the questions answered here,” the report said.In the report, METR said Anthropic justified the redactions on the grounds that releasing the information could benefit its rivals. However, METR said “most of the redacted information was very high-level,” even though it said it was not in position to comment whether redactions were justified commercially or not.
paragraph5: “We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work,” Anthropic cofounder Sam McCandlish acknowledged in a lengthy post on X responding to METR’s findings. “But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster,” he said, adding that doing so would make the risks METR is concerned about “worse.”McCandlish said that it’s a trade-off, but maintained Anthropic had made the “right call” in deciding to redact the information. He said the company plans to publish its own report on the speed of AI progress “in the coming weeks,” as well as new steps it’s taking to strengthen safety.Anthropic is accelerating the very technology it warns is dangerous and faster than many expectedThe publication of METR’s report has provoked a fierce backlash among AI safety researchers and commentators, largely centered on an apparent contradiction at the heart of Anthropic’s approach to AI: The company has been one of the most outspoken advocates for safety and responsible development, yet the report suggests it is helping accelerate the technology toward a threshold many consider dangerous, while seemingly failing to live up to its own commitments to transparency and accountability.For some, the findings suggest that even many of the field’s most aggressive predictions about AI progress may be too conservative. They indicate that recursive self-improvement — AI systems that can autonomously develop increasingly powerful successor systems without human intervention, potentially accelerating development dramatically — may be closer than previously thought, raising concerns about whether existing safety measures can keep pace. While METR’s report only covers Anthropic, OpenAI said in September that it is “making strong progress” toward building an AI researcher that can “further progress on deep learning and alignment” by March 2028.
