bangla_paragraph2: এআই অ্যানথ্রপিকের গবেষণা ও উন্নয়নকে নাটকীয়ভাবে ত্বরান্বিত করছেএমইটিআর এর সবচেয়ে উল্লেখযোগ্য ফলাফলগুলির মধ্যে একটি হ'ল অ্যান্থ্রপিক্সের এআই মডেলগুলি এক বছর আগে তুলনায় প্রায় দ্বিগুণ দ্রুত উন্নতি করছে, বেঞ্চমার্ক স্কোরগুলি ইঙ্গিত দেয় যে অ্যান্ট্রপাইক গত বছরের তুলনায় মোটামুটি দুই বছরের ঐতিহাসিক অগ্রগতি করেছে।
bangla_paragraph3: মডেল ২, মডেল ৩ এবং মডেল ৪ এর কোড নামের মডেলগুলি দ্রুত বিকাশের গতিতে রয়েছে, যথাক্রমে জুলাই, আগস্ট-সেপ্টেম্বর এবং সেপ্টেম্বর-অক্টোবরে প্রশিক্ষণ সম্পন্ন করে। এমইটিআর ২০২২ সাল থেকে প্রকাশিত হয়নি এমন একটি মডেলও সনাক্ত করেছে, যার নাম আনলিসড ২০২১।
bangla_paragraph4: আমরা এন্থ্রপিককে আমাদের মূল্যায়ন সম্পর্কে প্রায় ১০০ পৃষ্ঠার একটি সম্পূর্ণ প্রতিবেদন জমা দিয়েছি। জনসাধারণের সংস্করণের জন্য, এন্থ্ৰপিক আমরা সবচেয়ে তথ্যবহুল বলে মনে করি এমন বেশিরভাগ প্রমাণকে সংশোধন করেছে, এমইটিআর এক্স-এ লিখেছিল।এমইটিআর এই উদ্বেগগুলি প্রতিবেদনের সর্বত্র পুনরাবৃত্তি করেছে, এর অ্যাক্সেসের অন্যান্য সীমাবদ্ধতা তুলে ধরেছে। আমাদের তথ্য পাইপলাইন তুলনামূলকভাবে সংকীর্ণ ছিল এবং আমাদের তথ্যের অনুরোধগুলির একটি ছোট সংখ্যা অস্বীকার করা হয়েছিল।এমইটির বারবার জোর দেওয়া হয়েছিল যে এন্থ্রিকের সংশোধন সিদ্ধান্তগুলি তার যোগাযোগের ক্ষমতা সম্পর্কে ছিল
bangla_paragraph5: আমরা অনেক কিছু সম্পাদনা করেছি এবং আমি স্বীকার করি যে এটি অন্যদের জন্য METR এর কাজ পরীক্ষা করা কঠিন করে তোলে, এন্থ্রপিকের সহ-প্রতিষ্ঠাতা স্যাম ম্যাকক্যান্ডলিশ X-এ একটি দীর্ঘ পোস্টে স্বীকার করেছেন। কিন্তু আমরা সিদ্ধান্ত নিয়েছি যে গতি বাড়ানোর সঠিক কারণটি ভাগ করে নেওয়া সঠিক নয়, কারণ এটি বাণিজ্যিকভাবে সংবেদনশীল এবং এটি অন্যের জন্য আরও দ্রুত যাওয়ার জন্য একটি রোডম্যাপ বিতরণ করার ঝুঁকি রয়েছে, তিনি বলেছিলেন, এটি করলে MET R এর উদ্বেগজনক ঝুঁকিগুলি আরও খারাপ হয়ে যাবে।ম্যাককান্ডলিশ বলেন

title: The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
title_bn: বান্টু বিস্তার আফ্রিকাকে বদলে দিয়েছে। বিজ্ঞানীরা এখনও কিভাবে তা খুঁজে বের করছেন।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Genes and archaeology are revealing how Bantu speakers spread across much of Africa.
paragraph1: On the move Genes and archaeology are revealing how Bantu speakers spread across much of Africa. The dry-stone wall ruins of Great Zimbabwe—an ancient African capital that once presided over a thriving kingdom across much of modern-day Zimbabwe—are one legacy of the Bantu-speaking people who migrated there from western Africa. Credit: evanfh/Getty The dry-stone wall ruins of Great Zimbabwe—an ancient African capital that once presided over a thriving kingdom across much of modern-day Zimbabwe—are one legacy of the Bantu-speaking people who migrated there from western Africa. Credit: evanfh/Getty It’s not easy to extract iron from its ore. But the peoples of the ancient city of Great Zimbabwe—the capital of a thriving kingdom in southern Africa between 1000 to 1700 AD—were masters. At sites near the city’s stone ruins, clusters of iron-smelting furnaces survive today as mounds of rubble. At Mashava, a village 25 miles northwest, fragments bear fingermarks of those who long ago smoothed the structures’ clay interiors. Some of the furnaces were nearly an adult’s arm span in width, with walls thick and strong to contain the heat of more than 2,100° Fahrenheit needed to smelt iron. Unlike other furnaces that required workers to force air into them with bellows, these were designed to suck air in, then out through a chimney, no human labor required.
paragraph2: This would have made it significantly easier to produce the iron, which was fashioned into hoes, axes, and arrowheads. “The number and size of these furnaces, together with the use of natural-draft technology, indicate intensive and technologically sophisticated iron production,” says archaeometallurgist Ezekiel Mtetwa of Chicago’s Field Museum of Natural History, who has long studied the furnaces. Scientists are extremely interested in the peoples who created this and other iron-powered societies across eastern and southern Africa. Research points to an adaptable and innovative group from western Africa as the masterminds. Known as Bantu speakers, these communities began gradually expanding across the continent’s southern half, starting from 6,000 to 4,000 years ago. In doing so, they introduced a fundamentally new, sedentary way of life—characterized by farming, raising livestock, pottery-making, and metalworking—to regions previously dominated by hunter-gatherer communities. This migration transformed not only the region’s history and technology, but also its languages: Today, around 350 million Africans speak one of roughly 500 distinct Bantu tongues, from southern African Zulu to eastern African Swahili. And at least as many Africans—as well as many African Americans and Afro-Latinos—carry Bantu ancestry in their DNA. Reconstructing this expansion has been a tough puzzle, especially given the region’s sparse written historical records and limited research funding.
paragraph3: But a unique blend of scientists—linguists, archaeologists, and geneticists—have teamed up to unearth clues about the deep origins of the Bantu-speaking people, their path across Africa, and their relationships with other cultures. Although much debate and uncertainty remain, little by little the work is uncovering one of history’s largest and longest human migrations. “It completely reshaped the demography in sub-Saharan Africa, and we are really interested in trying to understand it,” says population geneticist Sandra Beleza of the United Kingdom’s University of Leicester. People on the move The first evidence of the Bantu expansion came from observations of similarities among Bantu languages. They’re so alike, in fact, that when the Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama sailed around the southern tip of Africa in 1497, a Portuguese crew member who had spent time in west-central Africa could reportedly communicate with locals in southeastern Africa. Linguists working in the 19th century started referring to the language family as Bantu, the plural of muntu, meaning “human being” in many Bantu tongues. Later linguists reasoned that the languages stemmed from an ancestral people who migrated across the continent from western Africa, which harbors the greatest diversity of Bantu languages (as would be expected for where the languages originated). Soon, archaeologists found supporting evidence: across eastern and southern Africa, pieces of pottery of similar yet diverse styles, alongside first-time traces of village life, metal-making, domesticated animals, and western African crops—all developed within the last 2,000 years. Northern sites usually dated back to earlier time periods than sites farther south.
paragraph4: “You can clearly see a north-to-south progression,” says archaeological scientist Shadreck Chirikure of the University of Oxford. By the 1990s, however, some scholars began to question the idea that Bantu languages and skills spread through a migration. Couldn’t these cultural habits have spread while people stayed in the same place, with hunter gatherer communities passing along new technologies, languages, and habits to each other? Genetic techniques that could analyze people’s ancestry helped to resolve that debate. All of us share DNA with our relatives: 50 percent on average with siblings, 12.5 percent with cousins, 3.3 percent with second cousins, and so on. Though these proportions become minute the further back in time a shared common ancestor lived, statistical techniques can tease out patterns. Sure enough, a 2009 genetic analysis of 2,432 Africans found that Bantu-speaking people from western, central, and southern Africa are much more closely related than one might expect given their geographic distance.
paragraph5: And in 2024, a team of scientists analyzed the genomes of 1,763 Africans and found the greatest genetic diversity among Bantu speakers in western Africa. As distance from the region increased, diversity declined. “This is a typical signature of a population expanding from one place to another,” explains coauthor Carina Schlebusch, a geneticist at Uppsala University in Sweden. Roughly 350 million people across sub-Saharan Africa speak one of roughly 500 Bantu languages—from Swahili in eastern Africa to Xhosa spoken in southern Africa. Credit: Wikimedia Commons Roughly 350 million people across sub-Saharan Africa speak one of roughly 500 Bantu languages—from Swahili in eastern Africa to Xhosa spoken in southern Africa. Credit: Wikimedia Commons Mysterious roots But while linguistic and genetic data point to western Africa—particularly the Grassfields region of Cameroon—as the Bantu homeland, conclusive archaeological proof is thin. At the best-studied archaeological site in the Grassfields, a rock shelter called Shum Laka, pottery fragments appear dating from 7,000 to 6,000 years ago and become abundant by 5,000 to 4,000 years ago.
bangla_paragraph1: চলতে চলতে জিন এবং প্রত্নতত্ত্ব প্রকাশ করছে কিভাবে বান্টু ভাষাভাষীরা আফ্রিকার বেশিরভাগ অংশে ছড়িয়ে পড়ে। গ্রেট জিম্বাবুয়ের শুকনো পাথরের প্রাচীর ধ্বংসাবশেষএকটি প্রাচীন আফ্রিকান রাজধানী যা একসময় আধুনিক জিম্বাবোয়ের বেশিরভাগ অংশ জুড়ে একটি সমৃদ্ধ রাজ্যের সভাপতিত্ব করেছিলএটি পশ্চিম আফ্রিকা থেকে সেখানে অভিবাসিত বান্টুর ভাষাভাষা মানুষের একটি উত্তরাধিকার। ক্রেডিটঃ evanfh/Getty গ্রেট জাম্বুয়েএক প্রাচীন অস্ট্রিয়ান রাজধানীর শুকনো-পাহর প্রাচির ধ্বংসাবলী যা এক সময় আধুনিক জিম্বাবোয়ের অনেক অংশ জুড়েই একটি সম্রষ্ট রাজ্যের প্রধানত্ব করেছিল।
bangla_paragraph2: প্রাকৃতিক-প্রস্রাব প্রযুক্তির ব্যবহারের সাথে এই চুল্লির সংখ্যা এবং আকার, নিবিড় এবং প্রযুক্তিগতভাবে পরিশীলিত লোহার উত্পাদন নির্দেশ করে, শিকাগো ফিল্ড মিউজিয়াম অফ ন্যাচারাল হিস্ট্রি এর প্রত্নতাত্ত্বিক ধাতুবিদ হিজিকিউল মটেটওয়া বলেছেন, যিনি দীর্ঘদিন ধরে চুল্লী অধ্যয়ন করেছেন। বিজ্ঞানীরা এই এবং অন্যান্য লোহা চালিত সমাজগুলি তৈরির বিষয়ে অত্যন্ত আগ্রহী।
bangla_paragraph3: কিন্তু বিজ্ঞানীদের একটি অনন্য মিশ্রণ - ভাষাবিদ, প্রত্নতাত্ত্বিক এবং বংশবিজ্ঞানীরা - বান্টু ভাষী মানুষের গভীর উৎপত্তি, আফ্রিকা জুড়ে তাদের পথ এবং অন্যান্য সংস্কৃতির সাথে তাদের সম্পর্ক সম্পর্কে সূত্র উন্মোচন করতে একত্রিত হয়েছে। যদিও অনেক বিতর্ক এবং অনিশ্চয়তা এখনও রয়েছে, ধীরে ধীরে কাজটি ইতিহাসের বৃহত্তম এবং দীর্ঘতম মানব অভিবাসনের একটি প্রকাশ করছে। এটি সাব-সাহারান আফ্রিকার জনগাঁথনকে সম্পূর্ণরূপে পুনর্নির্মাণ করেছে এবং আমরা এটি বোঝার চেষ্টা করতে সত্যিই আগ্রহী", পপ বলেছেন।
bangla_paragraph4: আপনি স্পষ্টভাবে উত্তর থেকে দক্ষিণে অগ্রগতি দেখতে পারেন, অক্সফোর্ড বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের প্রত্নতাত্ত্বিক বিজ্ঞানী শ্যাড্রেক চিরিকুরে বলেছেন। তবে ১৯৯০ এর দশকে, কিছু পণ্ডিত এই ধারণাটি নিয়ে প্রশ্ন করতে শুরু করেছিলেন যে বান্টু ভাষা এবং দক্ষতা একটি অভিবাসনের মাধ্যমে ছড়িয়ে পড়েছিল। এই সাংস্কৃতিক অভ্যাসগুলি কি একই জায়গায় থাকা অবস্থায় ছড়িয়ে পড়তে পারে, শিকারী-সংগ্রাহক সম্প্রদায়গুলি একে অপরের কাছে নতুন প্রযুক্তি, ভাষা এবং অভ্যাসগুলি পাস করে? মানুষের বংশধরত্ব বিশ্লেষণ করতে পারে এমন জেনেটিক কৌশলগুলি সাহায্য করেছিল
bangla_paragraph5: এবং ২০২৪ সালে, বিজ্ঞানীরা ১,৭৬৩ আফ্রিকানদের জিনোম বিশ্লেষণ করে পশ্চিম আফ্রিকার বান্টু ভাষীদের মধ্যে সবচেয়ে বড় জেনেটিক বৈচিত্র্য খুঁজে পেয়েছেন। অঞ্চল থেকে দূরত্ব বাড়ার সাথে সাথে বৈচিত্র্যের হ্রাস ঘটে। এটি একটি স্থান থেকে অন্য জায়গায় প্রসারিত জনসংখ্যার একটি সাধারণ স্বাক্ষর, সুইডেনের উপসালা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের জেনেটিক্স বিশেষজ্ঞ সহ-লেখক কারিনা শ্লেবুশ ব্যাখ্যা করেছেন। উপ-সাহারান আফ্রিকা জুড়ে প্রায় ৩৫০ মিলিয়ন মানুষ প্রায় ৫০০ বান্টুর ভাষাগুলির মধ্যে একটিতে কথা বলে।

bangla_paragraph1: কেন আমাকে ব্লক করা হয়েছে? এই ওয়েবসাইটটি অনলাইন আক্রমণ থেকে নিজেকে রক্ষা করার জন্য একটি নিরাপত্তা পরিষেবা ব্যবহার করছে।
bangla_paragraph2: আপনি যে ক্রিয়াটি সবেমাত্র সম্পাদন করেছেন তা নিরাপত্তা সমাধানটি ট্রিগার করেছে। এমন বেশ কয়েকটি ক্রিয়া রয়েছে যা একটি নির্দিষ্ট শব্দ বা বাক্যাংশ, একটি এসকিউএল কমান্ড বা ত্রুটিযুক্ত ডেটা জমা দেওয়া সহ এই ব্লকটি ট্রিকার করতে পারে।
bangla_paragraph3: আপনি সাইটের মালিককে ইমেইল করে জানাতে পারেন যে আপনাকে ব্লক করা হয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph4: দয়া করে এই পৃষ্ঠাটি যখন প্রকাশিত হয়েছিল তখন আপনি কী করছিলেন এবং ক্লাউডফ্লেয়ার রে আইডিটি এই পৃষ্ঠার নীচে পাওয়া গেছে তা অন্তর্ভুক্ত করুন।

title: British soldier ignored order to pull his SIM card, then got blackmailed
title_bn: ব্রিটিশ সৈনিক তার সিম কার্ড বের করার আদেশ উপেক্ষা করে, তারপর তাকে শ্যান্টেল করা হয়
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Soldier told repeatedly to lock down devices before deploying, got sextorted, court-martialed.
paragraph1: On January 19, Barton-Kennedy informed his platoon commander that he had received a message “from an unknown party who had acquired nude photographs of him from the photo section of his mobile phone and had identified him on social media.” Barton-Kennedy initially acquiesced to paying the attacker 100 British pounds ($133) but balked when he was asked to pay 250 British pounds ($333), and only then informed his platoon commander what had happened. Eventually, Barton-Kennedy was court-martialed and pled guilty at a hearing on July 30.
paragraph2: During that process, according to the court filing, Barton-Kennedy understood the orders that were given to him at the time, but asked the court to “consider the personal circumstances” that he faced at the time. Without his phone, he told the court, he could not reach his daughter on her birthday, nor his pregnant partner. In a written statement, Barton-Kennedy said he was stunned when he received the first blackmail message.
paragraph3: “Despite still being in a state of shock and uncertainty, I recognised that I had a duty to report the compromise without any further delay,” he wrote. Additionally, he said that he “deeply regrets” the incident and added that serving in the British Army “has been one of the greatest privileges of my life.” Barton-Kennedy appealed the sentence, which was denied in August 2026.
paragraph4: In response to an inquiry for comment, Lt. Col. EP Mackie, a British Army spokesperson, told Ars in a statement that the security measures imposed are meant to protect the safety of military personnel.
paragraph5: “Any breaches of Army security measures that might compromise personal safeguarding or operational security will be dealt with swiftly, and offending personnel can expect uncompromising disciplinary action,” he wrote.
bangla_paragraph1: ১৯ জানুয়ারি, বার্টন-কেনেডি তার প্লাটুন কমান্ডারকে জানিয়েছিলেন যে তিনি একটি বার্তা পেয়েছেন অজানা পক্ষের কাছ থেকে যিনি তার মোবাইল ফোনের ফটো বিভাগ থেকে তার নগ্ন ছবি অর্জন করেছিলেন এবং তাকে সামাজিক যোগাযোগমাধ্যমে সনাক্ত করেছিলেন। বার্টণ-কেনিডি প্রথমে আক্রমণকারীকে ১০০ ব্রিটিশ পাউন্ড (১৩৩ ডলার) দিতে রাজি হন তবে ২৫০ ব্রিটিস পাউণ্ড (৩৩৩ ডলারের) অর্থ প্রদানের জন্য তাকে জিজ্ঞাসা করা হলে তিনি বিরক্ত হন এবং তারপরে তার প্ল্যাটুন কমাণ্ডারকে কী ঘটেছিল তা জানান। শেষ পর্যন্ত বার্টান-কেনডিকে সামরিক আদালতে হাজির করা হয়েছিল।
bangla_paragraph2: আদালতের ফাইলিং অনুযায়ী, সেই প্রক্রিয়া চলাকালীন, বার্টন-কেনেডি সেই সময়ে তাকে দেওয়া আদেশগুলি বুঝতে পেরেছিলেন, তবে আদালতকে তার ব্যক্তিগত পরিস্থিতি বিবেচনা করতে বলেছিলেন। তিনি আদালত বলেছিলেন যে তার ফোন ছাড়া তিনি তার মেয়ের জন্মদিনে বা তার গর্ভবতী সঙ্গীর সাথে যোগাযোগ করতে পারবেন না। একটি লিখিত বিবৃতিতে, বার্টন-কেনিডি বলেছিলেন যে তিনি প্রথম শৃঙ্খলা বার্তাটি পেয়ে হতবাক হয়েছিলেন।
bangla_paragraph3: এখনও শক এবং অনিশ্চয়তার মধ্যে থাকা সত্ত্বেও, আমি স্বীকৃতি দিয়েছি যে আমার কোনও বিলম্ব ছাড়াই আপসটি রিপোর্ট করার দায়িত্ব ছিল, তিনি লিখেছেন। উপরন্তু, তিনি বলেছিলেন যে তিনি  ঘটনার জন্য গভীরভাবে দুঃখিত এবং যোগ করেছেন যে ব্রিটিশ সেনাবাহিনীতে সেবা করা আমার জীবনের অন্যতম বৃহত্তম সুযোগ ছিল। বার্টন-কেনেডি এই শাস্তি আপিল করেছিলেন, যা ২০২৬ সালের আগস্টে প্রত্যাখ্যান করা হয়েছিল।
bangla_paragraph4: মন্তব্যের জন্য একটি জিজ্ঞাসাবাদের জবাবে, ব্রিটিশ সেনাবাহিনীর মুখপাত্র লেফটেন্যান্ট কর্নেল ইপি ম্যাককি একটি বিবৃতিতে আর্সকে বলেন যে, আরোপিত নিরাপত্তা ব্যবস্থাগুলি সামরিক কর্মীদের নিরাপত্তা রক্ষা করার উদ্দেশ্যে।
bangla_paragraph5: তিনি লিখেছেন, সেনাবাহিনীর নিরাপত্তা ব্যবস্থা লঙ্ঘন করলে যা ব্যক্তিগত সুরক্ষা বা অপারেশনাল নিরাপত্তা নিয়ে হুমকি সৃষ্টি করতে পারে তা দ্রুত মোকাবিলা করা হবে এবং অপরাধী কর্মীরা আপসহীন শৃঙ্খলা ব্যবস্থা প্রত্যাশা করতে পারেন।

title: US FAA to eliminate floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028
title_bn: ২০২৮ সালের মধ্যে এয়ার ট্রাফিক কন্ট্রোল থেকে ফ্লপি ডিস্ক বাদ দিতে যাচ্ছে মার্কিন এফএএ।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The US federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is finally moving to retire floppy disks from its air traffic control infrastructure, with plans to to replace four decades-old information systems across 435 facilities by the end of 2028.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) The US federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is finally moving to retire floppy disks from its air traffic control infrastructure, with plans to replace four decades-old information systems across 435 facilities by the end of 2028. The agency announced the rollout on November 5, introducing a centralized platform that will give controllers faster access to weather reports, flight alerts and other operational information. “We’re moving away from outdated, manual processes and replacing technology that once relied on floppy disks with a modern system that allows controllers to instantly share critical flight alerts, restricted airspace schedules and pilot reports,” FAA administrator Bryan Bedford said, adding the agency wants to make critical information available more quickly across its networks.
paragraph2: Notably, the new Enterprise Information Display System (E-IDS) is designed to replace four legacy systems dating back to the 1980s. Rather than relying on separate information displays and manual processes, controllers will get a centralized view of operational updates, equipment problems, weather disruptions, and aviation advisories. The first five locations receiving E-IDS include Atlantic City International Airport, Nashville International Airport, Greater Rochester International Airport, and FAA data processing hubs in Atlanta and Salt Lake City, although the system could be extended to 453 sites by the end of 2028.

bangla_paragraph2: উল্লেখযোগ্যভাবে, নতুন এন্টারপ্রাইজ ইনফরমেশন ডিসপ্লে সিস্টেম (ই-আইডিএস) ১৯৮০ এর দশকের চারটি পুরানো সিস্টেমের প্রতিস্থাপনের জন্য ডিজাইন করা হয়েছে। পৃথক তথ্য প্রদর্শন এবং ম্যানুয়াল প্রক্রিয়াগুলির উপর নির্ভর করার পরিবর্তে, নিয়ামকরা অপারেশনাল আপডেট, সরঞ্জাম সমস্যা, আবহাওয়া ব্যাঘাত এবং বিমানের পরামর্শের কেন্দ্রীয় দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি পাবেন। প্রথম পাঁচটি অবস্থানে ই-আইডএস গ্রহণকারী আটলান্টিক সিটি আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দর, নাশভিল আন্তর্জাতিক বিমান বন্দর, গ্রেটার রোচেস্টার আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানਬন্দর এবং
bangla_paragraph3: টম হার্ডওয়্যারের সেরা সংবাদ এবং গভীর পর্যালোচনাগুলি সরাসরি আপনার ইনবক্সে পান। নিউটন গিটোঙ্গা হলেন একজন প্রযুক্তি সাংবাদিক যিনি গ্যাজেট, পিসি হার্ডওয়ার, এআই, ডেটা সেন্টার এবং আরও বিস্তৃত প্রযুক্তি শিল্পকে কভার করেন। প্রযুক্তিতে তাঁর আগ্রহ খুব তাড়াতাড়ি শুরু হয়েছিল, কীভাবে তারা কাজ করেছিল তা দেখতে বাড়ির চারপাশের জিনিসগুলি ভেঙে ফেলা, প্রায়শই তার বাবার হতাশায়।
bangla_paragraph4: তার কৌতূহল কখনও কখনও তাকে আরও ভাল করে তুলেছিল, ল্যাপটপগুলি ঠিক করার কয়েকটি ব্যর্থ প্রচেষ্টা সহ, তাদের মধ্যে একটি ছিল একটি প্রতিভাধর ডেল এক্সপিএস। তিনি পূর্বে নোটবুকচেক, জাইক্রিপ্টো, কয়েনসেন্ট্রাল এবং ক্রিপ্টা নিউজ ফ্ল্যাশের জন্য লিখেছেন।

title: India on right track in AI; firms moving from pilots to production: Oracles Kumar
title_bn: India on right track in AI; firms moving from pilots to production: Oracles Kumar
author: TechPulse
excerpt: India on right track in AI; firms moving from pilots to production: Oracle's Kumar
paragraph1: Las Vegas, Nov 7 (PTI) Indian businesses have moved from testing artificial intelligence in pilot projects to deploying it at full scale over the past year or so and are seeing real benefits, though cost, skills and infrastructure pose some challenges, Oracle India head Shailender Kumar has said."Around a year and a half back, we were talking about pilots. Now, we are seeing full-scale productions and the productions where the benefits are very, very real," Kumar, Senior Vice President and regional Managing Director, Oracle India and NetSuite JAPAC, told PTI on the sidelines of Oracle AI World 2026.Indian companies are not wary of new technology but want proof that it works, he said."What they want to see is what will come to them: whether they save time, cost or anything else.
paragraph2: Years back, there were a lot of reservations because people were not sure in terms of security, in terms of performance," he said, noting that once tangible benefits become visible, Indian enterprises swiftly move to adopt the technology.Asked what could slow AI adoption in India, he said cost is "certainly one of them".On skills, he said Oracle was working with universities, colleges and state governments to train students, including at industrial training institutes (ITIs) and polytechnics.Infrastructure "is a challenge", he said, but it is being addressed as new data centres come up in the country."People are willing to take the plunge as long as they see the benefit," he said.
paragraph3: On where the line should fall between decisions made by AI and those made by people, Kumar said, "When talking about AI, governance is the most important part".Organisations need people who can evaluate whether AI is producing the right outcomes and being used the way it was intended, he said.Beyond companies' own governance, Kumar said regulation would also evolve."In terms of regulation, yes, there will be changes. We will see things building up as the industry also matures," he said, pointing to incidents of AI models going rogue.
paragraph4: Oracle, which has been in India for 33 years and is present in more than 15 cities, has grown at a double-digit rate in the country for about 10 years, Kumar said.Banking is the company's biggest sector in India, followed by the public sector, he said, adding that all four of India's telecom operators use Oracle.Over the next three to five years, Kumar said his priority was faster growth."I want to ensure that the business grows faster than what it's growing today because the market has that potential," he said."India is on a very, very right track," he said."
paragraph5: There are a few things that we cannot control; the geopolitical things keep happening. But otherwise, from a country's standpoint, we are very well placed."

title: Data centre bosses cash in on India's AI and cloud expansion with handsome pay packages
title_bn: Data centre bosses cash in on India's AI and cloud expansion with handsome pay packages
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Higher revenues and massive capacity ramp-ups push executive compensation past the multi-crore mark.
paragraph1: India’s $5.5 billion data centre industry enters its biggest expansion phase yet.(AFP)SummaryHigher revenues and massive capacity ramp-ups push executive compensation past the multi-crore mark.Mumbai/Bengaluru: It’s boom time for data centres in India and their chief executive officers. Financials reported by India’s top data centres reviewed by Mint show that as they raked in higher revenue, their chiefs were handsomely rewarded.Manoj Paul, managing director of the Indian operations of Redwood City, California-based data-centre company Equinix, emerged as the top earner, taking home ₹5.91 crore in annual pay, although this was down 13% from FY24.While Equinix did not disclose if Paul’s salary was tweaked because of equity-linked payouts, it coincided with the company reporting its slowest annual revenue growth since Paul took charge in September 2021.Ashish Arora, CEO of Nxtra by Airtel, saw his remuneration rise largely in line with the company’s annual growth in earnings. Since joining in August 2022, Arora’s salary has increased at a compounded annualized growth rate of nearly 10% over four years to ₹3.1 crore in August 2026.
paragraph2: Nxtra’s revenue grew at a CAGR of 15% to ₹2,434 crore over this period.Piyush Somani, chairman and managing director of ESDS Software Solution, saw his net pay more than double from ₹83.8 lakh in FY24 to ₹1.8 crore in FY26, comfortably outstripping his firm’s 65% revenue growth to ₹472.2 crore over the same period.As India’s $5.5 billion data centre industry enters its biggest expansion phase yet, driven by demand from cloud companies and artificial intelligence (AI) businesses, executives leading the charge are winning a premium to manage these large projects, negotiate with global technology companies and deliver on time.Indian business houses, standalone operators and Big Tech companies have committed cumulative investments over $250 billion over the past 12 months to build data centres and AI infrastructure.Stock optionsSome executives are also being rewarded with equities. Nxtra’s Arora was granted 6,186 stock options in FY25, according to the company’s FY25 annual report. The filing did not establish their eventual cash value.
paragraph3: ESDS’s Somani, who is also the founder of the Nashik-based data centre company, holds about a fifth of its shares. The company commanded a market capitalization of over ₹13,000 crore on Friday. ESDS is eyeing $5 billion revenue in five years, Mint reported on 21 October.“Remuneration is linked to how a data centre company performs,” said Amit Chandra, vice president at HDFC Securities. “In a high-growth industry such as data centres, growth must not be an issue. Seems like bosses are paid based on execution and ensuring capacity goes live on time even as demand skyrockets. The faster the capacity that can go live, the better the pay, it seems.”Four companies – Yotta Data Services, NTT India, STT Global Data Centres and CtrlS Datacenters – did not disclose individual salaries or equity grants awarded to their top executives.For three other data centre companies – AdaniConneX, TCS HyperVault and Sify Infinit Spaces – Mint could not ascertain how the salaries of their top executives increased. The latest available pay packages, however, all exceed ₹1 crore – AdaniConneX’s Samir Vora earned ₹1 crore in FY26 and HyperVault’s Deepesh Nanda earned ₹1.6 crore in FY26.
paragraph4: Sify’s Sharad Agarwal earned ₹1.8 crore in FY25. Sify has not disclosed the salaries in its FY26 annual report.For now, the data centres are in the building and expansion phases.Ctrl S Data Centres and Sify Infinit Spaces declined to comment. Mint’s emails to the other eight companies seeking details of their pay packages and related expansion plans, did not receive responses until publishing time.IT executivesWhile the incomes of data centre chiefs jumped, their salaries remain significantly lower than those of the top executives of India’s IT services industry. Mint research showed that the salaries of the 10 largest tech outsourcers’ bosses ranged from ₹27 crore to ₹390 crore as of FY26, with a majority of the pay from stock options.“IT services firms are way bigger than data centres and the responsibility of managing them is much higher than data centres, which explains fatter paychecks to IT firms’ heads,” said Kunal Bajaj, an equity research analyst at Choice Institutional Equities.Bajaj, however, added that the gap is expected “to narrow, as most of these data centre operators are growing at double-digits, so the quantum of their heads’ salaries will also increase.”About the AuthorJas BardiaJas Bardia is a Bengaluru-based business journalist covering India’s information technology (IT) services sector and Global Capability Centres (GCCs).

title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
title_bn: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
paragraph1: Crusoe, an eight-year-old, Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion, confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe’s management. Crusoe initially announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity. Google did not disclose how much it paid Crusoe for the unfinished project, bu it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus.
paragraph2: The deal highlights how difficult it can be for independent data center developers to deliver massive projects on time and within budget, given the challenges of securing equipment and power. Growing opposition from local communities can further complicate development. Despite taking over the Wyoming facility, Google hasn’t walked away from working with Crusoe entirely. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. The deal to sell the site to Google was first reported by Bloomberg in June, but the Wyoming setback didn’t stop Crusoe from raising a $3.
paragraph3: 9 billion round in September. Crusoe makes money by leasing data center space to customers that bring their own GPUs, by renting out its own GPUs, and by selling compute power used to run AI models, known as inference. Crusoe’s largest projects serve some of the biggest names in AI. Its campus in Abilene, Texas, is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI, and the company is also constructing a separate 900-megawatt campus next door for Microsoft, with its first building expected to come online in mid-2027. Meta is also a customer, and Bloomberg reported that the trading firm Jane Street signed a $13 billion, five-year cloud deal with Crusoe.
paragraph4: Crusoe was founded by Chase Lochmiller, now its CEO, and Cully Cavness, who started it as a cryptocurrency-mining business powered by natural gas that would otherwise have been burned off. In September, alongside its $3.9 billion funding round, the company added three board members, including JB Straubel, the Redwood Materials founder and Tesla board member who invested in Crusoe in 2021. Crusoe later became the first customer of Straubel’s energy-storage business. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission.

title: OYO Parent PRISM’s Profit Jumps 17% YoY To ₹353 Cr In Q1
title_bn: OYO Parent PRISM’s Profit Jumps 17% YoY To ₹353 Cr In Q1
author: TechPulse
excerpt: IPO-bound hospitality chain PRISM, the parent entity of OYO, reported a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹353 Cr in…
paragraph1: SUMMARYPRISM’s revenue from operations zoomed 35% to ₹2,814 Cr in Q1 FY27 as against ₹2,078 Cr reported in the year ago quarter The profitability came largely on the back of a deferred tax credit of nearly ₹244 Cr in the quarter under review and a sharp growth in the top line The numbers come as PRISM is gearing up to list on the bourses. The startup has already filed its UDRHP with SEBI for a ₹6,650 Cr IPO, which will consist entirely of a fresh issue of shares IPO-bound hospitality chain PRISM, the parent entity of OYO, reported a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹353 Cr in the first quarter (Q1) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), up 17.3% from ₹301 Cr in the year-ago period. According to PRISM’s audited financials seen by Inc42, the profitability came largely on the back of a deferred tax credit of nearly ₹244 Cr in the quarter under review. Nevertheless, PRISM continued to grow its top line and generated an operating revenue of ₹2,814 Cr in Q1 FY27.
paragraph2: This was nearly 35% higher than ₹2,078 Cr reported in the year ago quarter. The IPO-bound startup also managed to improve its EBITDA by 24.3% to ₹760 Cr in the quarter under review as against ₹611 Cr in Q1 FY26. On the operational front, PRISM’s gross booking value (GBV) stood at nearly ₹9,600 Cr in the quarter ended June 2026, up nearly 30% from ₹7,408 Cr in Q1 FY26. This is largely in line with what PRISM founder and CEO Ritesh Agarwal had said during the company’s extraordinary general meeting (EGM) in October this year.
paragraph3: “Our performance (in Q1 FY27) across segments on hotels or on vacation homes has demonstrated improving gross margins, higher operating earnings, even as we invest in expanding our brands and strengthening customer demand,” Agarwal had said then. During the EGM, Agarwal also attributed PRISM’s performance to investments made in technology, brands and distribution capabilities over the past few years. Founded in 2012 by Agarwal, OYO initially operated a budget hotel chain. title: Hands-On With Apple's New OLED Touchscreen MacBook Pro
title_bn: Hands-On With Apple's New OLED Touchscreen MacBook Pro
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Happy touch your Mac day! Apple's new PROLED MacBook Pro is now in the hands of customers. We picked up one of the new machines to get our greasy fingerprints all over that pristine OLED display. Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more vi
paragraph1: Friday November 6, 2026 2:05 pm PST by Juli CloverHappy touch your Mac day! Apple's new PROLED MacBook Pro is now in the hands of customers. We picked up one of the new machines to get our greasy fingerprints all over that pristine OLED display. It's been five years since Apple last redesigned the ‌MacBook Pro‌, so it was due for an update. The PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ looks a lot like the mini-LED model, but it's thinner and lighter. The 14-inch model is about half a millimeter thinner and weighs just over three pounds, while the 16-inch model is almost a millimeter thinner and weighs four pounds. Apple shaved off about half a pound for the 14-inch model and 0.7 pounds for the 16-inch model, and while that doesn't sound like much, it makes a big difference. You can feel how much lighter it is the second you take it out of the box.
paragraph2: Apple brought back the glowing logo for the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌, so everyone around you will know you have the fancy new ‌OLED‌ model. The ‌OLED‌ display is the major new feature, and it looks as good as you would expect from a display in a laptop starting at $2,899. Blacks are true black, and since each pixel lights up individually, there's none of the bloom you get with mini-LED when viewing bright objects on a dark background. The PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ can get super bright too, and that brightness paired with the deep blacks, HDR content looks great. ‌OLED‌ sometimes isn't bright enough outdoors, but that's not the case here. The display bezels are thinner, and the 16-inch machine is actually 16.3 inches instead of 16.2. There's also an iPhone-like Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and houses Siri AI, Live Activities, and more.
paragraph3: The ‌Dynamic Island‌ makes sense because you can now touch the ‌MacBook Pro‌'s display. It works like touching an iPhone or iPad, so you can swipe through webpages, tap buttons, drag and drop, and pinch to zoom. Touch isn't meant to replace the trackpad and keyboard, but it's there if you want it. Apple made some tweaks to macOS, so menu options expand a little more when you touch them than when you click them, and tiny window resizing buttons get larger. Apple put a sturdier hinge in the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ so the display won't move as much when you tap it, but it's not perfect. It does still jiggle depending on where you tap. The touch feature is fine, but it's probably not a reason to go out and get the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌. It has the potential to be useful in some situations, but it's not going to dramatically change the way most people use a laptop. New chips weren't ready in time for the PROLED machines, so they use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max as the mini-LED models.
paragraph4: That's a disappointment in a laptop that starts at almost $3,000. Since Apple is still selling the mini-LED models, you're basically paying a $400 premium for the higher-end ‌OLED‌ display, the thinner and lighter design, and the touch functionality. The better display and the lighter weight are going to be worth the price for some people, and the touch is just a bonus. title: More Fun iPhone Duo Apps: 30 New Picks to Try
title_bn: More Fun iPhone Duo Apps: 30 New Picks to Try
author: TechPulse
excerpt: When the iPhone Duo launched, we shared a list of some of the fun apps developers created for the new form factor. Two weeks out, developers are continuing to come up with fresh ideas, so we thought we'd share some of our favorites. Games Marbles Unh
paragraph1: Friday November 6, 2026 3:27 pm PST by Juli CloverWhen the iPhone Duo launched, we shared a list of some of the fun apps developers created for the new form factor. Two weeks out, developers are continuing to come up with fresh ideas, so we thought we'd share some of our favorites. Games Marbles Unhinged ($2.99) - Marbles Unhinged is a marble maze designed for the Duo. When you fold it, the floor turns into a ramp. If you stand the top half up, you can bank a marble off of it. When you snap the hinge, the marble launches up. Midnight Fridge ($2.99) - Midnight Fridge turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a tiny refrigerator. It's a memory game where the idea is to look at the magnets on the fridge and then find the items inside. Greens: Mini Golf ($2.99) - Greens is a mini-golf app made for the ‌iPhone Duo‌, and it's playable in any orientation. When folded like a laptop, you can putt on the half on the table, with the upright half serving as a caddie camera. Chirpfold (Free) - Chirpfold is a Flappy Bird-style app where you fold the phone to cause your bird to flap its wings. Valley Run ($0.99) - Valley Run is a neon-themed racing game where you fold the ‌iPhone Duo‌ to direct a marble down a series of challenging tracks. PianoFold ($4.99) - PianoFold is a rhythm game you can play with the ‌iPhone Duo‌ positioned like a laptop. Press and hold on the keys to match the song that's playing. It's free to download, but the full unlock is $4.99.
paragraph2: Load Bearing ($5.00) - Load Bearing is a roguelite Tetris-style game that's meant to be played with the Duo half open. The controls are on the bottom, and the blocks fall at the top. It also has deck building elements, so you can put together a set of your preferred block pieces to beat each level. Who's at the Door? (Free) - Who's at the Door? is an app that turns your ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a door. Open it up to see who is on the other side, and if it's something scary, make sure to slam the Duo shut quickly before it gets you. Fold Match ($2.99) - Fold Match is a game where you're given a shape on one side of the Duo and a blank spot where the shape needs to go on the other side. The idea is to position the shape to get to that empty space, but you won't know how close you were until you close the iPhone. Battlefleet Duo (Free) - Battlefleet Duo takes advantage of the Duo's design for a Battleship-style game. In laptop mode, you can see your fleet on the lower screen and the enemy's waters in front of you. Simple But Clever Duo Aquarium ($1.00) - As the name suggests, this app turns your ‌iPhone Duo‌ into an aquarium. When in tent mode, it serves as a virtual fish tank and clock. You can choose your fish and your add-ins, then feed them. AltoPaint ($5.99) - AltoPaint is an app that turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a tiny canvas with a paint palette. There are watercolor, oil, and gouache paints with mixable colors. Post Club ($4.
paragraph3: 99) - Post Club is a cute app where you can pick a typewriter, fold the Duo like a laptop and type up a letter. There are 10 typewriters and 14 paper styles to choose from. Halfpage ($2.99) - Halfpage is another app that turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a typewriter when it's used in a MacBook-like orientation. The keys are at the bottom, and what you type is at the top. It has a simpler design than Post Club. Callsign ($1.49+) - Callsign turns your ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a sign that lets people know if you're free or busy on a call. Just set it up, put it in tent mode, and people can know at a glance not to bother you. It's free to download, and there are different visual packs to unlock with one-off $1.49 purchases. AskZine ($1.99) - AskZine is a Magic 8 Ball-like app where you ask a question, unfold the screen, and see your answer. Lullabox (Free) - Lullabox turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a music box where you can wind the key, lift the lid, and watch a porcelain ballerina spin while soft music plays. The music gets louder as the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is opened further. DuoBook (Free) - DuoBook turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a tiny Mac with a keyboard and trackpad that work like the Mac equivalent. You can also use it to send photos and files to the Mac. Special Duo Features Wakeout ($59.99/year) - Fitness app Wakeout was Apple's App of the Year back in 2020. It offers up workout games you can do in just minutes a day. You can put your Duo in tent or laptop mode to follow along with workout moves, playing games with your body.
paragraph4: Faro (Free) - Faro is an app that helps you find movies to watch so you don't waste time browsing through Netflix without ever making a choice. On ‌iPhone Duo‌, you can see two films side by side to choose between them, or see your list of picks on one half of the display with details on each movie on the other half. CalibReader (Free) - CalibReader is an EPUB and PDF reader that turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a book. The outer screen shows the title's cover, and when you open it, there's a two-page spread with page-turning animations. Retrocade (Apple Arcade) - Retrocade turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a mini arcade machine and works on the Duo in multiple fold positions. Blankie (Free) - Soundscape app Blankie has a dual view with Now Playing on one side and Sound Mixer on the other. When folded in tent mode, it shows a view of what's playing. Camera Apps IncrediBooth (Free) - IncrediBooth turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a little photo booth. Press the red button to capture an image, and your photo strip appears on the outer display. It's free to download, with five strips available per day. VNTG (Free) - VNTG is an instant camera app where you close the ‌iPhone Duo‌ to take a shot and then open it up to develop it. It's free to download, with in-app purchases to unlock camera lenses. Flipcorder ($4.99) - Flipcorder is a video recording app that turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a retro camcorder. It's designed to be used for daily video diaries, and each tape is displayed on a shelf in the app. To film, just unfold the Duo. Recordings have classic VHS-style effects. Less Fun, More Serious Brim ($0.89) - Brim is a Safari extension that lets Safari use the full width of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s outer display for websites. It reclaims the blank space Apple left in Safari and moves links and buttons out from under the side controls. Widen ($3.
paragraph5: 99) - Widen is another extension that expands Safari to take up the width of the outer display. It also hides cookie banners and works in Split View. There are multiple settings, so you can set just pictures to take up the full screen, or opt to have pictures and text expand. SPAN (Free) - SPAN is an app that turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a project tracker and timer. It has different views for each ‌iPhone Duo‌ orientation. SPAN is free to use for the current week, with a $4.99/month pro subscription available for unlimited projects and full monthly and yearly reports. BrainDrain (Free) - BrainDrain is a 60-second brain dump app that helps you sort your thoughts. On the ‌iPhone Duo‌, different Duo orientations have different purposes. You can use it like a laptop in a half fold, type thoughts with the Duo closed, or put it in tent mode to use voice capture. More Apps Know of some fun ‌iPhone Duo‌ apps not on our list? Let us know in the comments. Be sure to check out our first iPhone Duo app article too. Camera Apps IncrediBooth (Free) - IncrediBooth turns the ‌iPhone Duo‌ into a little photo booth. Press the red button to capture an image, and your photo strip appears on the outer display. title: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
title_bn: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
author: TechPulse
excerpt: It's the exact path, not the apparent severity that matters most, doctors say.
paragraph1: The man then moved to intensive care, where he recovered rapidly. A day after surgery, doctors were able to remove his breathing tube. He developed some minor right-side weakness, but it resolved two days later. Scans of his brain showed steady improvement—a little bleeding and swelling, and there was some air in his brain tissue from where the knife had been. But otherwise, it appeared to be healing. He developed no infections and had no seizures.
paragraph2: (A–D) Postoperative axial CT images demonstrating expected changes along the surgical tract, including intracranial air, minor hemorrhage and oedema extending toward the inner table of the left temporal bone. There is oedema adjacent to the anterior limb of the left internal capsule, correlating with the patient’s transient postoperative right-sided weakness. (A–D) Postoperative axial CT images demonstrating expected changes along the surgical tract, including intracranial air, minor hemorrhage and oedema extending toward the inner table of the left temporal bone. There is oedema adjacent to the anterior limb of the left internal capsule, correlating with the patient’s transient postoperative right-sided weakness. Credit: BMJ Case Reports, 2026 Despite the “dramatic intracranial trajectory,” his language function was preserved, and he had no loss of movement or coordination, they reported. He was discharged from the hospital and at follow-up appointments remained “neurologically well,” with ongoing eye and mental health care.
paragraph3: Lucky recovery As for how the injury happened, his doctors still don’t know. “The mechanism is unclear,” they wrote. However, they noted he had a history of depression. The doctors reflected on how lucky the man was to have survived and to have such a full recovery. Such injuries that go through the eye and the brain are rare. When they do occur, they’re usually from “high-velocity mechanisms” such as gunshots or other ballistic injuries.
paragraph4: Knives, rods, and nails fit into the rarer “low-velocity mechanisms. “Such “low-velocity penetrating brain injuries carry substantial morbidity and mortality because of hemorrhage, vascular injury, abscess, meningitis, cerebrospinal fluid leak, seizures and neurological deficit,” they wrote. But such fortunate recoveries aren’t unheard of; they cited reports of other remarkably unexpected recoveries from seemingly devastating brain injuries. That includes the famous case of Phineas Gage, a railroad foreman who survived an 1848 accident that sent a large iron rod directly through his head. The rod entered below his left cheekbone and exited the top of his skull. (Although he survived and recovered, Gage’s personality was said to have changed after the accident.
paragraph5: The doctors in the knife-wound case did not mention any such personality changes.) “Echoing classic and contemporary examples of severe frontal lobe penetration with unexpectedly preserved neurological function, including Phineas Gage and a reported nail-gun injury, this case highlights that outcome may depend less on external severity than on precise trajectory relative to critical vascular, cortical and subcortical structures,” the doctors concluded.

title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
title_bn: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
author: TechPulse
excerpt: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks.
paragraph1: In Brief Posted: 2:53 PM PST · November 6, 2026 Image Credits:Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto / Getty Images OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion. Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet.
paragraph2: The round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg. In late September, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion in the upcoming round. The current figures fall well short of that target. TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment and will update this story if it responds.
paragraph3: The news comes only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the IPO of OpenAI’s chief competitor, Anthropic, are eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted. Bloomberg writes that some potential buyers believe Anthropic’s valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion that investors were said to be expecting roughly a month ago. OpenAI previously intimated that it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans.
paragraph4: There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point. The market for AI hangs in a particularly precarious place. The Democratic landslide in the U.S.
paragraph5: midterms — and overwhelmingly negative voter sentiment around data centers — has caused jitters throughout the market, with many anticipating potential regulatory challenges in the future.

title: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
title_bn: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
author: TechPulse
excerpt: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network
paragraph1: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth.As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm, which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile, potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network.SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. Tim Höttges, the CEO of T-Mobile’s parent company Deutsche Telekom, said he takes SpaceX’s plans “super serious” but that it could cost Musk more than $200 billion to pull off.
paragraph2: Follow along for the latest updates on Starlink’s major mobile carrier ambitions.PinnedSpaceX’s ambitious, pricey gamble to replace AT&T and VerizonToday, I’m talking with Walter Piecyk, a partner and analyst at LightShed Partners who covers tech, media, and telecom, about SpaceX’s recently announced plan to become a major wireless carrier.Last week, SpaceX agreed to buy a big chunk of low-band spectrum to expand the Starlink network, spectrum that’s been traded around the telecom business for decades now. SpaceX’s ambitious plan is to use that spectrum to help build “the world’s most advanced mobile network.”Read Article >What will it take for SpaceX to launch its “major” mobile network?Bloomberg has a breakdown of how Starlink Mobile will operate — and what SpaceX still needs to do to get its hybrid 5G network up and running.SpaceX is working with Qualcomm to build its Starlink Mobile 5G networkImage: QualcommSpaceX could buy Boost Mobile as part of its big mobile carrier plansImage: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty ImagesSpaceX has discussed a deal with Boost Mobile to launch its own service through the budget-friendly carrier, according to a report from The Washington Post.
paragraph3: The deal, which comes as SpaceX aims to make Starlink a “major” mobile carrier, reportedly involves the Elon Musk-owned company acquiring Boost Mobile or accessing its network.Musk discussed the potential agreement with Charlie Ergen, chairman of Boost Mobile parent company EchoStar, last month, as reported by The Washington Post. Boost Mobile’s network is currently powered by T-Mobile and AT&T, meaning SpaceX may need permission from the two carriers to launch its service.Read Article >SpaceX’s mobile carrier push reportedly involves tapping into 80,000 cell sitesPhoto: George Frey / AFP via Getty ImagesSpaceX plans to access at least 80,000 cell sites as part of efforts to compete directly with Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T, according to a report from Bloomberg. Sources tell the publication that SpaceX is in talks with Crown Castle Inc., one of the nation’s largest cell tower owners.The move would give SpaceX access to half of the 158,500 cell towers currently operational in the US, according to Reuters.
paragraph4: When asked about a potential partnership with SpaceX, Amazon, or other satellite services during an earnings call on Wednesday, Crown Castle CEO Chris Hillabrant said, “I don’t think I want to get into customer-specific detail, but you can assume that we’re talking to all parties.” SpaceX plans to pair a network of cell towers with its constellation of direct-to-cell satellites.Read Article >SpaceX announces plan to become a ‘major mobile carrier’Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty ImagesSpaceX has acquired a portfolio of low-band spectrum licenses — a move the company says “will pave the way” for its Starlink Mobile service to become a “major” US carrier. When the Federal Communications Commission signs off on the deal, SpaceX says it will deploy its new architecture that combines its satellite-to-mobile constellation with a terrestrial mobile network, directly competing with T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.The licenses include up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, which SpaceX says will allow Starlink Mobile’s signal to penetrate through walls and buildings. SpaceX previously acquired 2GHz spectrum from EchoStar as part of efforts to bolster its direct-to-device service.Read Article >SpaceX is coming for T-Mobile, AT&T and VerizonImage: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty ImagesSpaceX is preparing to build a terrestrial mobile network to “acquire quite a few” of the customers now subscribed to T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.
paragraph5: The message to compete head-to-head with the US carriers was delivered by SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell and CEO Elon Musk during the Q&A section of the company’s first earnings call.“The spectrum that we purchased from EchoStar does have terrestrial components, so we definitely intend to build out the terrestrial component,” said Shotwell. “You will have not only the capacity from the satellites themselves, but you will have a buildout of the terrestrial, basically the hardware and systems necessary to make a true mobile service exactly what you want it to be.

excerpt: There are now 100,000 Duo-optimized apps, says Apple, and thousands more arrive daily.
paragraph1: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch. But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front. The company on Friday announced there are now over 100,000 apps built for the Duo live on the App Store, and it’s seeing thousands more being added to the store every day. The news was timed alongside the release of over a dozen more notable Duo-ready apps, including Microsoft Word and Outlook, Zoom, sports apps from the NBA and NHL, shopping apps like Etsy and LTK, productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra, the Halide Mark III camera app, and others. These join the iPhone Duo-optimized apps that were already available, like Netflix, YouTube, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Non-optimized apps are definitely less than ideal, as they come with a black bar on the side of the screen, which takes up valuable space. Sometimes, they hide important functions under an overflow menu.
paragraph2: Apple’s data seems to suggest that at least some iOS developers may have needed extra time to get their apps ready for its latest form factor. The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide. Here, the developers could use the Duo and work on their apps with Apple’s support. The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year. On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve.
paragraph3: “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added. Other notable apps that have been updated for iOS 27 and optimized for the iPhone Duo include the following: Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (U.K.), Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada), Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot, Excel, PowerPoint, SAP Concur, monday.com, PDF Expert, Documents, iA Writer, Substack, The Washington Post, Yahoo News, FOX News, Kalshi, Yahoo Finance, Canva, Suno, Tinder, Google Translate, Strava, Alma, Withings, MyFitnessPal, Bevel, Transit, Citi Bike, ParkMobile, Viator, Tesla Robotaxi, Priceline, Kroger, Domino’s, Taco Bell, Untappd, The Weather Channel, FOX Weather, and RainViewer. Not all these updates have yet to fully roll out, we should note.
paragraph4: Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo. However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
title_bn: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Explaining the Great Unconformity, where Cambrian deposits sit on top of older rocks.
paragraph1: Old and new Explaining the Great Unconformity, where Cambrian deposits sit on top of older rocks. The Great Unconformity between red sedimentary deposits and earlier rocks is very apparent at this site in Colorado. Credit: Marli Miller In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. “This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth’s mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet’s interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. The leading explanation was glaciation. Between roughly 720 and 635 million years ago, glaciers reached the tropics, and some scientists think the entire planet froze over, a scenario called Snowball Earth.
paragraph2: “Ice sheets are very good at grinding, scouring, scraping the surface,” Flament explains. He said that glaciers are about 10 times more effective than rivers at eroding rock away. But if the whole planet froze, the Great Unconformity should be found everywhere. And it’s not. Other explanations included rifting, pulling and stretching of Earth’s crust, and a global drop in sea levels. But rifting acts mostly on the edges of continents, and a sea level change should have affected all continents alike. “There’s no doubt that there was extensive glaciation. There’s no doubt that there have been sea-level changes throughout time. The question is, was that enough to put the Great Unconformity puzzle together?” Flament says. A fourth idea held that the mantle itself was moving continents up and down, a process called dynamic topography. “It had been proposed, but it hadn’t been quantitatively tested,” Flament says. So, his team set out to do so. Lava lamp planet From roughly 100 to 200 kilometers beneath the surface down to nearly 3,000 kilometers, Earth’s mantle slowly convects.
paragraph3: “An analogy would be a lava lamp, where some stuff comes up and some stuff comes down,” Flament explains. “Cold rock sinks and hot rock rises.” The mantle is solid, yet a piece of rock can slowly travel from the surface to the deep Earth over some 200 million years. That motion tugs on the surface. Where cold slabs of ocean floor sink into the mantle at subduction zones, the ground gets pulled down; where hot mantle rises, it gets pushed up. The amplitude of this up and down motion is still debated, though. “The short of it is several hundreds of meters, and it’s still to be worked out exactly what that [precise value] is,” Flament says. Dhungana and Flament ran six simulations of mantle convection going back 1 billion years, driven by reconstructions of how tectonic plates moved over that time. Then they grouped regions where the ground rose and fell in similar ways to find where the unconformity should have formed, and where it should have survived to the present. Flament, however, says the starting configuration of these simulations remains uncertain. Magnetic records in ancient rocks reveal how far continents were from the equator, but not their longitude. “It’s possible that some continents may be in the wrong hemisphere,” Flament admits. The ancient ocean floor, long since recycled into the mantle, had to be invented entirely from scratch in the models. Still, the simulations produced a consistent story.
paragraph4: Laurentia, the ancient core of North America, had little or no subduction along its margins between about 930 and 510 million years ago, much like Africa today, so it sat above some rising mantle and was pushed up. Five of the six models showed this pattern of Laurentia seeing long uplift followed by sinking in the Cambrian. For northern Europe and North China, this pattern showed up in four. But the uplift alone, Flament’s team concluded, was too gentle to strip away enough rock to create the Great Unconformity. Glacial grind “The uplift could create a tilt for the whole continent, but it’s not great at creating a steep slope,” Flament says. The missing piece of the puzzle, he argues, were glaciers that ground through rock even on low ground and gentle slopes. The models show the uplift was still building when Snowball Earth hit. “This gentle uplift that’s continuous, and then that glacial erosion that comes on top, work together,” Flament explains. “They’re not coupled. They just happen to coincide in time.” When the continents sank in the Cambrian, seas flooded in and buried the eroded surface. The models made by Flament’s team also explain why the gap is so obvious in North America but hard to find elsewhere. Compared with records of sediment preserved on each continent, North America and Eurasia show one long rise followed by one long fall, which the researchers interpret as the ideal recipe for the Great Unconformity. South America and Australia, on the other hand, went through two cycles.
paragraph5: “This would form potentially two unconformities, and then the Great Unconformity would be more difficult to see,” Flament says. Africa was a different case altogether—hemmed in by mountain belts at the time, its erosion and sediment were shaped by the mountains rather than by the mantle beneath. But if the mantle goes through such up and down cycles on a regular basis, the remaining question was why we can see only one Great Unconformity, and not many. One of a kind The team says the Great Unconformity is unique in the geological record because of a combination of a rise-and-fall cycle lasting over 900 million years, a near-global glaciation that happened at the right moment, and rock records that get harder to read farther back in time. Flament suspects there may be an older candidate, tied to a glaciation 2.4 billion years ago, but rocks that old lack the fossils that make younger sediments easier to date. “Having life in sediments makes it a lot easier to have a sense of time,” he says. His work, however, may help explain what happens right after the Great Unconformity formed. The intense erosion that carved the Great Unconformity washed rock material into the oceans, possibly fertilizing them just before the Cambrian explosion, when calcium became abundant in seawater. “That’s when life learns to mobilize calcium and create skeletons and shells,” Flament says. He admits, though, that mantle dynamics likely wasn’t the only process that enabled the Cambrian explosion.

title: Control the Glowing Apple Logo on Your New MacBook Pro
title_bn: Control the Glowing Apple Logo on Your New MacBook Pro
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Once a common sight in lecture theaters and coffee shops everywhere, the glowing emblem of an Apple logo featured on the lids of many Mac laptops launched in the early 2000s. In a nice touch, the new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with PROLED
paragraph1: Once a common sight in lecture theaters and coffee shops everywhere, the glowing emblem of an Apple logo featured on the lids of many Mac laptops launched in the early 2000s. In a nice touch, the new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with PROLED XDR displays bring back the much-loved logo. It's lit up whenever the Mac is awake, and it automatically dims or brightens based on your screen's brightness level and the ambient light in the room. Image credit: MacRumors forum member sniffiesIf you'd rather keep the logo dark, Apple has shared a way to turn it off. Unusually though, there's no switch in System Settings. Instead, you need to enter a command in the Terminal app. If that sounds intimidating, don't worry – it's a single line that you can copy and paste. Note that the following command only works on MacBook Pro models with a PROLED XDR display. Open Terminal on your Mac: it's in the Applications ➝ Utilities folder, or you can search for "Terminal" using Spotlight (Command + Space).
paragraph2: Type or paste the following command, then press Enter: sudo defaults write com.apple.CoreBrightness LEBacklightMode -int 0 When prompted, enter your administrator password and press Enter. (Terminal doesn't show the password as you type it.) After performing the steps, the logo illumination should turn off immediately, no restart required. The change applies to all macOS user accounts on the machine, and it will carry over even if you start up from macOS Recovery. If you later migrate to a new Mac, the setting even transfers across with the rest of your system. Relight the Apple Logo Reinstalling macOS turns the illumination back on, but you can also turn it back on yourself at any time by entering the following command in Terminal: sudo defaults delete com.apple.
paragraph3: CoreBrightness LEBacklightMode Remember to press Enter! Backstory The first Mac laptop with a lit-up Apple logo was the third-generation PowerBook G3 launched in 1999. The glowing symbol proved a mainstay through consecutive Apple notebooks for the next 16 years. The only change in that period was that the logo got flipped upright, so that it no longer appeared upside-down to onlookers when someone was sat in public with the lid open. According to former Apple employee Joe Moreno, the original orientation was deliberate: Apple's design group had found that users kept trying to open their laptops from the wrong end. "Steve Jobs always focused on providing the best possible user experience and believed that it was more important to satisfy the user than the onlooker," Moreno recalled. Ironically, Jobs later reversed the decision. "Opening a laptop from the wrong end is a self-correcting problem that only lasts a few seconds," said Moreno. "However, viewing the upside logo is a problem that lasts indefinitely."
paragraph4: The earlier orientation, seen in Sex and the City (Image: HBO/Everett/Rex Features) In 2015, Apple began nixing the illuminated insignia from its laptops, starting with the ultra-thin 12-inch MacBook, which had a polished metal logo instead, like iPads before it. In 2016, a new generation of MacBook Pro models continued the unlit trend. Apple hasn't launched a Mac laptop with a glowing logo since – until now. title: Developer ends lucrative screensaver deal with Roku because Fox bought it
title_bn: Developer ends lucrative screensaver deal with Roku because Fox bought it
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Developer: “I can’t be part of the Fox world.”
paragraph1: Sachs told Ars he’s interested in placating fans of the Marine Aquarium and said Roku has asked him to restore the license. When asked what his biggest concerns about Fox buying Roku are, Sachs said: It seems that Fox simply wants another venue for spreading their philosophy, which I consider repugnant. I can’t stand the idea of my artwork being used to lure even one person down that rabbit hole. The decision to not renew the licensing contract has “major financial consequences,” Sachs said.
paragraph2: “Our needs are very small, with a high property tax bill being the only significant expense,” he said. “We’ll be okay but can’t start any of the projects I had planned.” According to Sachs, the licensing “agreement was $80,000 per year for exclusive rights to all set-top devices, or $60,000 per year for non-exclusive. They have always opted for exclusive.
paragraph3: ” Ars asked Roku to confirm the details of the licensing agreement but didn’t hear back ahead of publication. The licensing deal with Roku was Sachs’ primary form of income, he told Ars, noting low sales of the version of the screensaver for computers. Marine Aquarium fans can still buy the screensaver for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android, but it seems unlikely that it will return to the Roku platform. “One of the best reasons to buy Roku was the themes and less ads than competitors.
paragraph4: But they haven’t added any new themes in years aside from sponsored ones, and they increased the amount of ads,” a Reddit user posted this week in response to Roku’s loss of the Aquatic Life screensaver. Sachs, meanwhile, says he has “no delusions” that pulling the license will have any meaningful impact. However, he’s hopeful that another streaming company will look to offer the screensaver. “I’m assuming that Fox will not be reversing their whole rage-based business model and take responsibility for all the harm it has caused.
paragraph5: I’d be happy to restore the license under those circumstances. They could even have it for free,” he said. Fox closed its acquisition of Roku today for $22 billion.

title: FAA to finally ditch floppy disks in what it calls "historic" tech upgrade
title_bn: FAA to finally ditch floppy disks in what it calls "historic" tech upgrade
author: TechPulse
excerpt: FAA information display systems to be floppy-free at 435 sites by end of 2028.
paragraph1: “Good news America: floppy disks are out, 21st century tech is in,” US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. Duffy posted a video yesterday about the upgrade in which a newscaster describing the FAA’s outdated technology says, “the FAA systems are essentially running on Windows 95.” Like other Trump appointees, Duffy was quick to give credit to the president, although the plan was shepherded through by officials in both the Biden and Trump administrations. “The greatest nation in the world deserves a state-of-the-art air traffic control system, and under President Trump, we’re delivering just that,” Duffy said. In August 2020, the FAA awarded a contract to Leidos to design and develop E-IDS. Leidos said in a press release at the time that E-IDS is part of the FAA’s Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) modernization project, which encompasses numerous upgrades going back to 2008.
paragraph2: The FAA said E-IDS will replace the Information Display System 4 (IDS-4), Controller Equipment Information Display System (ACE-IDS), NAS Information Display System (NIDS), and En Route Information Display System (ERIDS). IDS-4, one of the systems being replaced, runs on MS-DOS and “has been in constant use since the early 1990s as a vital informational resource/tool for air traffic controllers,” according to a 2018 press release issued by Systems Atlanta, a vendor that had an FAA contract to support the system. As PCMag notes, IDS-4 appears to run on desktop PCs with 3.5-inch floppy disk drives. Image from Department of Transportation report on the E-IDS upgrade. Image from Department of Transportation report on the E-IDS upgrade.
paragraph3: Credit: US Department of Transportation Obsolete tech “cumbersome for controllers” An April 2026 report by the Department of Transportation said, “Controllers have used a system that is driven by floppy disks and an antiquated operation system for critical information such as weather, NOTAMs and airport status.” With E-IDS, those controllers will have “a single platform that pulls that data into one view. Instead of searching for info, they [will] have immediate access to everything they need to make split-second decisions,” the report said. The out-of-date systems were criticized in a September 2026 report by the US Government Accountability Office (GAO). “Legacy display systems rely on obsolete technology (e.g.
paragraph4: , floppy disks) and interfaces from the 1980s, inefficient data organization, and manual update methods,” the report said. “The systems are cumbersome for controllers to search, retrieve, and display information. Multiple diverse display systems create inefficient activities needed to sustain these systems.” The GAO report said these information display systems are used in Air Route Traffic Control Centers, Terminal Radar Approach Control facilities, and control towers. The systems display textual and graphical information, “such as flight approach charts, combined with Notice to Airmen and weather information. This information is needed to support controller-to-pilot flight operations,” the GAO said.
paragraph5: This post was updated with further information and a graphic on floppy disks on Nov. 6, 2026 at 15:05 pm.

title: Apple Says More Than 100,000 Apps Optimized for iPhone Duo, Here's What's Still Missing
title_bn: Apple Says More Than 100,000 Apps Optimized for iPhone Duo, Here's What's Still Missing
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple today announced that more than 100,000 apps have been optimized for the iPhone Duo, released two weeks ago. We confirmed that this figure refers to apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later, meaning these apps fill the full width of the iPhone
paragraph1: Apple today announced that more than 100,000 apps have been optimized for the iPhone Duo, released two weeks ago. We confirmed that this figure refers to apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later, meaning these apps fill the full width of the iPhone Duo's inner and outer displays and have vertical controls in the status bar. A statement from Susan Prescott, Apple's Vice President of Worldwide Developer Relations: It's been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we're grateful for their creativity and innovation. Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day. In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users. The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we're excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.
paragraph2: Apple said thousands of apps optimized for the iPhone Duo are being added to the App Store each day, with recent examples including Microsoft's Excel, OneNote, PowerPoint, and Word apps, along with the Etsy, Goodnotes, Halide Mark III, NBA, NHL, and Zoom apps. Other apps optimized for the device include Amazon Prime Video, Fantastical, Flighty, Instagram, MLB, Netflix, SmartGym, WhatsApp, YouTube, and more. There are too many to list. Apps optimized for the iPhone Duo have a "Made for iPhone Duo" badge in their App Store listings on the device, making them easy to identify. iOS 27.2 added Apple Pencil (USB-C) support to the iPhone Duo, enabling users to draw in apps like Procreate Pocket, take notes in Apple Notes, Fineliner, and TypeDraw, and mark up documents in apps like Preview on the device. On the other hand, with millions of apps available in the App Store, there are unsurprisingly many apps that are still not optimized for the iPhone Duo, with the following examples listed in alphabetical order: AMC Theaters, Amazon Fire TV, Apple Store, Best Buy, Bluesky, Delta, DoorDash, Duolingo, Fandango, FedEx, Goodreads, Google Docs, Google Home, Google Sheets, Google Slides, GrubHub, JetBlue, Libby, Microsoft Authenticator, Microsoft Teams, MTA, Nike, PayPal, PictureThis, Ring, Southwest, Spectrum TV, Starbucks, Steam, Uber Eats, UPS, USPS, Venmo, Verizon, Wells Fargo, Whole Foods, and YouTube Music.
paragraph3: Apple said developers can easily optimize their apps for the iPhone Duo. Apps that use standard SwiftUI and UIKit components adapt automatically to each display, with controls moved to the status bar and multi-column support on the inner display. New APIs let developers optimize their apps for the device's various layouts and poses. Apple has hosted more than 50 in-person iPhone Duo app workshops in 19 cities worldwide, and there are online resources like the Apple Developer Forums. In the meantime, apps built with the iOS 27 SDK resize to fill most of the inner display on the iPhone Duo, but they avoid the status bar on the right edge. Apps built with the iOS 26 SDK or earlier run on the iPhone Duo, but appear in the center of the inner display, with lots of empty black space on the left and right sides of the apps. iPhone Duo app optimization has been a hotly debated topic on social media platforms, with some people pointing out apps that are not yet optimized and others saying the issue is overblown.
paragraph4: It is clearly a mixed bag, with some apps optimized and some not. More apps are being updated by the day, though, so the situation is improving rapidly.
