Interestingly, there’s also an image that shows the Galaxy Fit 4 at 100% battery with an estimated four days and three hours of usage remaining.The Galaxy Fit 3, for reference, offers roughly 13 days of battery life on a single charge, suggesting that its successor could either see a significant drop in battery life or that the estimate is simply placeholder data. The latter is likely to be the case here.
bangla_paragraph5: Samsung has yet to announce a release date for the Galaxy Fit 4, though considering that the wearable has already secured an FCC certification, an official announcement might not be too far away.

title: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
title_bn: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference on Wednesday, the executive touted how the company had been gaining ground in the enterprise market, where rival Anthropic had already successfully made inroads.
paragraph1: OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman said the company would be ready for an IPO in 2027, noting that its enterprise revenue has been growing. Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference on Wednesday, the executive touted how the company had been gaining ground in the enterprise market, where rival Anthropic had already successfully made inroads. In response to the interviewer’s question about being IPO-ready next year, Brockman replied, “I think so. Yes.” “We’ve been very clear this year that we want to go public when we feel is the right time for us, and I feel extremely good about the business. I feel like we’ve made so much progress this year, and I’ve honestly never felt more confident in what we’re doing,” Brockman said.
paragraph2: He detailed how OpenAI’s trajectory as an enterprise had changed over the course of 2026, noting that the first and second quarters were “pretty rough.” He also admitted that OpenAI “wasn’t even in the conversation” when it came to agentic coding — an area where Anthropic’s Claude Code has gained market share. “We had Codex, but no one was talking about it,” Brockman continued, “and I think that we just kept our heads down and executed.” By the third quarter, activity picked up, as OpenAI saw 70% quarterly growth in its annualized revenue — something Brockman attributed to the enterprise side of the business doubling. He explained that the growth wasn’t simply the result of something that happened in the quarter itself, but rather the culmination of investments the company had been making up to that point. Now the majority of OpenAI’s revenue is coming from the enterprise business, which previously accounted for only around 30% of its total revenue.
paragraph3: “And it’s not that consumer [revenue has shrunk] … It’s been growing, but it’s the enterprise segment has really taken off,” he said, pointing to a recent partnership with JPMorgan Chase as one example of the type of client it’s now winning deals with. Brockman also spoke more broadly about the lessons OpenAI learned from selling into the enterprise market as well. He said the company had come to understand that its job was to help businesses identify the most important milestones they could achieve with its AI technology, build trust with clients, and demonstrate that it was a reliable partner for the long haul. “A year ago, we weren’t even really in the enterprise game, right? We were really perceived as a consumer company, and a lot of the companies we’d start talking to would say, ‘Is OpenAI really committed to the enterprise?’” Brockman said.

title: India targets creating homegrown GPUs within 2 years and plans to commercialize indigenous SHAKTI and VEGA processors
title_bn: India targets creating homegrown GPUs within 2 years and plans to commercialize indigenous SHAKTI and VEGA processors
author: TechPulse
excerpt: MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan says India plans to develop its own GPU under Semiconductor Mission 2.0, with a target of approximately two years. The country is also looking to commercialize its SHAKTI and VEGA RISC-V processors, expand domestic server
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) India wants to develop its own graphics processing unit (GPU) within the next two years as the country steps up efforts to build a domestic semiconductor industry and reduce its dependence on foreign chip suppliers, reports ETGovernment. The target was outlined by S.Krishnan, secretary of India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), in a November 4 interview. "Under India Semiconductor Mission 2.
paragraph2: 0, we intend to target the development of an indigenous GPU chip. We should have a GPU chip of our own. This will not happen overnight. It is a project that will require approximately 24 months, and we intend to work towards that objective," Krishnan said.
paragraph3: The proposed GPU is part of a wider plan to establish an Indian hardware and software ecosystem, with Krishnan describing five layers needed to support AI development. These include: energy, accelerator chips, computing infrastructure and servers, AI models and applications. Indian companies such as VVDN, Kaynes and Avalon are already manufacturing servers, while the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) has developed its Rudra server range, whose systems are designed to support AI workloads, after which the government transfers the technology to local manufacturers. Krishnan also sees AI as a potential repeat of the opportunity India's IT industry experienced during the Y2K (the year 2000 bug) transition.

title: Google Home bug is repeatedly asking some users to set up the app again
title_bn: Google Home bug is repeatedly asking some users to set up the app again
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Some smart homes keep forgetting who's in charge.
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR Some Google Home users say the app repeatedly asks them to sign in or complete setup whenever they open it. Reports dating back to mid-October mention versions 4.34.22 and 4.35.25.1, although the issue doesn’t appear widespread.
paragraph2: No confirmed fix exists, but affected users can try updating to version 4.36.24 or newer. The Google Home app is supposed to remember your smart home devices, but some users say it’s having trouble remembering them. For at least two weeks, the app has been repeatedly welcoming existing users as though they’ve never opened it before, turning a routine trip to their smart home controls into an unexpected account setup exercise.The complaints have been trickling into Reddit discussions and Google’s support forums since mid-October. Instead of landing on their familiar dashboard, affected users say they see a welcome screen whenever they launch Google Home, forcing them to select or set up their Google account before accessing connected devices.
paragraph3: The app isn’t always in a hurry to cooperate, with some users reporting waiting up to 10 minutes for their devices to appear when they skip setup. It’s one of those bugs that easily disrupt your usual habit of controlling smart home devices directly from the lock screen, so we understand the frustration among those affected.The fact that the complaints span multiple Google Home app versions, including v4.34.22 and the newer v4.35.25.
paragraph4: 1, is even more frustrating. However, the issue doesn’t appear widespread. We’ve used the Google Home app regularly on the affected v4.34.22 and even the latest v4.36.24 without encountering the issue.
paragraph5: So if you’re affected, it’s worth checking the Play Store for the latest version. It hasn’t been confirmed as a fix, but it’s a reasonable first step while the cause remains unclear.One user claims Google support acknowledged a known issue following an app update. However, Google has not publicly confirmed this, and community representatives continue directing complaints to support.We’ve reached out to Google for clarification on what’s causing the repeated sign-in prompts, whether the latest app update addresses the problem, and if a broader fix is underway. We’ll update this article if we hear back.

title: YouTube bug makes the app appear in half dark mode, half light
title_bn: YouTube bug makes the app appear in half dark mode, half light
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A bug is causing issues with dark and light mode on YouTube.
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR YouTube viewers are reporting an issue with using the app in light mode and dark mode. The issue causes the playback area and comments section to be displayed in dark mode, while the rest of the screen is in light mode. Both Android and iOS users are experiencing the bug. Some YouTube viewers are reporting a display issue with the mobile app.
paragraph2: The top half of the screen, where the player and comments section are located, is displayed in dark mode. Meanwhile, the rest of the UI is displayed in light mode.According to the reports (1, 2, 3, 4), the bug happens regardless of whether you have dark mode or light mode enabled. Switching Ambient mode on or off reportedly doesn’t have an effect either.
paragraph3: Users have tried restarting the app, restarting their phones, clearing cache, uninstalling and reinstalling the app, and adjusting accessibility settings. Despite taking these measures, the effected users claim that the issue persists.A majority of the reports come from Android users, but the problem is not exclusive to one platform. We also spotted at least one report from an iPhone user.
paragraph4: While there are plenty of new reports, it appears that some viewers have been experiencing this issue for a while.It’s understandable why such a bug would be irritating. If you want apps to be in dark mode, then you want the entire app to be dark and vice versa. A screen split into half dark mode and half light mode kind of defeats the purpose.
paragraph5: Android Authority has reached out to Google for comment. We will update this article when new information becomes available. If you’re experiencing this glitch, let us know in the comments section.

paragraph1: SUMMARYGo Digit General Insurance reported a 31.1% YoY decline in net profit to ₹142.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, while insurance revenue grew 1.7% to ₹2,720.5 Cr. The insurer's insurance service result fell 73.4% YoY to ₹43 Cr as insurance service expenses increased 22.4% to ₹2,607.7 Cr Motor Third Party insurance remained Go Digit’s largest segment, generating ₹1,066.1 Cr in Q2 FY27 revenue, up 8.3% YoY Insurtech Go Digit reported a 31.1% year-on-year (YoY) decline in its net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹142.4 Cr from ₹206.8 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. The insurtech major’s profit also declined 62.4% sequentially from ₹378.61 Cr in the June quarter. The decline in profitability came despite a marginal increase in insurance revenue, which rose 1.
paragraph2: 7% to ₹2,720.5 Cr during the quarter from ₹2,674.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, insurance revenue increased 2.1% from ₹2,665.6 Cr. Segment-wise, Motor Third Party (TP) insurance remained Go Digit’s largest business, contributing ₹1,066.1 Cr to insurance revenue in Q2 FY27, up 8.3% YoY. Motor Own Damage (OD) insurance revenue grew at a faster pace of 11.4% YoY to ₹640.64 Cr. The company’s gross written premium for the quarter dipped by 3.6% YoY to ₹2,571 Cr while gross direct premium, dipped 1.2% to ₹2,351 Cr. However, the company’s insurance service result, which reflects the profitability of its insurance operations before investment and other financial income, sunk 73.4% YoY to ₹43 Cr from ₹161.98 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
paragraph3: The figure also fell 62.3% sequentially from ₹114 Cr. The deterioration in the insurance service result came as insurance service expenses increased 22.4% YoY to ₹2,607.73 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹2,130.85 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. Incurred claims rose 9.2% to ₹1,968.03 Cr from ₹1,802.96 Cr, while employee benefit expenses increased 4.3% to ₹95.48 Cr. Commission expenses, on the other hand, declined 2.6% YoY to ₹781.88 Cr from ₹803.10 Cr. Other insurance service expenses increased 1.7% to ₹94.
paragraph4: 52 Cr. On the investment front, Go Digit reported a 20.6% YoY increase in investment income to ₹368.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹305.5 Cr in the year-ago period. However, investment income declined 39.2% sequentially from ₹606.47 Cr. The company’s net finance result, which includes investment income and insurance finance income or expenses, increased 28.6% YoY to ₹196.94 Cr. Consequently, Go Digit’s profit before tax (PBT) declined 31.2% YoY to ₹190.18 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹276.30 Cr in Q2 FY26. The figure was also down 62.4% sequentially from ₹505.96 Cr in Q1 FY27.
paragraph5: Total tax expense stood at ₹47.79 Cr during the quarter, comprising current tax of ₹3.93 Cr and deferred tax of ₹43.86 Cr. This compared with a total tax expense of ₹69.51 Cr in Q2 FY26. For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), Go Digit reported a 3.2% YoY decline in net profit to ₹521 Cr from ₹538.23 Cr in H1 FY26. Insurance revenue increased 4.5% YoY to ₹5,386.09 Cr during the six-month period. Shares of Go Digit ended today’s trading session 1.05% higher at ₹260.30.

title: Venomics AI Raises $2.7 Mn To Turn Venom Into Medicine
title_bn: Venomics AI Raises $2.7 Mn To Turn Venom Into Medicine
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Bengaluru-based biotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale…
paragraph1: SUMMARYBiotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons The fresh capital will be used to expand ‘Venom Atlas’, a molecular dataset of venom-derived compounds, and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities The startup combines venom biology, AI and experimental screening to identify and develop venom-derived molecules into potential therapeutic leads Bengaluru-based biotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.
paragraph2: 5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio. The startup, spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), combines venom biology, AI and experimental screening to identify and develop venom-derived molecules into potential therapeutic leads. The fresh capital will be used to expand ‘Venom Atlas’, a molecular dataset of venom-derived compounds, and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities. The startup also plans to expand its team across venom biology, computational science and drug discovery, while supporting the validation and optimisation of promising molecules.
paragraph3: Founded in 2026 by Kartik Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, Venomics AI is working to tap the largely unexplored molecular diversity found in animal venoms to identify potential drug candidates. Animal venoms contain complex molecules that have evolved over millions of years to interact with specific biological targets. Some of these compounds have already inspired medicines. However, a large part of the molecular diversity across venomous species remains unexplored, presenting an opportunity for drug discovery.
paragraph4: Venomics AI is building a platform that combines molecular sequencing and venom biology to map this diversity through its Venom Atlas. It then uses AI to prioritise promising molecular candidates and validates its predictions through functional laboratory screening. “Animal venoms represent one of nature’s richest yet least explored sources of potential medicines, and at Venomics AI, we are combining cutting-edge experimental science with artificial intelligence to unlock this extraordinary potential,” Sunagar said. India’s bioeconomy is on track to reach $300 Bn by 2030, with the country’s rapid emergence as a global biotechnology hub, based on IBEF data.
paragraph5: Notably, the biotech sector in the country has been booming in recent years. The country is home to more than 11,000 biotech startups. Also, as part of the Budget 2027, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced a new ‘Biopharma SHAKTI’ scheme with an outlay of ₹10,000 Cr. Meanwhile, investor interest in this space has been gradually seeing an uptick, where earlier this year, Cellogen Therapeutics secured ₹20 Cr in funding from Kotak Alternate Asset Managers (Kotak Alts), while StrainX Bioworks has raised $13 Mn in a funding round led by Prime Venture Partners and Leo Capital.

title: Micron's $4.5 billion Taoyuan plant construction halted amidst labor dispute
title_bn: Micron's $4.5 billion Taoyuan plant construction halted amidst labor dispute
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Micron and the Taoyuan labor union is set to meet again on November 6 as the two parties engage in a protracted labor dispute regarding profit-sharing.
paragraph1: Micron has paused construction on its Fab 11E site at Taoyuan as the company and its Taoyuan labor union have failed to reach an agreement regarding clearer profit-sharing terms. Bloomberg reports that activity on the site has all but halted, except for minor safety work, with some sources saying that executives are concerned about uncertainties regarding negotiations with its workers.
paragraph2: The company hasn’t released a statement about the move but has already informed local officials about the suspension.“Taiwan plays an important role in Micron’s global footprint, and our operations today continue as normal,” Micron said.
paragraph3: “We are confident in maintaining business continuity for our customers.” The company has recently announced a bonus that could give as much as five times the annual salary of some eligible workers, and has also wrapped up a deal with the bigger Taichung union, although some members say they were dissatisfied with the outcome.
paragraph4: On the other hand, the Taoyuan union is still holding out for better terms, with the two parties set to meet again on November 6. It even launched a one-day strike last month to show the chipmaker its resolve and how its operations could be disrupted if it does not meet their demands.

title: SaaS Company RateGain’s Q2 Profit Rises 47% YoY To ₹75 Cr
title_bn: SaaS Company RateGain’s Q2 Profit Rises 47% YoY To ₹75 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Travel-focused SaaS company RateGain reported a 46.5% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in the September quarter…
paragraph1: SUMMARYRateGain reported a consolidated net profit of ₹74.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 46.5% YoY, while operating revenue jumped 152.6% to ₹745.4 Cr. The consolidation of Sojern significantly expanded RateGain’s revenue and expenses, with marketing technology now accounting for 80.2% of its revenue. RateGain’s UK subsidiary repaid another $46.3 Mn today, reducing the outstanding acquisition-related debt to $31.3 Mn, a quarter of the original facility. Travel-focused SaaS company Rategain reported a 46.5% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from ₹51 Cr a year ago. Operating revenue jumped 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr, reflecting the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, which RateGain acquired for $250 Mn in November last year.
paragraph2: Sequentially, net profit declined 21.3% from ₹94.9 Cr, while operating revenue fell 5% from ₹785 Cr. RateGain reported negative other income of ₹26.2 Lakh, taking its total income to ₹745.1 Cr. Total expenses rose about 158% YoY to ₹647.7 Cr. Adjusted for deferred deal consideration related to the Sojern acquisition, RateGain said its net profit rose 78% YoY to ₹90.8 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to ₹169.1 Cr. For H1 FY27, operating revenue increased 169.5% YoY to ₹1,530.4 Cr from ₹568 Cr. Reported EBITDA rose 214.2% to ₹324.
paragraph3: 5 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA increased 250.9% to ₹362.5 Cr. The company said its reported H1 EBITDA had already exceeded its full-year FY26 EBITDA. Sojern Integration And Debt The Sojern acquisition expanded RateGain’s travel marketing business, particularly its presence among destination marketing organisations (DMOs), hotels, and other travel businesses. To finance the acquisition, RateGain’s UK subsidiary secured a $125 Mn debt facility from HSBC and Citibank, backed by a corporate guarantee from the Indian parent. Including a repayment of $46.3 Mn today, the subsidiary has repaid $93.8 Mn, or 75%, of the original facility. Its outstanding debt now stands at $31.3 Mn. Alongside the expansion in revenue, RateGain said the Sojern integration helped broaden its customer base. It had 14,538 customers at the end of September, about 4.5X the 3,224 customers it had at the end of FY25. Its customers include hospitality companies, online travel agencies (OTAs), airlines, car rental companies, and DMOs. Marketing Drives Business Mix RateGain operates across three verticals: data as a service (DaaS), distribution, and marketing technology.
paragraph4: Its offerings span competitive pricing and demand intelligence, hotel distribution, digital marketing, and guest engagement. Marketing technology now accounts for 80.2% of revenue, followed by DaaS at 13.2% and distribution at 6.6%. By customer industry, hospitality contributed 48.6% of H1 revenue, followed by DMOs at 30.9%, OTAs at 7.2%, airlines at 3.7%, and car rentals at 2.3%. North America accounted for 63.7% of H1 revenue, followed by Europe at 21.5%, Asia-Pacific at 12.3%, and other markets at 2.5%.
paragraph5: The company’s client roster includes 33 of the world’s top 40 hotel chains, four of the top five airlines, and seven of the top 10 car rental companies. RateGain also highlighted its AI products. Chairman and MD Bhanu Chopra said shifting travel demand is increasing customers’ reliance on data and AI. He said RateGain’s priorities included adding customers, increasing their use of its platform, and extending AI into more of their daily operations. In H2 FY27, the company plans to take the combined RateGain and Sojern offering to more customers. RateGain reported a total pipeline of ₹660 Cr and new contract wins worth ₹277.7 Cr. The company’s employee headcount stood at 1,244 at the end of September, up 42.8% YoY. Shares of RateGain ended today’s trading session 3.3% higher at ₹819.50 apiece on the BSE.

title: [Update] Exclusive: RapidClaims In Talks To Raise $30 Mn
title_bn: [Update] Exclusive: RapidClaims In Talks To Raise $30 Mn
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Update | November 5, 19:43 After the story was published, RapidClaims founder and CEO Dushyant Mishra said the startup is…
paragraph1: SUMMARYRapidClaims is in talks to raise around $30 Mn in a funding round led by WestBridge Capital at a valuation of about $200 Mn, sources told Inc42 The proposed fundraise comes amid investor bets on healthcare automation startups, including recent rounds raised by Confido Health and Consint.AI. Existing investors Accel and Together Fund are likely to participate in the round, which is expected to be the startup’s Series B. Update | November 5, 19:43 After the story was published, RapidClaims founder and CEO Dushyant Mishra said the startup is not in talks with WestBridge Capital to raise any funding round. He also said that the $200 Mn valuation figure is “incorrect”. Original | October 5, 18:22 AI-powered SaaS startup RapidClaims is in talks to raise around $30 Mn in a funding round led by WestBridge Capital at a valuation of about $200 Mn, sources told Inc42.
paragraph2: The round is expected to be its Series B, with existing investors Accel and Together Fund likely to participate, the sources added. RapidClaims did not respond to questions sent by Inc42, while WestBridge Capital declined to comment. Founded in 2023 by Dushyant Mishra, Abhinay Vyas, and Jot Sarup Singh, RapidClaims builds AI-powered revenue cycle management (RCM) software that helps healthcare providers automate medical coding, improve clinical documentation, prevent insurance claim denials, and recover outstanding payments. The startup primarily caters to healthcare providers in the US, helping them address billing errors, rejected claims, and delays in reimbursements. Automating Healthcare Revenue Workflows RapidClaims’ products include RapidCode for medical coding, RapidVBC for clinical documentation and risk adjustment, and RapidRecovery for managing denied claims, automating appeals, and detecting underpayments. The platform integrates with healthcare providers’ existing electronic health record systems.
paragraph3: It serves physician groups, hospitals, health systems, federally qualified health centres (FQHCs), and ambulatory surgery centres, among other healthcare organisations. The startup is also developing inpatient coding capabilities with design partners, extending its automation tools to coding for hospital admissions. In April 2025, RapidClaims raised $8 Mn in a Series A round led by Accel, with participation from Together Fund. It also disclosed that it had previously raised $3 Mn in seed funding. RapidClaims had earmarked the Series A proceeds for expanding its go-to-market efforts, strengthening its technology and product capabilities, and growing its sales and marketing teams. At the time, the startup said it had grown sixfold over the preceding four months and served a double-digit client base.
paragraph4: It was also looking to expand its presence among FQHCs, physician groups, outpatient facilities, and ambulatory surgery centres. Investors Bet On Automation The proposed fundraise comes amid increasing investor interest in startups looking to automate healthcare administration and insurance workflows. In October, Confido Health raised $12.5 Mn in a Series A extension led by Z47, taking its total Series A funding to $22.5 Mn. The startup develops AI agents for tasks including appointment scheduling, insurance verification, prescription refills, and payment collection.
paragraph5: Meanwhile, Consint.AI raised ₹22 Cr to expand internationally and develop its AI capabilities for fraud detection and claims processing. Its products automate claims processing, digitise documents, and standardise healthcare records.

title: I downloaded the first third-party app store from Google Play, and I’m hopeful for what’s next
title_bn: I downloaded the first third-party app store from Google Play, and I’m hopeful for what’s next
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Aptoide Games is a decent first start, but it leaves me waiting for more.
paragraph1: Andrew Grush / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: Third-party app stores have been part of the Android experience since literally its earliest days, with the SlideME store predating Google’s official Android Market by several months. Since then we’ve seen plenty of other third-party stores rise up, but they’ve always required extra hoops on the user’s end, like sideloading. That’s no longer the case, as Google Play recently added its very first officially authorized third-party store.This is a major shift in Google’s behavior, but it didn’t come from kindness. Epic Games spent years fighting a legal and PR battle against Apple’s and Google’s app store monopolies. The effort paid off, as it led to several changes, including the passing of anti-monopoly laws like Europe’s Digital Markets Act (DMA). These laws require Google to open up the platform to allow competing storefronts.So far, the effort has been fairly tepid, though it seems many more could be coming later this year. Thankfully, at least one such storefront has made it off the ground: Aptoide Games.
paragraph2: Let’s take a look at how easy it is to install, as well as my general thoughts on the future of third-party app stores.Are you excited about third party app stores coming to Google Play?0 votesInstalling is a piece of cake, and so is using itAndrew Grush / Android AuthorityAs someone who has downloaded countless third-party app stores, I’m used to a little friction here. What I found was basically a one-click installation process that’s no different from installing Angry Birds. While it’s not exactly prominently advertised, finding Aptoide Games was as easy as using the search bar. After that, I tapped “Install,” and in less than a minute, the app store opened and was ready.The first official third-party app store is laid out similarly to Google Play, with a bottom bar of shortcuts to different sections and an easy way to search for specific apps. The layout is clean, easy to use, and feels much more polished than some of the less-refined sideloaded stores I’ve tested over the years.Installing it was easy, though it also felt a bit redundant next to Google Play.
paragraph3: The other thing I learned quickly is that this wasn’t a barren storefront, as it pretty much had every game I could imagine. The catch is that many of these games aren’t actually hosted by Aptoide Games at all, due to a program called the Play Catalog Access Program. This program was part of the legal rulings against Google in the Epic Games lawsuit and basically grants any third-party app store full access to Google’s library. As you can imagine, there are restrictions and rules here, which is partially why Aptoide Games has been the only officially approved candidate so far.Now, to be fair, it’s not just Google-hosted apps. Aptoide Games has a small share of exclusive apps, including those with special reward incentives. In many ways, though, the experience felt a bit redundant next to Google Play. I fear that could be true of other app stores available from Google Play in the future, but it is still too early to tell for sure.I love the potential here, but am also realistic about the limitsAndy Walker / Android AuthorityThere’s a reason that there’s only one official third-party app store so far.
paragraph4: As you might have guessed, publishing a third-party app store requires going through more hoops than publishing an ordinary app. Google’s own documentation has the exact guidelines for those who want to dive deeper, but basically Google requires every app store to ensure a few things: Stores must offer open access with clear, non-discriminatory policies regarding which apps and services they offer. All apps on a store must have clear developer authorization and IP compliance. Certain security, privacy, and safety standards must be met. This includes following Google Play policies, “with the exception of policies that are not applicable to third-party app stores, such as the Payments policy.” All new apps added to a storefront must be signed off by Google, and failure to do so can result in a third-party store being delisted. Those are just a few of the bigger rules. Still, Google says it will occasionally audit random samples of third-party catalogs and that a store must not exceed a 2% content-policy violation rate across audited apps. In addition to quite a few rules, Google also charges a $15,000 upfront annual service fee to perform the necessary security and policy reviews on an app store.
paragraph5: It will also invoice developers if review costs exceed $10,000 per month.If I’m honest, I have a feeling that the Google Play-focused third-party app store experience will likely remain a curated, partial experience. There’s a reason we didn’t get the full-blown Aptoide market here, after all. The good news is this also isn’t Google’s only program from the sounds of it. In addition to Google Play adding select, highly niche stores like Aptoide Games, Google has a broader plan that will bypass some of Android’s recent sideloading restrictions and make it easier to sideload approved app stores as well.Between two similar but slightly different approaches to third-party app stores, it’s clear that third-party app stores will have a larger presence than ever before. It’s also clear Google will do its best to make the process difficult and expensive, which likely rules out some of the smaller, independent open-source stores out there.Still, even with the program somewhat held back by Google, I’m excited to see how it plays out. As sideloading gets harder, adding select curated app stores to Google Play and making it easier to sideload approved stores will only make Android stronger and will help keep it from turning into a walled garden, for better or worse.

title: Spacetech Startup Cosmoserve Nets $6 Mn, Eyes Commercialisation By 2028
title_bn: Spacetech Startup Cosmoserve Nets $6 Mn, Eyes Commercialisation By 2028
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Japan-based Rebright Partners. While Aranya Holdings and…
paragraph1: SUMMARYCosmoserve raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Rebright Partners and inaugurated India’s first private space debris removal facility in Hyderabad It aims to launch another mission in the coming months to validate its soft robotic capture technology to remove defunct satellites and orbital debris from space Following this and another tech demonstration next year, Cosmoserve aims to start commercial operations by 2028 Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Japan-based Rebright Partners. While Aranya Holdings and Naandi Ventures also participated in the round, existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC doubled down on their erstwhile bet. The startup shared plans to utilise the fresh capital to support tech demonstrations, fuel two upcoming missions, as well enhance the operations of its recently unveiled Hyderabad facility. Cosmoserve has now raised over $9 Mn since inception last year. The startup has doubled its valuation since it raised pre-seed funding in September, founder Chiranjeevi Phanindra told Inc42. The exact valuation is yet to be discerned.
paragraph2: For context, the startup is building tech to remove defunct satellites and orbital debris from space and reduce the collision risks for operational spacecraft in a cost effective manner. It plans on optimising costs by setting up features within its craft that will allow it to refuel in-orbit and remove multiple pieces of debris in a single mission. The startup made its first tech demonstration, Mission Embrace-1, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The mission was designed to test the startup’s soft robotic capture system that removes space debris, but the system’s robotic petals failed to deploy as intended. Cosmoserve claims to have now identified and addressed potential issues with the thermal mechanism used to release the petals and the impact of low temperatures on the system, according to Phanindra. The startup is now gearing up for Embrace-2, an upgraded version of the mission to validate its upgraded robotic capture mechanism, which is expected to launch in the coming months.
paragraph3: It is also planning a full-scale demonstration of its debris-removal capabilities, aiming to break a world record by approaching within 10 m of a dead satellite. Phanindra, who served close to 15 years with the ISRO before setting up Cosmoserve in June 2025, believes that the startup would be able to complete all tech demos by 2027 and start commercial operations by 2028. “We have several letters of intent from satellite constellation operators – one from the US, one from Europe and two from India. They have to abide by the regulation for removing the dead satellite from space … so we are aiming to get one paid customer before actual commercial operations begin,” he added. Cosmoserve’s Base 1 Alongside the funding announcement, Cosmoserve inaugurated its new space debris removal facility in Hyderabad named Base 1 today, in an event attended by union minister of state Dr Jitendra Singh and Telangana IT Minister D Sridhar Babu. Phanindra says that Base 1 is India’s first private and the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation.
paragraph4: In simpler terms, Base 1 can recreate conditions that spacecraft and equipment encounter in space, allowing companies to test how their tech will perform before an actual mission. This includes simulating how objects behave in microgravity (near-weightlessness) and how they appear or function under space-like visual conditions. This costs around ₹6 Cr to construct, per Phanindra. Base 1 houses infrastructure for designing, building and testing satellite servicing and space debris recovery missions. This includes an orbital rendezvous and capture lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integration, a mission control centre and a microgravity simulation platform. The facility will also support the development of in-orbit satellite repair and refuelling technologies.
paragraph5: Besides, the startup plans to use Base 1 to develop more critical technologies in-house in order to increase its share of local manufacturing from 60% and reduce dependence on imported components such as optics, avionics and space-grade electronics. “Primarily, the core technology we are building is a soft robotic capture system. We have a space robotics innovation lab where the R&D is happening. Then the next technology we are working on is a vision-based navigation system,” the founder told Inc42.

title: Sarvam’s Prism Enters India’s Growing AI Decision Model Race
title_bn: Sarvam’s Prism Enters India’s Growing AI Decision Model Race
author: TechPulse
excerpt: AI models are increasingly being built to do more than answer questions. Some are now designed to make specific decisions,…
paragraph1: SUMMARYSarvam AI has launched Prism, an open-weight decision model built on its Sarvam 105B model for fast, structured decisions across enterprise workflows. The launch puts Sarvam alongside Indian builders such as ConvAI Innovations and PurpleTalk’s Sthānika, as well as global players developing models designed to make decisions rather than generate text. Sarvam claims Prism achieves an average score of 71.8 across three evaluation indices, with a median response time of 44 milliseconds on an Nvidia B200 GPU. AI models are increasingly being built to do more than answer questions. Some are now designed to make specific decisions, such as whether a customer query should go to a sales or support team, whether a document needs further review, or whether an AI agent has completed a task correctly. In India, Kerala-based ConvAI Innovations was one of the first to explore this category with Laya, an open-weight decision model intended to run locally on devices such as laptops and phones. Hyderabad-based PurpleTalk’s research lab, Sthānika AI, has also developed Sieve, a family of decision models that returns probabilities for a fixed set of possible answers. Both startups are betting that specialised models can make these decisions faster and more efficiently than general-purpose AI systems. The space has now attracted Sarvam AI, one of India’s prominent homegrown AI model developers. The company introduced Prism, a decision model built on its 105B-parameter foundation model. Sarvam says Prism combines high accuracy with low response times, while allowing enterprises to customise and run it on their own infrastructure.
paragraph2: The launch raises a bigger question for India’s AI ecosystem, especially given the implications on cost, reliability and speed: Are decision models the opportunity for Indian AI startups to compete with global players, rather than trying to match them across every general-purpose AI capability? What Are Decision Models, And Why Now? Most large language models (LLMs) are designed to generate text. Even when asked to make a simple choice, they typically produce a response that another software system must interpret. This can add processing time, increase costs and introduce inconsistencies. Decision models approach the problem differently. They receive information, a question and a defined set of possible answers, then return a score or probability for each option. Instead of generating a paragraph explaining which department should handle a customer complaint, for instance, the model can assign probabilities to sales, support and billing. This makes them useful for repetitive tasks performed at scale, including customer-support routing, content moderation, fraud checks, security screening and evaluating the actions of AI agents. General-purpose models can perform these tasks too, but a specialised decision model may be faster and easier to integrate into workflows that require predictable outputs. The category gained visibility with Jev, the first public model from TypeSafe AI. Global companies, including Microsoft and Perplexity, have since introduced their own decision-model offerings.
paragraph3: Indian startups are also developing alternatives, with different priorities around local deployment, openness and enterprise use. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU How Sarvam Is Positioning Prism Prism is built on Sarvam 105B, the company’s large language model, but is fine-tuned specifically for making decisions. Rather than generating a sequence of words to arrive at an answer, it evaluates the available options in a single processing pass and returns a probability for each. According to Sarvam, Prism recorded an average score of 71.8 across three evaluation indices, with a median response time of 44 milliseconds on an Nvidia B200 GPU. The company said this was the highest average score among the 25 decision models it tested that responded in under 100 milliseconds. Sarvam also tested whether the order of available options would change the model’s decision. It reported that Prism produced consistent results across 2,000 questions after applying a fixed ordering mechanism before scoring. The company further said that Prism’s observed error rates were lower than its predicted error rates across the confidence thresholds it tested, including in Indian languages. These are company-reported results, and independent testing across comparable workloads will be important to establish how they translate into production performance. Sarvam is releasing Prism’s weights under the Apache 2.0 licence.
paragraph4: This allows developers to access the model’s trained parameters, adapt them and deploy the model on their own infrastructure, subject to the licence terms. It is also available through an API. The company is targeting applications such as customer-support routing, document intelligence, security checks, prompt-injection detection and evaluation of AI-agent activity. Its positioning is not simply about offering another language model, but about adding a specialised decision-making component to the broader AI stack. Laya, Sieve and Prism reflect different approaches to decision models in India. Laya prioritises small models that can run locally, while PurpleTalk’s research lab Sthānika AI focuses on open-weight Sieve models, with an emphasis on evaluation and tasks such as intent detection and AI-agent tool selection. Sarvam’s Prism builds on its foundation-model capabilities, with speed, confidence calibration, Indian-language performance and open-weight deployment among its key selling points. Articul8, an enterprise AI company, is also developing the category through Bivia, its multimodal decision model designed for domain-specific, evidence-backed decisions across text, images, documents, audio and video. Ananthanarayanan S, managing director for India at Articul8, said Sarvam’s launch adds to the growing range of general-purpose models, while positioning Bivia around a different enterprise need. He said Articul8 benchmarks Bivia against models such as Jev and evaluates it through a broader enterprise lens, including its ability to abstain when evidence is insufficient. He believes that the competition, however, will extend beyond benchmark scores and response times. Enterprises need models that can handle unfamiliar situations reliably and integrate with existing systems through domain grounding, orchestration and execution frameworks.
paragraph5: Prism has also drawn scrutiny from developers and independent evaluators. Sandipan Kundu, a developer relations and AI engineer focused on fine-tuning and inference, and the builder of Tensorant, a platform for fine-tuning, evaluating and deploying open models, said on X that the model appeared capable but questioned whether its 44-millisecond median latency claim reflected real-world performance. He cited a p95 latency of 420 milliseconds in his testing. He also flagged the cost of self-hosting a model of its size. Separately, Faizan Shaik, a software engineer at Atlan, an enterprise data and metadata management platform, shared results from the company’s Decision Bench, where Prism scored 91.5% across 1,071 decisions on 36 public datasets, placing it 12th among 22 models. His evaluation reported a median latency of 65 milliseconds on a B200 GPU. These assessments suggest that Prism is competitive, but also underline the need to examine performance across different benchmarks and deployment conditions. For Indian builders, the opportunity lies in proving that specialised decision models can deliver measurable gains in cost, latency and reliability across real-world workflows.

title: Reading on your phone is a trap, but this $200 BOOX is my escape hatch
title_bn: Reading on your phone is a trap, but this $200 BOOX is my escape hatch
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Read more articles again.
paragraph1: Stephen Radochia / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: If you’re like me, you struggle to find the quiet time you need to read during the day. We’re constantly bombarded with alerts, notifications, and phone calls, so it feels almost impossible to steal a few minutes to sit down and absorb something. I’ve struggled with solutions for years, but the problem only seems to get worse.I’ve written quite a bit about my love of e-Ink tablets, especially the BOOX lineup. I love the combination of outstanding battery life and a full Android experience on my BOOX Go 10.3 Gen II. I carry it around with me often, but it’s not always the most convenient option. Fortunately, there’s a smaller alternative. The BOOX Go 6 Gen II is a massive improvement over the original, and paired with a handy Android app, it’s gone a long way toward solving my reading problem.Would you ever carry around a second device just for reading?0 votesInstapaper solves the same problem TiVo did 25 years agoStephen Radochia / Android AuthorityIt seems like such a simple concept, but the Instapaper app on my BOOX Go 6 makes it much easier to read the content I want to read.
paragraph2: I install the Instapaper extension in Chrome on my desktop and use the Instapaper app’s share option on my phone, link everything to my account, and I’m ready to go. I don’t know how many times I found something I was interested in on Google Discover, only to forget about it or not have time in the moment to read it. Instapaper takes care of that. I can save it and have it ready for me later. It was a revelation when I found out I could record live TV shows to watch later with TiVo, and Instapaper offers much the same convenience more than 25 years later.It doesn’t matter how awesome a particular device is at complementing my smartphone if I don’t have it with me.It’s a fantastic feeling to slide into bed at the end of the day and have a full list of interesting articles to read waiting for me on my BOOX Go 6. It gives me a chance to catch up on a few of my hobbies I never have time for during the day. You’ll also be amazed at how much more you retain, as I’ve found my brain has quieted to the point that I can actually digest what I’m reading. Of course, sometimes you just need to read something during the day, and that’s where the BOOX Go 6 excels over other devices.Reading on my phone is more of a hassle than anythingStephen Radochia / Android AuthorityI know it might seem counterintuitive to carry yet another device around for reading when we have our smartphones with us 24/7.
paragraph3: However, it doesn’t take long to realize how inferior our phones are for reading. It’s tolerable for a short article or two, but serious reading on even the best OLED panels can strain your eyes. There are also constant distractions. I can’t get through even a two-minute read without a notification from something or someone. It’s not always something pressing from work or family that causes the split attention. One minute I’m reading about why the Knicks are off to a slow start, and the next, Uber Eats decides it’s the perfect time to remind me to add a Crunchwrap Supreme to my Taco Bell order.Stephen Radochia / Android AuthorityA device like the BOOX Go 6 Gen II makes that easy. Sure, it runs full Android (Android 11, with the Play Store), and you can fill it with the same nagging apps if you want, but it’s a choose-your-own-adventure. I keep mine stripped down so I only have the programs I need. I can get through multiple articles, emails, and longer PDFs without having my attention pulled away.It makes a bigger difference than you’d think, and like a frog in boiling water, I don’t think many of us realize just how distracted we become during the day.
paragraph4: The BOOX tablet’s 6-inch HD ePaper display also offers a much better reading experience. I can sit for a few hours, whether using the backlight or not, and my eyes don’t cry out for a break. Once you get some time reading on an ePaper display, you’ll have a hard time looking at your phone the same way.The best ability is availabilityStephen Radochia / Android AuthorityIt doesn’t matter how awesome a particular device is at complementing my smartphone if I don’t have it with me. Smartphones often win out for reading just because of sheer convenience. They’re already in our pockets, so why not just deal with a less pleasant experience in the name of expediency? I run into that problem with my BOOX Go 10.3. It’s not a huge tablet, but it’s still a commitment to carry it if I’m not carrying my messenger bag.The Go 6 Gen II can technically fit in a pocket, but even when it doesn’t, it’s not the burden or commitment of a larger tablet. I also like the changes BOOX made.
paragraph5: The first-generation Go 6 was portable, and I liked the idea, but it was too slow. Input lag was constant, and I found myself more frustrated than anything. Thankfully, BOOX has fixed that in this generation, helped by a bump to 3GB of RAM (the processor is unchanged). The new model is snappier, and I can navigate between apps quickly. It’s turned a frustrating experience into one that I believe is worth the $200 price of admission, especially with the benefits I’ve been enjoying. It’s not easy to find quiet when we are always connected, but devices like the Go 6 Gen II help me reclaim a little solace, and I can’t put a price on that.ONYX BOOX Go 6 Gen IIONYX BOOX Go 6 Gen IIDistraction-free • Portable • Eye-friendly • - VersatileMSRP: $199.99The pocket-sized Android e-reader that helps you reclaim your reading timeThe BOOX Go 6 Gen II is a compact Android e-reader that makes reading easier on the go. Its eye-friendly ePaper display, distraction-free experience, and access to the Play Store make it ideal for anyone looking to read more and scroll less.

title: Google Play could finally catch up to Apple and Steam with this long-missing store feature
title_bn: Google Play could finally catch up to Apple and Steam with this long-missing store feature
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Why send gift cards, when you can just gift games directly?
paragraph1: Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR The Google Play Store does not yet natively support gifting app purchases to other users. Google now appears to be preparing a system designed to support gifting games to your friends. Buyers will be able to include a note, and re-gift titles recipients don’t ultimately want. Right now, gamers everywhere are up in arms over what’s being seen as an assault on physical media: New games are increasingly only distributed online, and it’s becoming harder and harder to get the latest releases on optical discs or cartridges. Even though Android’s been doing app distribution over the internet since the beginning, it still has a lot of catching up to do when it comes to store features — but at least one big upgrade may be landing soon.
paragraph2: You’re reading an Authority Insights story. Authority Insights brings you all the latest exclusive reports, app teardowns, leaks, and in-depth tech coverage from the Android Authority team that you won’t find anywhere else.While storefronts like Steam support easily gifting games to your friends, so far Google Play has lacked an equivalent option. Sure, you can send a friend a gift card for the game’s value, but that’s not quite the same. But today as we crawl though some of the changes present in version 53.
paragraph3: 9.23-24 of the Play Store for Android, we’ve spotted what looks like work towards finally adopting its own gifting mechanic.You won’t see this interface live right now in the app, but should Google finish up work and choose to enable it, we could get a new “Gift” option for premium, paid apps within the three-dot overflow menu.Once you choose a game you’d like to buy for someone, you’ll be able to fill out a short (200 characters max) note, just like you’re attaching a virtual card. Once nice feature we’re already spotting here is that Google seems prepared for the possibility that the recipient may not want to take you up on your kind gesture, and in that case you’ll still be free to transfer the gift to someone else (who’s hopefully a little more open to it).
paragraph4: As you can see on the right, this workflow appears to support your choice of payment options and allow you to apply discounts, just like you’re buying an app for yourself. And while it’s not quite functional here, you can see those “%s” variables acting as placeholders where your message and delivery instructions will appear. Understandably, the person you’re buying the app for needs to also be a Google user, which we’re sure some lawyers asked the devs to point out here.Honestly, this has been a long time coming for Android, and especially as Google works to make the Play Store a more favorable destination for premium games, features like this are exactly what users and game devs alike are going to be looking for. Apple’s supported gifting for years now, and it’s high time Google catches up.

title: IIT Guwahati researchers use drones and AI to decode traffic patterns on Indian roads
title_bn: IIT Guwahati researchers use drones and AI to decode traffic patterns on Indian roads
author: TechPulse
excerpt: IIT Guwahati researchers use drones and AI to decode traffic patterns on Indian roads
paragraph1: New Delhi, Nov 5 (PTI) Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Guwhati have used high-resolution drone-based traffic data from a highway near Delhi to develop traffic stream models that can help analyse and predict traffic movement under heterogeneous Indian road conditions, according to officials.The research has been published in the prestigious International Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems Research.The study captures not only the relationship between traffic density and vehicle speed but also the variability in speeds observed under similar traffic conditions.According to Akhilesh K Maurya, Professor, Department of Civil Engineering, the study tracked more than 36,000 vehicles and nearly 9 million vehicle positions on a Delhi highway.The research team used this large dataset to study how vehicle speed changes with traffic density. Based on this data, the IIT Guwahati research team developed mathematical and machine learning models for traffic prediction."
paragraph2: Traffic stream modelling uses computer-based and mathematical methods to understand how vehicles move on roads. Such models can be useful for traffic management, road design, traffic signal control, emergency response, traffic simulation, capacity assessment and the development of intelligent transportation systems," he said.However, many existing traffic models are based on road conditions where traffic is relatively orderly and vehicles are more homogeneous. These conditions are different from those on Indian roads, where several types of vehicles, including two-wheelers, three-wheelers and four-wheelers, share the road along with pedestrians.This heterogeneity results in greater variability in vehicle interactions, speeds and spacing, which may not always be adequately represented by conventional traffic models."Traffic conditions in India are different from those in many countries where existing traffic models have been developed.
paragraph3: We need traffic data that represents the diversity and characteristics of Indian roads. Drone-based data collection provides an opportunity to observe a large number of vehicles and their movements over a road section at high spatial and temporal resolution," Maurya added.To overcome the limitations of existing traffic stream models in Indian road conditions, the research team used drones to collect video footage from eight-lane divided highway (wide paved shoulders) on the outskirts of Delhi during daytime traffic. The team used this data to analyze the relationship between traffic density and vehicle speed.Based on the collected data, the research team found that on relatively empty roads, vehicles tend to maintain larger gaps from one another."As traffic becomes moderately heavy, the gaps between vehicles become smaller and vehicles tend to follow one another more closely.
paragraph4: When traffic becomes very heavy, the gaps between vehicles increase again as traffic conditions undergo substantial changes near congested conditions."These observations indicate that the relationship between traffic concentration, vehicle spacing and speed is not necessarily linear and can change significantly as traffic moves from free-flow to congested conditions," Maurya said.In addition to this, the researchers observed that before congestion set in, nearly 3,000 vehicles passed a point in each lane under full traffic flow. During traffic jams, when vehicles were not moving, the density reached nearly 900 vehicles per kilometre of road through entire width.Using these insights, the research team tested six mathematical models and trained two Machine Learning models. Considering the variability and unpredictability of traffic on Indian roads, the researchers developed the models to estimate a range of possible vehicle speeds rather than a single speed value.
paragraph5: This approach allows the inherent variability of heterogeneous traffic to be represented more realistically."Reliable traffic management begins with models that represent how traffic actually behaves on Indian roads. The high-resolution trajectory data generated through drones allows us to capture interactions among different vehicle types and the large variability that conventional traffic models often overlook."Such India-specific models can support more realistic traffic simulation, better road and intersection design, congestion management, capacity assessment and the development of intelligent traffic-management systems suited to Indian conditions," Maurya said.

title: India flags Chinese-linked AI tools in hacking campaign against financial firms
title_bn: India flags Chinese-linked AI tools in hacking campaign against financial firms
author: TechPulse
excerpt: INDIA-CYBER/AI:India flags Chinese-linked AI tools in hacking campaign against financial firms
paragraph1: * India's CERT-In names 'Crafty Falcon' as group behind AI-driven attacks on financial firms* CERT-In identifies four AI hacking tools, at least two linked by researchers to China* The group uses victims' payment systems to move money and has hit some firms twice* Several Indian lenders have flagged cyber breaches in recent weeksBy Munsif Vengattil and Ashwin ManikandanBENGALURU/MUMBAI, Nov 5 (Reuters) - India's cybersecurity agency named the hacking group behind a wave of AI-driven attacks on financial firms and identified its tools, at least two of them linked to China, adding India to a growing list of countries where such tools have been used against banks.The group, which the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) calls "Crafty Falcon," has breached non-bank lenders, fintech firms and cryptocurrency exchanges, according to an advisory issued on Wednesday.CERT-In did not say who was behind the breaches or where the organisation operates.The advisory came after a spate of cyberattacks on Indian banks and non-bank lenders in recent weeks, even as authorities issued warnings and the Reserve Bank of India tightened cybersecurity checks.CERT-In said the attackers use publicly available AI tools to automate break-ins "at machine speed," calling the threat "active and ongoing."
paragraph2: It named four tools: ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI. Security researchers have linked at least two of them to China.China-made ARTEX has been used in attacks on South Korean banks since late September, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike has said.It said a China-linked group also used the tool in an espionage campaign targeting more than 200 organisations in at least 14 countries.CERT-In did not name the affected companies or say how much money was stolen.
paragraph3: The agency did not say the attacks were state-sponsored and the tools it named have been freely available online. ARTEX, however, was made private by its developer last month after it was linked to the South Korean attacks.CERT-In, the ​Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre and India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.PAYMENT INTERFACES TARGETEDCERT-In said Crafty Falcon "surveys its targets with machine intelligence" and moves money by invoking victims' own payment and disbursement systems.Attacks were timed around holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring periods to delay detection.
paragraph4: Firms that had fixed flaws after earlier alerts were attacked again after incomplete remediations were made, it said.Reuters previously reported, citing a police complaint, that last month two Mumbai-based non-bank lenders lost about $2 million in more than 700 unauthorised instant transfers from accounts of India's third-largest lender ICICI Bank on October 8 and 9.The complaint said hackers compromised its ⁠application programming interfaces (APIs), the software links banks use to connect with non-bank lenders and fintech firms to send loan-disbursal instructions.State Bank of India, the country's largest lender, disclosed a dark-web leak of 3,897 customer records last month. Spandana Sphoorty Financial, a non-bank lender, reported unauthorised debits from a bank account on November 1, and AU Small Finance Bank said it was probing a potential customer-data leak.
paragraph5: CERT-In did not say which incidents were linked to Crafty Falcon.

title: Daksham Capital Launches ₹300 Cr Consumer Fund, Marks First Close At ₹125 Cr
title_bn: Daksham Capital Launches ₹300 Cr Consumer Fund, Marks First Close At ₹125 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Multi-family office and wealth management group Daksham Capital has launched its maiden consumer-focused fund, Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV) Fund I,…
paragraph1: SUMMARYDaksham Capital has launched Daksham Growth Ventures Fund I with a target corpus of ₹150 Cr and a ₹150 Cr greenshoe option The fund will back consumer brands and enablers with established product-market fit, targeting businesses that can scale their annual revenue to ₹300-500 Cr Led by Shivam Diwan, the fund has secured around ₹125 Cr in its first close and plans to invest ₹5-20 Cr each in 10-15 companies Multi-family office and wealth management group Daksham Capital has launched its maiden consumer-focused fund, Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV) Fund I, with a target corpus of ₹150 Cr and a ₹150 Cr greenshoe option. The fund has secured around ₹125 Cr in its first close, following its registration as a SEBI Category II AIF last month. Family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs), and entrepreneurs participated in the first close. The fund will continue raising capital towards its target, including the greenshoe option. Led by cofounder and managing partner Shivam Diwan, DGV plans to invest in 10-15 startups, with cheques ranging from ₹5 Cr to ₹20 Cr. It will primarily back Pre-Series A and Series A startups, while considering select later-stage investments. Its investment mandate spans D2C brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C platforms, supply-chain businesses, and startups using AI in consumer services.
paragraph2: Betting On Capital Efficiency DGV will focus on businesses with established product-market fit rather than those still testing demand, Diwan told Inc42. “We will only come where the product-market-fit risk is established,” he said. The fund will typically evaluate startups with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of ₹25-75 Cr, assessing their unit economics, addressable market, founders’ execution capabilities, and differentiation. It is targeting businesses with the potential to scale annual revenue to ₹300-500 Cr. Startups need not be profitable when DGV invests, but the fund expects them to have positive or neutral contribution margins, even if they remain loss-making at the EBITDA level. “Growth by burning an enormous amount of money is not the mantra. It should be a capital-efficient business,” Diwan said.
paragraph3: Beyond capital, DGV plans to help portfolio startups with corporate governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development, and distribution expansion. It also intends to provide board-level guidance and access to its industry network. The fund will evaluate businesses across food and beverages, apparel, snacking, beauty and personal care, accessories, jewellery, and bags. Direct consumer businesses are expected to account for 50-70% of its investments. The remainder will go towards consumer enablers, including contract manufacturers, sourcing and supply chain companies, and B2B2C platforms. DGV is also open to businesses outside the traditional consumer sector, provided their growth is linked to consumer demand. Diwan said the fund is evaluating startups across food and beverages, accessories, and B2B2C segments, including a few D2C brands.
paragraph4: It is yet to make an investment. DGV will also consider a small number of late-stage investments in startups that could go public within two to three years. These deals are likely to comprise largely secondary transactions, Diwan said. Bullish On Consumer AI And Enablers DGV expects AI to play a growing role in consumer businesses over the next decade, particularly in product discovery, personalisation, customer acquisition, and fulfilment. While it does not intend to invest directly in deeptech or standalone AI startups, the fund will evaluate consumer businesses using AI to improve customer engagement and operations. Diwan expects consumer AI to gain momentum over the next 12-24 months, with startups increasingly integrating the technology into how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products. The fund is also bullish on consumer enablers, particularly contract manufacturers and B2B businesses supplying multiple brands.
paragraph5: Diwan said these businesses offer exposure to demand across several brands, reducing dependence on a single consumer-facing startup. Daksham’s launch adds to the pool of dedicated capital targeting Indian consumer businesses. Earlier this year, Kairon Capital announced the ₹90 Cr first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund against a ₹150 Cr target and a ₹50 Cr greenshoe option. Fireside Ventures closed its fourth fund at ₹2,265 Cr ($253 Mn) in December last year. The fund aims to invest in 30-35 early-stage consumer brands, with initial cheques of $1 Mn to $12 Mn, across categories including health and wellness, food and beverages, beauty and personal care, and lifestyle.

title: Rising memory costs may push mobile prices up 30%, could trigger second-hand device market: Jefferies
title_bn: Rising memory costs may push mobile prices up 30%, could trigger second-hand device market: Jefferies
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Rising memory costs, driven by growing demand from the artificial intelligence industry, could push prices of low-end smartphones up by around 30 per cent and force consumers to delay fresh purchases or opt for second-hand devices, according to a rep
paragraph1: Rising memory costs, driven by growing demand from the artificial intelligence industry, could push prices of low-end smartphones up by around 30 per cent and force consumers to delay fresh purchases or opt for second-hand devices, according to a report by Jefferies.PC component prices to rise amid global memory & chip price hikes?New Delhi [India], November 5 (ANI): Rising memory costs, driven by growing demand from the artificial intelligence industry, could push prices of low-end smartphones up by around 30 per cent and force consumers to delay fresh purchases or opt for second-hand devices, according to a report by Jefferies.The report said memory costs have increased sharply as AI-related demand continues to absorb a larger share of global supply. AI is estimated to account for around 60 per cent of memory demand in CY27, while targeted capital expenditure of around USD 1.
paragraph2: 5 trillion by AI players in the same year could keep memory prices elevated for several more quarters.Memory prices are expected to peak by mid-CY27, according to the report. However, the impact of rising component costs is already being felt by smartphone manufacturers, particularly in the affordable segment."Memory cost per unit is likely to have surged ~3x, from est $20 in CY25 to est $60-65 now," the report said.The pressure is particularly high for low-end Android smartphones priced below USD 200, where memory is estimated to account for around 60 per cent of the total bill of materials.
paragraph3: The report said that "a price hike of ~30% in low-end phones could defer new purchases or trigger second-hand affordable purchases", indicating that higher manufacturing costs could affect consumer buying decisions.To manage the increase in input costs, manufacturers may reduce the number of lower-priced smartphone variants and downsize their distribution channels.The impact could also be reflected in global smartphone shipments. The report expects shipments to decline by 15 per cent annually to 1,067 million units in CY26 and 911 million units in CY27. Although the shipment forecasts for CY26 and CY27 were slightly raised by 5 per cent and 3 per cent, respectively, the overall outlook remains weak.
paragraph4: The affordable smartphone segment is expected to face the biggest setback. Its share of the global market could decline from 42 per cent in CY25 to 24 per cent in CY26. In contrast, the share of smartphones priced above USD 600 could increase from 29 per cent to 38 per cent during the same period.The report also pointed to continuing supply-chain pressure, with semiconductor shortages emerging as the biggest bottleneck. Manufacturers are looking at using one- to two-year-old chips instead of the latest flagship processors to control costs.
paragraph5: Even if smartphone demand recovers rapidly from CY28, the industry could find it difficult to restore shipment levels if manufacturers reduce production capacity during the current slowdown, the report cautioned.

title: Lenskart Shares Jump 11% To All-Time High After Q2 Profit More Than Doubles
title_bn: Lenskart Shares Jump 11% To All-Time High After Q2 Profit More Than Doubles
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Shares of omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart surged as much as 11.1% to an all-time high of ₹767.4 on the BSE…
paragraph1: SUMMARYLenskart shares climbed as much as 11.1% to an all-time high of ₹767.4, following the announcement of its Q2 FY27 results yesterday Strong India sales growth and improving profitability reinforced brokerages’ confidence in its expansion, with Jefferies and Equirus raising their price targets Nomura’s ₹888 target is the highest among the brokerages, while Citi retained a ‘Neutral’ rating, citing premium valuations and tougher second-half comparisons Shares of omnichannel eyewear retailer LensKart surged as much as 11.1% to an all-time high of ₹767.4 on the BSE today after the company reported a sharp increase in its September-quarter profit. The stock opened 7.8% higher at ₹745.05 against yesterday’s closing price of ₹691. It subsequently pared some gains to trade at ₹733.55 at 11:15 IST, up 6.
paragraph2: 2%. At that price, Lenskart’s market capitalisation stood at ₹1,27,586.8 Cr (about $13.5 Bn). The rally followed Lenskart’s Q2 FY27 results, announced yesterday. Consolidated net profit increased 124.7% YoY to ₹232.5 Cr, while operating revenue grew 35.7% to ₹2,845 Cr. Revenue growth outpaced the increase in expenses, supporting the improvement in profitability.
paragraph3: Most brokerages remained positive on the company, pointing to strong same-store sales growth in India, store additions, higher realisations, and increasing in-house manufacturing. Brokerages Back Growth Outlook Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating and raised its price target to ₹780 from ₹680, citing continued growth and margin expansion. The brokerage said Lenskart is broadening its customer base through Hustlr Club, targeting the next 100 Mn Indians, while its premium retail format, evolv, and smart glasses offer additional growth opportunities. It added that strong growth supports the company’s premium valuation. Equirus also raised its target to ₹874 for December 2027 from ₹698 for September 2027, retaining its ‘Long’ rating. The brokerage expects Lenskart’s revenue to grow at a compounded annual rate of 24% between FY26 and FY29, supported by growth in both India and international markets. It models around 620 annual store additions over the next few years and expects greater in-house manufacturing to support margins. Nomura retained a ‘Buy’ rating with a target of ₹888, implying potential upside of 21.1% from ₹733.55.
paragraph4: It highlighted operating leverage across India and international operations, with in-house manufacturing and rent leverage supporting domestic margins. Meanwhile, CLSA maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating with a ₹773 target. It said Q2 sales growth was in line with its estimate, while EBITDA exceeded consensus estimates by 3%. The brokerage highlighted robust India volumes and better-than-expected profitability. Manufacturing Supports Margin Outlook HSBC retained its ‘Buy’ rating with a ₹790 target, highlighting India same-store sales growth of around 21% and international constant-currency growth of 23%. The brokerage sees a larger opportunity in international operations than previously anticipated and revised its assessment of India’s margin expansion potential. Macquarie maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating with a ₹750 target. It said faster store additions and an improved product mix helped India EBITDA grow 50% YoY, exceeding its expectations. The brokerage also sees AI-led eye testing increasing testing capacity and easing constraints arising from optometrist availability. It factored in stronger average selling prices, supported by 7% growth in the first half of FY27.
paragraph5: Lenskart added 165 net stores during Q2, including 143 in India and 22 overseas. India same-store sales grew 20.8%, while eyewear volumes increased 26.5% to 86 Lakh units. Citi took a more cautious stance, retaining its ‘Neutral’ rating despite raising its target to ₹700 from ₹650. While store expansion, premium lenses, and higher volumes should support growth, the brokerage expects operating leverage and in-house manufacturing to drive gradual margin improvement. However, it said premium valuations and tougher comparisons in the second half would limit the scope for a valuation rerating.
